description: An EDGE references a B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS whose knot vector contains an interior multiplicity equal to (degree+1)+1 = 5 (for a degree-3 curve). ISO 10303-42 caps interior multiplicity at degree+1 to ensure C^0 continuity; super-multiplicity makes the curve discontinuous at the knot. NX's writer accepts this; Parasolid's importer flags it as a discontinuity and aborts. The Onshape user sees a generic "translation error" with no specific entity callout.
expected_kernel_behavior: validate knot-multiplicity invariants at parse time; either reject with a precise "interior knot multiplicity exceeds degree+1" diagnostic or split the curve at the discontinuity. Translators must surface specific entity / knot index, not a generic "translation error".
notes: Synonyms: "NX super-multiplicity knot", "Onshape translation error generic", "B-spline interior multiplicity > degree+1", "Parasolid rejects discontinuous spline", "knot vector violates ISO cap".
reproducer: B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS degree 3 with 8 control points; knot multiplicities (4, 5, 4) at parameters (0, 0.5, 1) — interior knot multiplicity 5 violates the (degree+1) cap.
sender: Siemens NX (which tolerates super-multiplicity knots in B-spline curves)
sources: bug-reporter language: "Onshape just says 'translation error' with no detail", "NX file imports fine in Catia but Onshape can't read it".
title: NX → Onshape "translation error" via super-multiplicity B-spline knot

description: The top-level PRODUCT_DEFINITION exists but no SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION binds it to a SHAPE_REPRESENTATION. Child PRODUCT_DEFINITIONs each have their own SDR. Some receivers (FreeCAD, Onshape) infer the missing top-level binding from the child graph; Inventor's reader treats it as structurally invalid and aborts the entire import even though the children are fine.
expected_kernel_behavior: when the top-level PRODUCT has no SDR but children do, infer a default top-level SHAPE_REPRESENTATION wrapping the children and emit a warning; do not abort the import. Strict-mode kernels should reject with "top-level PRODUCT_DEFINITION has no SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION".
notes: **See also**: A065. Synonyms: "missing root SDR", "PRODUCT_DEFINITION not bound to SHAPE_REPRESENTATION", "Inventor rejects empty top-level assembly", "AP242 from CATIA structurally invalid", "import aborts on missing SDR".
reproducer: top-level PRODUCT_DEFINITION with no SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION pointing to it; one child PRODUCT_DEFINITION with a proper SDR / SHAPE_REPRESENTATION / AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D / GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT.
sender: CATIA / Creo AP242 writer for empty top-level assemblies
sources: forums.autodesk.com inventor 10994597 "STEP import fails for AP242 from PTC Creo"
bug-reporter language: "Inventor refuses the file as structurally invalid", "the children import fine alone but the assembly fails".
title: CATIA AP242 → Inventor: top-level PRODUCT_DEFINITION without SDR

description: Two distinct defect modes in one fixture: (1) Component A's SHAPE_REPRESENTATION has an empty items list (zero geometry attached) — the footprint is "missing" on receive; (2) Component B's MAPPED_ITEM references the wrong REPRESENTATION_MAP target — TO-220 ends up rendering a TO-252 pin. Both arise from the writer's component-to-3D-model lookup pipeline failing to resolve attachments, with the MAPPED_ITEM still emitted but pointed at whatever happened to be in the lookup cache.
expected_kernel_behavior: receivers should warn on empty SHAPE_REPRESENTATION items lists ("component has no geometry"); validate MAPPED_ITEM target consistency (the target's name should match the source PRODUCT's name or carry an explicit mapping_origin); never silently render the wrong geometry.
notes: **See also**: Xp031 (KiCad name-collision). Synonyms: "KiCad PCB STEP missing components", "MAPPED_ITEM wrong target", "footprint imports as different package", "empty SHAPE_REPRESENTATION items", "STEP component swap on export".
reproducer: PRODUCT 'R0805' bound to SHAPE_REPRESENTATION with empty items; PRODUCT 'TO-220' bound to MAPPED_ITEM whose REPRESENTATION_MAP target is the SHAPE_REPRESENTATION named 'TO-252_pin_should_be_TO-220'.
sender: KiCad PcbNew STEP writer (3D model attachment pipeline)
sources: forum.kicad.info t/30144 "Exporting step file some parts broken"
t/12588 "Why some 3D components are missing from Step file export?"
t/27615 "Exporting step files fails for some components"
bug-reporter language: "some footprints are missing entirely", "TO-220 imports as TO-252", "donut artefacts on the pin".
title: KiCad PCB STEP export: missing components / wrong MAPPED_ITEM target

description: Every record line in the DATA section ends with one or more ASCII space (0x20) characters before the line terminator. Spec-conforming parsers accept this (whitespace is insignificant outside string literals), but downstream tools that diff exports for change-detection see noise on every line, version-control systems show every line as modified on every export, and crude line-based regex parsers that anchor on `;$` mis-match. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file has trailing spaces", "every line ends with whitespace", "diff is huge but nothing changed", "git keeps marking the file dirty".
expected_kernel_behavior: read tolerantly; the spec permits insignificant whitespace anywhere outside string literals. Optionally normalise on re-emit. A downstream tool that warns on this is over-strict; a producer that emits this is sloppy but not malformed.
notes: Practically harmless to parse; the cost is to humans who diff exports.
reproducer: minimal Part-21 file where each `#NNN=ENTITY(..);` line ends with ` ` (three spaces) before `\n`.
sender: Older FreeCAD STEP writer (pre-0.20) and some Pro/E export filters
sources: FreeCAD #4231 "STEP exporter pads lines with spaces"
bug-reporter language: "diff between exports is all whitespace"
title: Trailing whitespace on every record line

description: The HEADER section uses CRLF (`0x0D 0x0A`) line terminators while the DATA section uses bare LF (`0x0A`), or any other inconsistent mix within one file. Spec-conforming parsers ignore line-ending choice (whitespace), but tools that count lines for diagnostics report misleading line numbers, some text editors display the file as binary, and content-hash-based caches see the file as different from a CRLF-normalised copy. Bug-reporter language: "line numbers in error messages are wrong", "file shows up as binary in editor", "STEP from Windows opens weird on Mac".
expected_kernel_behavior: read tolerantly; treat any of `\n`, `\r\n`, or `\r` (classic Mac) as a line terminator. Diagnostics that report a line number should normalise.
notes: **See also**: Wr042. Cousin of Le028 but emitted by writer rather than introduced by transit.- **Byte assertion**: contains(b'\r\n') and contains(b'\n')
reproducer: HEADER section terminated with `\r\n`, DATA section terminated with `\n`.
sender: Windows-hosted writers that build the HEADER block in-memory (CRLF) and append the DATA block from a streamed buffer (LF), or vice versa
sources: OCCT bug forum "STEP file from Windows looks corrupt on Linux"
title: Mixed CRLF and LF line endings within one file

description: The closing `END-ISO-10303-21;` token is emitted without a trailing newline. The spec does not require one (it requires only the closing marker), so the file is well-formed. But concatenation of two such files produces `END-ISO-10303-21;ISO-10303-21;` on a single line, which trips a class of crude scripts that grep for `^ISO-10303-21;`. Bug-reporter language: "can't concat two STEPs", "POSIX text-file rule violated", "no newline at end of file".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: parsers normalize / accept this form (the spec permits it); downstream tooling that concatenates files adds its own separator.
notes: A POSIX-text-file convention (text files end with newline) but not a Part-21 requirement.
reproducer: Part-21 file ending with the bytes `END-ISO-10303-21;` and no `0x0A` after.
sender: Older Siemens NX export and several in-house writers
sources: OCCT forum "concatenating two STEP files produces unparseable result"
title: Final `END-ISO-10303-21;` without trailing newline

description: Continuation lines for long records mix TAB (0x09) and SPACE (0x20) for indentation, or use TAB for some continuations and 2-SPACE for others within the same file. Parsers don't care; humans diffing or reviewing exports do. Bug-reporter language: "tabs and spaces mixed", "indentation inconsistent", "looks bad in editor".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize by ignoring the whitespace.
notes: Cosmetic only, but reviewer-fatiguing.
reproducer: a long argument list where some continuation lines start with a TAB and others start with two SPACEs.
sender: KiCad PCB-to-STEP exporter and a few homegrown writers
title: Tab characters used for line continuation indentation inconsistently

byte_assertions: contains(b'1.0E-7') and contains(b'1e-07') and (contains(b'0.0000001') or contains(b'1.0e-007'))
description: Floating-point values appear in three or more distinct formats within a single DATA section: `1.0E-7`, `1e-07`, `0.0000001`, and `1.0e-007` (extra exponent digit) all coexist. The spec permits any valid REAL formatting, so each value parses correctly, but tools that hash REAL streams to detect change disagree on equality, regex-based extractors fail, and human reviewers find the file unreadable. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file has weird number formatting", "every coordinate looks different", "scientific notation inconsistent".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize / parse all valid REAL formats; coerce / canonicalise on re-emit if the kernel's policy is normalised output.
notes: ISO 10303-21 §6 allows any of these forms; producer is sloppy but conforming.
reproducer: one CARTESIAN_POINT with coordinates `(1.0E-7, 1e-07, 0.0000001)` and a second with `(1.0e-007, 1.0, 1.)`.
sender: Multi-source writer pipelines that compose entities from different subsystems (e.g. older Pro/E, multi-pass NX export)
sources: bug-reporter language: "every number formatted differently" (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Floating-point format inconsistency within one file

description: Coordinates that were entered as exact rationals or simple decimals (1.0, 1.5, 0.25) appear in the emitted file as nearly-but-not-exactly the original (1.4999999999998, 0.25000000000004). The defect is invisible per-value but accumulates across round-trips: a vertex stamped from STEP→kernel→STEP→kernel drifts microns per cycle. Bug-reporter language: "coordinate 1.5 became 1.4999999999998 after re-export", "precision lost on round-trip", "model creeps after every save".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize internal storage to sufficient precision to preserve the input on round-trip within the spec's REAL precision; coerce emit to the smallest representation that recovers the internal value exactly.
notes: Discoverable only by comparing pre- and post-round-trip files; the file as observed is plausible.
reproducer: a CARTESIAN_POINT with coordinates `(1.4999999999998,2.5000000000003,0.99999999999996)` claiming to represent `(1.5, 2.5, 1.0)`.
sender: Writers that store coordinates in single-precision (float32) internally but emit double-precision strings, or use printf("%.15g") on values that were 1.5 represented as 1.4999999999998 due to prior arithmetic
title: Floating-point precision degradation on round-trip

description: Numeric attributes appear with commas as decimal separator (`1,5` instead of `1.5`) because the writer used a locale-aware formatter. ISO 10303-21 mandates the period (`.`) as the decimal separator; comma-decimal output is malformed. Receivers either fail at the lexer (a `,` mid-number ends the argument and the next field is mis-counted) or, with bizarre tolerance, accept the comma and produce wrong geometry. Bug-reporter language: "commas in numbers", "German locale STEP", "STEP file from European user looks corrupt".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as malformed with a diagnostic that names the offending attribute and column; do not silently accept comma-decimals because that makes the failure mode geometric rather than syntactic.
notes: Le023 covers this from the read side; Wr007 documents the producer-side root cause. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts the malformed file (no diagnostic, empty result); kernel mishandling is the documented signal here; the catalog claim above describes the desired future behavior, not what OCC does today.
reproducer: a CARTESIAN_POINT entry with coordinates `(1,5,2,5,3,5)` (intended as `(1.5,2.5,3.5)` but parsed as 6 separate integers).
sender: Writers that use locale-aware `sprintf` / `std::to_string` without forcing the C locale; reported on Windows builds running with German, French, or other comma-decimal locales
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0029xxx-class issue "STEP file from German workstation unreadable"
bug-reporter language: "STEP file has commas where it should have periods" (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Locale-sensitive decimal separator emitted (comma instead of period)

description: Every numeric coordinate is emitted with 17 or more decimal digits, padded with trailing zeros where the underlying value has fewer significant digits (`1.0` is emitted as `1.00000000000000000`). The file inflates 2-3× over what minimal-form output would produce. Spec-conforming, but bandwidth- and storage-hostile. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file unnecessarily huge", "20 digits for every zero", "compresses 95%".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: parse normally; a re-emit policy may normalize / shorten to minimal round-trip-safe form (`%.17g` shortened to the smallest digit-count that round-trips).
notes: Cousin of Wr006 from the opposite direction.
sender: Writers using `printf("%.20f", ..)` or `printf("%.17g", ..)` indiscriminately on every coordinate
sources: prostep ivip "exchange file size grew 3× without geometry change"
bug-reporter language: "STEP file is huge for what it contains"
title: Excessive trailing zeros in numeric output

description: The producer emits `$` (omitted) where the EXPRESS schema declares the attribute as required (non-OPTIONAL). Example: `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D('placement',#10,$,$)` where the schema specifies `axis` and `ref_direction` as effectively required when both are present (one cannot be `$` if the other is non-`$` and the Z-axis convention is to be applied). Some kernels invent a default direction; others reject. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file has dollar signs for required fields", "missing axis direction", "writer omitted required attribute".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as malformed when a required attribute is `$`; do not silently substitute Z+X defaults because the producer's intent is unrecoverable.
notes: AP242 marks `axis` and `ref_direction` as OPTIONAL in the EXPRESS; but most receivers expect both populated when the placement is referenced from a non-trivial geometry context. **OCC behavior**: silently substitutes the Z+X default convention rather than rejecting; this is the kernel mishandling the catalog above forbids.
reproducer: `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D('p',#10,$,$)` paired with a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` that depends on the placement.
sender: Older Pro/E and some lightweight web-CAD STEP exporters
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0026xxx-class "missing direction in AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D from kernel X"
bug-reporter language: "writer skipped required attribute" (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Spurious `$` for required parameter (writer omits required value)

description: The `*` token denotes an attribute inherited from a supertype and overridden in a subtype context; valid only inside complex (subtype-stack) records. The producer emits `*` in a simple-entity instance where no supertype exists, producing `CARTESIAN_POINT('p',(*,0.0,0.0))` or similar. Receivers diverge: some treat `*` as an error, some treat it as zero, some treat it as `$`. Bug-reporter language: "asterisk where number expected", "STEP file has stars in coordinates", "writer used override-marker incorrectly".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as malformed; `*` is meaningful only in complex-instance subtype-override position.
notes: ISO 10303-21 §10 defines `*` semantics narrowly.
reproducer: `CARTESIAN_POINT('p',(*,0.0,0.0))` in a non-subtype context.
sender: Buggy writers that mis-handle the inheritance-override mechanism for complex (subtype) entities and apply it to non-inherited attributes
sources: OCCT forum "writer emitted asterisk in CARTESIAN_POINT coords"
title: Re-emitted `*` (overridden) where schema does not allow it

description: A `CLOSED_SHELL` entity with an empty face-list `()` appears in the file because the producer pruned all faces but left the shell wrapper. Schema requires the face-list to be non-empty. Some readers reject; some accept and produce a vacuous shell that flows through the rest of the import as an empty solid. Bug-reporter language: "empty shell", "STEP closed_shell with no faces", "writer left a stub entity".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject the empty-shell case as schema-violating; do not silently accept the placeholder.
notes: Strongly related to Wr020 (empty SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION chains). **OCC behavior**: silently accepts the empty face-list and produces a vacuous shell with no diagnostic; the kernel mishandling is the documented signal here.
reproducer: `CLOSED_SHELL('hollow',())` referenced by a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`.
sender: Writers that prune the model and forget to suppress now-empty container entities
sources: bug-reporter language: "empty list, expected at least one face" (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Empty parameter list `()` where the schema requires at least one element

description: Instance numbers in the DATA section follow no monotonic pattern: `#1`, then `#1000`, then `#5`, then `#1003`, then `#7`. The spec does not mandate monotonic numbering, so the file is well-formed; but human reviewers, line-based diff tools, and forward-reference-detecting linters all stumble. Bug-reporter language: "STEP instance numbers are random", "file numbering jumps", "can't follow refs visually".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: parse normally; numbering is content-addressable, not order-bearing; a re-emit policy may normalize / renumber sequentially.
notes: Discoverability is the main cost; correctness is unaffected.
reproducer: a Part-21 file in which the order of `#NNN` in the DATA section is `#1, #1000, #5, #1003, #7, #1006`.
sender: Writers that allocate instance numbers from a hashed pool keyed on entity-identity rather than emit-order; observed in some Java-based exporters
sources: OCCT forum "STEP file has random instance numbers"
title: Random `#N` numbering with no monotonic structure

description: The producer emits `#5 = ORIENTED_EDGE(..,#10,..)` before `#10` has been defined. Spec-conforming readers must do a two-pass parse (or a deferred-resolution mechanism), but a class of single-pass kernels reports "reference to undefined instance #10" and rejects. Bug-reporter language: "forward references in STEP", "ref before def", "kernel doesn't support out-of-order STEP".
expected_kernel_behavior: implement two-pass parsing or deferred-resolution; the spec permits forward references. Reject only if a reference remains unresolved after the full file is parsed.
notes: Lh006-class issue but writer-attributable.
reproducer: `#5 = CARTESIAN_POINT('p',(0.,0.,0.));` followed later by `#1 = AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D('a',#5,$,$);` — but `#5` appears first; or, more pathologically, `#1 = .. (#5,..);` first, then `#5 = ..;` second (forward).
sender: Writers that emit entities in topological-construction order without a topological sort; observed in some open-source exporters
sources: OCCT bug "kernel chokes on forward refs"
title: Forward references where sequential numbering was expected

description: A file with 50 entities uses instance numbers like `#42`, `#9876543`, `#21000000`; the maximum number is many orders of magnitude larger than the entity count. Spec-conforming, but a class of receivers naïvely pre-allocates an array of size `max(#N)`, blowing up memory. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file with huge instance numbers", "out of memory loading 50-entity file", "instance #N overflow".
expected_kernel_behavior: use a sparse map (hashtable) for instance lookup; never assume `#N` is a dense array index. Reject only if `#N` exceeds 32-bit signed integer range and the kernel uses int32 indices internally.
notes: Spec does not bound `#N`; ISO 10303-21 Ed.3 §5 defines it as an unbounded positive integer.
reproducer: a 5-entity file where the highest instance number is `#999999999`.
sender: Writers that hash entity identity to a wide integer space and use the hash as the instance number directly
sources: OCCT forum "instance numbers run to 10 million for 50 entities"
bug-reporter language: "huge instance numbers", "memory blows up loading STEP"
title: Sparse instance numbering with huge gaps

description: Two entities in the same DATA section share the same `#N`. Spec violation. Receivers diverge: first-wins, last-wins, both-loaded-and-randomly-resolved, reject. Bug-reporter language: "duplicate #5", "same instance number twice", "STEP file has collision".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as malformed; spec mandates unique instance numbers per DATA section. Document the resolution policy if the kernel chooses tolerant first-wins / last-wins.
notes: Lh010-class.
reproducer: `#10 = CARTESIAN_POINT('a',(0.,0.,0.));` and later `#10 = CARTESIAN_POINT('b',(1.,1.,1.));` in the same DATA section.
sender: Writers with broken counter logic when emitting multi-section or multi-pass files (collision between sections or passes)
sources: bug-reporter language: "duplicate instance number", "two entities with same #N" (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Duplicate `#N` instance numbers in the same DATA section

description: The DATA section contains hundreds of `CARTESIAN_POINT`, `LINE`, `CIRCLE`, and other primitive entities that are not transitively referenced by any `PRODUCT_DEFINITION_SHAPE → SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION → MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` chain. The model is correct but the file is bloated 3-5× by construction-history scratch geometry. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file has unreferenced entities", "orphan geometry in DATA section", "construction history not pruned", "STEP file unnecessarily large".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: parse normally; ignore unreferenced entities; a re-emit pass may normalize / prune; a strict policy emits a warning.
notes: Common in Pro/E exports of complex parts with sketch history.
reproducer: a minimal valid solid plus 30 unreferenced `CARTESIAN_POINT` entities scattered through DATA.
sender: Writers that emit every kernel-internal entity, even those not referenced by the product structure (intermediate construction history, scratch geometry)
sources: OCCT forum "STEP file has unreferenced entities"
bug-reporter language: "orphan geometry", "STEP file 3× larger than it should be"

description: A file that arrived at the writer carrying `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` geometry is re-exported as `TESSELLATED_SHELL_REPRESENTATION` (AP242) or as a mesh-of-PLANE faces approximating the original surfaces. The semantic loss is silent; the file is well-formed, but the analytical surfaces are gone. Bug-reporter language: "STEP went from B-rep to mesh", "lost analytical surfaces on round-trip", "cylinder became 36 facets", "STEP file is now triangulated".
expected_kernel_behavior: Warn and accept: detect tessellation-only content and emit a warning that round-trip from this file forward will be mesh-quality only; do not auto-fit (heal) surfaces back from triangles unless explicitly requested.
notes: Schema-version-agnostic; both AP203 and AP242 permit tessellated representations.
reproducer: a STEP file that contains only `TESSELLATED_SHELL_REPRESENTATION` with triangle list, claiming to represent what was originally a `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE`.
sender: Lightweight viewers and web-based CAD tools that internally tessellate on import and have only a tessellation export path
sources: prostep ivip CAx-IF "B-rep entered, tessellated mesh exported"
bug-reporter language: "STEP lost B-rep, became mesh"
title: Tessellation re-emitted from B-rep input (silent precision loss)

description: The file contains a complete product-structure scaffold (`APPLICATION_CONTEXT`, `PRODUCT`, `PRODUCT_DEFINITION`, `SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION`, `SHAPE_REPRESENTATION`) with all the right cross-references, but the `SHAPE_REPRESENTATION.items` list is empty or contains only placement axes; no `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`, no `SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL`, no `TESSELLATED_SHELL_REPRESENTATION`. The receiver loads "successfully" but reports zero solids. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file loaded but nothing visible", "empty model", "product tree but no geometry", "ghost STEP file".
expected_kernel_behavior: Warn and accept: emit a warning that the file describes a product but contains no geometry; do not reject (well-formed empty product is permitted).
notes: A "successful empty load" is the most confusing failure mode for end users.
reproducer: full scaffold ending with `SHAPE_REPRESENTATION('main',(#13),#24)` where `#13` is just an `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` and there is no shape.
sender: Writers that initialise the product structure tree before geometry is computed and forget to suppress empty trees on export when computation fails or is cancelled
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP loaded but model is empty" (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Empty `SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION` chain (placeholder structure with no geometry)

description: The producer received a file with face- and solid-level colour assignments (`STYLED_ITEM`, `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT`) and emits a file that lacks them entirely, even though the geometry is intact. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file lost colours after round-trip", "colours gone", "all faces grey now".
expected_kernel_behavior: preserve `STYLED_ITEM` / `COLOUR_RGB` chains on round-trip; surface a warning if the kernel's internal model cannot represent them.
notes: Visible in §12.6 / §12.8 colour-bound entries; Wr019 documents the writer-side root cause. Bytes alone are insufficient to demonstrate this defect; needs sibling input fixture. Tagged provenance_tier: requires-sibling-pair.

sender: Writers without a colour-metadata propagation layer that drop `STYLED_ITEM` / `PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT` / `COLOUR_RGB` chains on export
sources: bug-reporter language: "colours gone after STEP round-trip"
title: Re-export drops face and solid colour assignments

description: User-assigned feature labels — e.g. `PRODUCT.name = 'left_bracket'`, face labels via `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT`, descriptive `name` strings on `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` — are replaced with empty strings or auto-generated identifiers (`'BREP_001'`, `''`). The geometry is preserved but the human-readable labelling is lost. Bug-reporter language: "feature names dropped", "names replaced with auto-IDs", "STEP file forgot the part name".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: preserve `name` attributes and `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT` content end-to-end.
notes: Subset of the broader "metadata stripped on re-export" pattern.

title: Re-export drops feature labels and product names

description: The input file contained AP242 PMI entities (`DIMENSIONAL_LOCATION`, `GEOMETRIC_TOLERANCE`, `DRAUGHTING_ANNOTATION_OCCURRENCE`, etc.); the re-emitted file contains none of them, only the underlying geometry. Bug-reporter language: "PMI annotations lost during round-trip", "GD&T disappeared", "STEP file lost dimensions".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept (if AP242), warn and accept (if AP203): preserve PMI on round-trip if the output schema supports it (AP242); emit a loud warning when the output schema is AP203 (no PMI representation possible).
notes: §12.7 covers PMI input defects; Wr021 covers writer-side data loss. Bytes alone are insufficient to demonstrate this defect; needs sibling input fixture. Tagged provenance_tier: requires-sibling-pair.
reproducer: a clean MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP file with the title comment noting the input had GEOMETRIC_TOLERANCE and DIMENSIONAL_LOCATION annotations.
sender: Writers without an AP242 PMI handling layer (AP203-only writers, web-CAD viewers, older Pro/E AP203 export pipeline)
sources: bug-reporter language: "GD&T lost in round-trip", "PMI gone after STEP export"
title: PMI annotations dropped on re-export

description: The input contained AP242 saved-view entities (`CAMERA_MODEL_D3`, `PRESENTATION_VIEW`, `DRAUGHTING_PRE_DEFINED_CURVE_FONT`); the re-emitted file omits them. The geometry is preserved but the curated set of "look from front", "look from above" views the original author defined is gone. title: Saved-view / camera metadata lost on re-export

description: The producer writes `FILE_DESCRIPTION(('CAD-System-X version 12.4.1 build 2026-04-15'),'2;1')`. Some receivers contain heuristic special-casing keyed on vendor strings; they apply a "fix-up X model" filter only if the vendor string matches. This couples the receiver's behaviour to the producer's exact wording, so a minor wording change ("CAD-System X" with a space versus "CAD-System-X" with a hyphen) silently disables the fix-up. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file behaves differently after vendor renamed product", "kernel detects wrong vendor", "vendor sniffing failed".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize / avoid behaviour-altering vendor sniffing; if vendor-specific compatibility is needed, expose it as an explicit user opt-in.
notes: Sender-attribution in `FILE_DESCRIPTION` is a long-standing interop hazard. Bytes alone are insufficient to demonstrate this defect; needs sibling input fixture. Tagged provenance_tier: requires-sibling-pair.
reproducer: a fixture with `FILE_DESCRIPTION(('CAD-System-X v12.4.1'),'2;1')` and a comment noting the receiver special-cases the exact spelling.
sender: Writers that include vendor-version strings in `FILE_DESCRIPTION.description` such that downstream readers branch on them
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP from vendor X behaves weirdly"
title: Vendor-specific FILE_DESCRIPTION strings that downstream readers special-case

sources: OCCT forum "header description has line break"

description: A complex (subtype-stack) record like `(LENGTH_UNIT() NAMED_UNIT(*) SI_UNIT(.MILLI.,.METRE.))` is re-emitted on round-trip as `(SI_UNIT(.MILLI.,.METRE.) NAMED_UNIT(*) LENGTH_UNIT())`; the same complex entity but with the supertype list reordered. Spec-conforming (the order within `(... ..)` is supertype-significant per ISO 10303-21 §11 but only by inheritance hierarchy, not by emission order); receivers that build canonical hash strings see the file as different. Bug-reporter language: "subtype-stack reordered", "complex entity attribute order changed", "STEP round-trip permutes inheritance order".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize / emit complex-record supertype lists in a canonical order (e.g., alphabetic or schema-declaration-order) deterministically.
notes: Subtle: parsers handle either order, but file-equivalence tests fail.
reproducer: `#20=(SI_UNIT(.MILLI.,.METRE.) NAMED_UNIT(*) LENGTH_UNIT());` (canonical ordering would be `LENGTH_UNIT() NAMED_UNIT(*) SI_UNIT(..)`).
sender: Writers that build complex records by iterating an unordered set of supertype names
sources: OCCT forum "complex entity attribute order changed"
bug-reporter language: "round-trip reorders attributes in compound entity"
title: Re-export re-orders attributes within complex (subtype-stack) records

The output is malformed under strict spec interpretation; receivers that strictly enforce the lexeme reject, while heuristic receivers fold the long form. Producer-side root cause for the receiver-side defect Le055. Bug-reporter language: "STEP writer emits .TRUE.", "long-form boolean", "exporter wrote TRUE/FALSE".

notes: Producer-side root cause for Le055. **See also**: Le055, Le056.
reproducer: a complete file where every `EDGE_CURVE` `same_sense` and every `ORIENTED_EDGE` `orientation` attribute uses `.TRUE.` / `.FALSE.` instead of `.T.` / `.F.`.
sender: Writers built on a generic EXPRESS-instance serialiser that maps the EXPRESS `BOOLEAN` keyword to its long-form spelling, or hand-rolled writers that confuse EXPRESS reserved-word case-insensitivity with Part-21 lexeme conformance

description: Records inside a single DATA section terminate with mixed `;\n` and `;\r\n` line endings. The spec is silent on line-ending conformance — whitespace is whitespace — but tools that line-count for diagnostics report inconsistent line numbers, content-hash caches see the file as different on each export, and editors display the file as binary. Cousin of Wr002 (HEADER vs DATA section uses different line ending) but at the per-record granularity. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file mixed newlines per record", "diff of exports is full of line-ending changes".
expected_kernel_behavior: parsers must accept (whitespace tolerance); writers should be deterministic per-file. A normaliser is the simplest fix.
notes: **See also**: Wr002, Le028.
sender: Multi-pass writers where one pass appends records via a buffered text stream (LF) and a separate pass appends records via a Windows-line-ending logger (CRLF), interleaved within the same DATA section
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP file mixed newlines per record", "writer outputs CRLF then LF inconsistently"
title: Inconsistent end-of-record terminator: `;\n` and `;\r\n` mixed in same file

description: A producer's writer emits non-ASCII characters as raw UTF-8 bytes (`\xC3\xA9` for `é`) inside a string literal, while the file's `FILE_DESCRIPTION` declares Edition-2 (`'2;1'`). Edition-2 mandates 8-bit default with non-ASCII expressed via `\X\HH`, `\X2\HHHH\X0\`, or `\PA\.\PI\` page-shift directives; raw multi-byte UTF-8 violates the edition's encoding contract. Edition-3 readers (UTF-8 default) decode the bytes correctly by accident; Edition-2 readers see two single-byte ISO-8859-1 characters instead of one composed `é`. The writer is the producer-side root cause for the receiver-side defect Le003 / Ad058. Bug-reporter language: "STEP writer outputs UTF-8 in Ed.2 file", "non-ASCII in Edition-2 STEP", "exporter does not escape non-ASCII".
expected_kernel_behavior: the writer detects the file's declared edition and emits non-ASCII characters via the edition-appropriate directive; Edition-2 uses `\X\` / `\X2\` / `\PA\.\PI\`; Edition-3 may emit raw UTF-8 with proper `FILE_DESCRIPTION` declaration. Never silently mismatch edition and encoding.
notes: Producer-side root cause for Le003 (now merged into Le021), Le050, Ad058. **See also**: Le050, Le021. Provenance tier: requires-sibling-pair — bytes alone (this fixture's body) demonstrate the defect; the fuller demonstration is the differential between the in-memory string and the bytes the writer emits. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); catalog disallows silent-accept. Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers enforcing the spec must reject (or surface a diagnostic) — silent acceptance defeats the catalog's stated invariant.
reproducer: a `FILE_DESCRIPTION` `'2;1'` (Edition 2); a `PRODUCT.name` containing the raw bytes `\xC3\xA9` representing UTF-8 `é` instead of the spec-required `'\X\E9'` escape.
sender: Writers that rely on the host runtime's default UTF-8 string handling but emit `FILE_DESCRIPTION` with `'2;1'` implementation-level (Edition 2)
sources: ISO 10303-21 Ed.2 §6.4 (8-bit default with explicit escapes for non-ASCII)
bug-reporter language: "STEP writer outputs UTF-8 in Ed.2 file"
title: Writer emits raw UTF-8 bytes in string literal where Ed.2 mandates `\X\` / `\X2\` escape

description: The user selects inches in the STEP-export unit dialog. The writer emits a `LENGTH_UNIT` complex record claiming inches, but every `CARTESIAN_POINT` carries the original millimetre values verbatim with no scale division. A part the user authored as a 25.4 mm cube round-trips as a 25.4 inch (645 mm) cube; visibly 25.4× larger on re-import. The unit declaration and the numeric content disagree.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: writer divides every coordinate by 25.4 when it changes the declared unit; or warn and accept by warning the user that values were not converted. Receivers should heal the mismatch when validation properties (volume, surface area) are present and contradict the declared unit; otherwise they have no way to know. Accepting unit/value disagreement without diagnostic is a coverage gap.
notes: Subset of Wr035 but with concrete inch-vs-mm symptom. **See also**: Wr035, U015. Synonyms: "STEP file marked inch but model is mm-sized", "unit dropdown changes label only", "inch unit but coords are mm", "writer forgot to convert when changing unit".
reproducer: minimal `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` cube; `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT` with `LENGTH_UNIT` complex record `(LENGTH_UNIT() NAMED_UNIT(*) CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT('INCH', ..))`; `CARTESIAN_POINT` corner coordinates `(25.4, 25.4, 25.4)` (millimetre values, not inches).
sender: FreeCAD with OCCT 7.8.x where the user picks "inch" in the STEP-export unit drop-down but the writer skips the value-side conversion.
sources: bug-reporter language: "exports geometry data as mm but tags file as inch — model scales up", "inch unit selected but values are still mm".
title: Inch unit declared in `LENGTH_UNIT` context but coordinates emitted in millimetres (no conversion)

description: A user authors a 10 mm cube. They change the export-unit setting to "m" (or "in"); the writer flips the `LENGTH_UNIT` text in the `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT` but emits the same numeric values. Re-import produces a 10-metre or 10-inch cube. Distinct from Wr044 because the trigger is "user selected a different unit on the way out" rather than "the source kernel was already mm". Bug-reporter language: "labels change but numbers don't".
expected_kernel_behavior: writer multiplies/divides coordinates whenever the declared unit differs from the canonical kernel unit; or refuses the unit change with a clear diagnostic.
notes: Cousin of Wr044 (inch case) and Wr035 (scale-applied-twice). Synonyms: "metre unit but mm values", "unit field decorative", "STEP exporter doesn't convert when user changes units".
reproducer: a 10 mm cube; declare `LENGTH_UNIT` as SI metre (`SI_UNIT($,.METRE.)` — *not* `MILLI`) but emit corner coordinates `(10.0, 10.0, 10.0)`.
sender: FreeCAD STEP exporter when the unit drop-down is changed (mm → m, mm → in) but the writer treats the unit choice as metadata only.
sources: bug-reporter language: "values are unchanged when I change the units", "10mm cube exports as 10 metres tagged AP214", "unit field is just a label, numbers stay the same".
title: Unit name in `LENGTH_UNIT` changed without rescaling coordinate values

description: A Body whose document Placement is non-identity (e.g. rotated 45° about Z, translated 100 mm in X) is written out as if the Placement were identity; the writer flattens the model-space coordinates from local-frame coordinates without composing the Placement transform, so the geometry is emitted in body-local coordinates with no `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` carrying the original orientation. Round-tripping into KiCad / FreeCAD itself yields a part at the origin without rotation. Wrapping the Body in a Compound first is the user-side workaround because the Compound has identity placement.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: writer composes the document Placement into the emitted shape's `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` transform; or pre-multiplies it into the coordinates; or warn and accept with a diagnostic when a non-identity Placement is dropped. Loading geometry whose original Placement has been silently flattened is a coverage gap.
notes: **See also**: Wr025, A024. Synonyms: "Placement ignored on STEP export", "single-body export drops orientation", "compound workaround needed for placement", "exported part lands at wrong position".
reproducer: STEP file with a single `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` whose `SHAPE_REPRESENTATION` `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` is the identity, but the source kernel had a non-identity placement before export.
sender: FreeCAD when exporting a non-zero-Placement Body directly (workaround: wrap in Compound first).
sources: bug-reporter language: "if I export a part to step the export will not use the Placement", "rotational orientation is wrong on import", "compound exports correctly because placement is zero".
title: Body Placement (rotation/translation) not applied during STEP export of a single part

description: A STEP file produced by a recent FreeCAD development build contains two solid `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`s whose authored placements overlap by an exact zero-volume amount (for example, two cylinders sharing a co-incident face that should have been fused in the producing kernel). On re-import the receiver runs a fuse pass that emits `BOPAlog_AlertBadPositioning` warnings for every co-incident pair, surfacing as "STEP Import Broken / Unknown C++ exception thrown" in the GUI. The geometry is technically valid but represents a CSG residual the producer should have collapsed.
expected_kernel_behavior: writer fuses or rejects co-incident-face operand pairs before emission; receiver tolerates positioning alerts as warnings rather than aborting import.
notes: Regression introduced in FreeCAD 1.2.0dev. Synonyms: "BOPAlog_AlertBadPositioning during STEP import", "STEP import broken Unknown C++ exception", "OCC fuse raised warning on STEP import", "scrubEdges fails on imported STEP".
reproducer: STEP file with two `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`s whose `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` co-locates a face of solid A flush with a face of solid B (no gap, no overlap volume) — the receiver's BOP fuse will alert.
sender: FreeCAD 1.2.0dev STEP writer/exporter that leaks pre-Boolean operand positions into the emitted assembly graph, causing the receiver's BOP fuse pass to flag "bad positioning" on every overlap.
sources: bug-reporter language: "Step Import Broken since 1.2.0dev", "DrawProjectSplit::scrubEdges - OCC fuse raised Warning(s): BOPAlog_AlertBadPositioning", "Unknown C++ exception thrown".
title: STEP import regressed by `BOPAlog_AlertBadPositioning` warnings (writer emits CSG-residual positions)

description: Exporting a body that is the direct result of a Boolean operation crashes the writer mid-export inside `TKXDESTEP`. The stack trace centres on the color-attribution pass (it traverses sub-shapes to record `STYLED_ITEM` for each face). When the topmost shape is a freshly-fused Boolean result, the sub-shape iterator dereferences a face whose owner-edge map has not yet been populated. A trivial workaround is to chamfer or fillet one edge after the Boolean; that re-walks the sub-shape graph and populates the maps. The on-disk artefact (when the writer doesn't crash, e.g., on a different OS / OCCT build) is a STEP file with `STYLED_ITEM` references to entity numbers that don't exist in the file's own DATA section.
expected_kernel_behavior: writer must validate sub-shape maps before traversal; receivers must reject dangling entity references with a clear diagnostic rather than crash.
notes: **See also**: P028, A018. Synonyms: "STEP/STEPZ crash exporting boolean", "TKXDESTEP segfault on boolean export", "writer dies on STYLED_ITEM map", "chamfer workaround for boolean export crash".
reproducer: a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` whose face has a `STYLED_ITEM` annotation referencing an entity number that is not declared elsewhere in the DATA section (forward reference to `#999` that has no `#999=..` definition).
sender: FreeCAD STEP/STEPZ writer (OCCT 7.7) when the top-level body is the *direct* output of a Boolean fuse/cut without any subsequent feature (chamfer, fillet) applied.
sources: bug-reporter language: "Crash on exporting a boolean operation", "STEP/STEPZ: Crash on exporting", "doing a chamfer on the boolean lets export complete", stack trace points at `libTKXDESTEP.so.7.7`.
title: Boolean-result body crashes STEP writer in `libTKXDESTEP` color-attribution pass

description: A subtractive-pipe (PartDesign-style sweep used for material removal) along a path with 90° or greater bends with rounded corner transitions emits the corner-fill sphere as part of the additive-result solid in the STEP file, even though the source kernel correctly hides it during display. On re-import the geometry shows a solid sphere occupying the would-be-hollow joint region. The on-disk symptom is a stray closed sub-shell whose centre coincides with the bend pivot point and whose radius equals the pipe radius; a sub-shell that should have been Boolean-subtracted before emission.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: writer Boolean-subtracts construction-residual primitives before emission; receivers may warn and accept on isolated sub-shells with no NAUO/styled-item parent that were obviously construction artefacts. Loading stray construction residuals as visible geometry is a coverage gap.
notes: Synonyms: "subtractive pipe leaves sphere at joint", "right-angle pipe joint has invisible ball", "STEP export shows extra material in pipe corners", "construction residual sphere in joint".
reproducer: STEP file with a `SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL` containing two cylindrical sub-shells joined at a right angle, plus an extra closed `SPHERICAL_SURFACE`-bounded sub-shell at the joint pivot — the sphere is the residual that should have been hidden.
sender: FreeCAD PartDesign subtractive-pipe feature with rounded-corner transition between segments.
sources: bug-reporter language: "subtractive pipe joints get a solid ball in joints that are 90 degrees or more", "solid balls do not show up in FreeCAD but appear after re-importing", "stl shows ball, step shows ball, view does not".
title: Subtractive pipe at right-angle joints emits hidden sphere of material in joint

description: A part the user dimensioned as 20 mm outer / 13 mm inner round-trips as 40 mm / 26 mm — every coordinate doubled. The writer applies both the source-document scale (which was already 1.0) and the export-unit conversion factor — but treats the document scale as if it were a coordinate-space transform on top. The output STEP carries doubled coordinates in a context that still claims millimetres. Distinct from Wr035 (×1000) and Wr044 (inch label only) by the specific 2× factor.
expected_kernel_behavior: writer composes the Placement-and-unit pipeline once; refuses to chain document-scale into unit-conversion; emits a self-test that round-trips a known-volume primitive before writing user data.
notes: **See also**: Wr035, U015, Wr044. Synonyms: "STEP export doubles all coordinates", "20mm becomes 40mm on import", "two-times scale factor on STEP export", "writer applies scale twice".
reproducer: STEP cube authored as 20 mm side; emit `CARTESIAN_POINT` coordinates of `(40.0, 40.0, 40.0)` with `LENGTH_UNIT` declaring SI MILLI METRE.
sender: FreeCAD writer when both a Draft Scale operation and a unit conversion are in the pipeline; the writer composes them in series instead of choosing one path.
sources: bug-reporter language: "outer diameter 20mm exports as 40mm", "model is 2x bigger after export", "stl and step both wrong size".
title: Geometry coordinate values doubled on export (writer applies scale and unit-conversion both)

description: A STEP file imports cleanly via `step-g` (the resulting .g file contains a `Brep_2.s` solid with face count > 0), but the downstream `g-stl` tessellator prints `ERROR(Brep_2.s): tessellation failure` and writes `0 triangles written`; the resulting `.stl` is empty. The two halves of the BRL-CAD pipeline disagree on whether the model is "good": step-g believes it converted the geometry; g-stl cannot triangulate it. The user-facing symptom is an empty `.stl` with no diagnostic at the file-format interface; the failure happens deep in `PullbackCurve` / `SurfaceTree`. The class of inputs that trigger this is narrow but real: any face whose pcurves and 3D curves agree at vertices but drift to ~1e-3 mm in the interior (because the importer treats 1e-3 as the tolerance, but the tessellator treats anything below 1e-3 as a degeneracy). Distinct from M005 (number-of-facets validation property: facet count, not pipeline disagreement).
expected_kernel_behavior: reject; the importer and tessellator must agree on a single tolerance value; if a face cannot be tessellated at the importer's tolerance, the importer must reject it at parse time rather than commit a `Brep_2.s` to the .g file. Pipeline diagnostic must surface both the offending face id and the tolerance comparison.
notes: **See also**: M005, M022, N019, N050. Synonyms: "BRL-CAD step-g imports but g-stl emits empty", "0 triangles written silently", "tessellation failure on sliver face", "importer/tessellator tolerance disagreement", "STEP→.g→.stl produces empty STL no diagnostic".
reproducer: STEP `BEZIER_SURFACE` with a 4×4 control net whose v-extent is 3 micrometres (well below step-g's 1e-3 mm tolerance). step-g loads the face; g-stl emits zero triangles.
sender: STEP files whose features sit at or below the BRL-CAD step-g hard-coded 1e-3 mm tolerance (sliver faces, micro-fillets, sub-tolerance B-spline patches) — the importer treats the geometry as valid but the tessellator's adaptive sampler cannot find sample points satisfying the same hard-coded tolerance.
sources: BRL-CAD users mailing list 2017 (Filip Binkiewicz reproducer): "ERROR(Brep_2.s): tessellation failure" + "0 triangles written"
bug-reporter language: "step-g converts cleanly but g-stl outputs empty file", "BRep imports OK but cannot triangulate", "STEP→.g→.stl pipeline silently produces empty STL".
title: step-g imports cleanly but downstream `g-stl` tessellator silently writes zero triangles

description: A STEP writer emits an EDGE_CURVE whose `edge_geometry` slot is filled by an unbounded LINE entity rather than a TRIMMED_CURVE(LINE, t0, t1) or a SURFACE_CURVE with explicit param bookkeeping. The vertices nominally define the edge's domain, but the LINE itself carries no parametric extent, so receivers that traverse the LINE directly (rather than the EDGE_CURVE bookkeeping) walk into an unbounded range.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal — re-bound the LINE via implicit vertex-parameter projection, or wrap it in a TRIMMED_CURVE post-load.
notes: Synonyms: "EDGE_CURVE points to unbounded LINE", "STEP writer emits untrimmed curve", "missing TRIMMED_CURVE wrapper around LINE", "line-edge without parametric trim". See also Twi248 (null-3D-curve sibling case).
reproducer: a single EDGE_CURVE with edge_geometry = #(LINE). No TRIMMED_CURVE, no SURFACE_CURVE wrapper. Two distinct VERTEX_POINTs delimit the topological edge but the geometric curve is intrinsically unbounded.
sources: Pattern-mined from OCCT/tests/bugs/step/bug32817_1 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). OCCT method `STEPControl_Writer::Transfer` on a single-line edge.
title: Writer emits EDGE_CURVE backed by untrimmed LINE entity

description: A fused solid built from a TOROIDAL_SURFACE (major radius 5, minor radius 3) and a CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE (radius 2, height 10, offset center) loses geometric fidelity through STEP write+read. The torus parameters round-trip cleanly, but the post-fuse face_outer_bound topology gets corrupted: edge count and vertex count drift from the in-memory original. Receivers see a shape with the wrong number of sub-shapes after the round-trip.
expected_kernel_behavior: preserve sub-shape counts and torus/cylinder parameters through round-trip; if the fuse-result is corrupted, healer must repair the face_outer_bound topology.
notes: Synonyms: "torus fused solid corrupted on STEP round-trip", "TOROIDAL_SURFACE write corruption", "fused toroidal+cylindrical loses edge count", "torus + cylinder write+read produces wrong shape counts". See also Wr052 (writer untrimmed-curve sibling).

The geometric path is the same (the underlying EDGE_CURVE endpoints don't change), but the loop's directed-traversal sense is broken: receivers that follow the orientation flags end up with face normals pointing every which way. Distinct from Tsh012 (.U. seam flag) and Wr054 (single-face inversion) — this is a *systematic* half-population reversal.
expected_kernel_behavior: validate edge-loop orientation consistency before emit; check loop traversal forms a closed cycle in either direction.
