description: ISO 10303-21 §6.2 specifies that a record is terminated by `;`; the spec is silent on whether a trailing newline is required after the final `;` of the file. A producer may emit `..);ENDSEC;END-ISO-10303-21;` with no newline anywhere, or with the final newline omitted. POSIX tools that read line-by-line (and strict line-buffered tokenisers) drop the last line if it lacks a `\n` — the final record (or the `END-ISO-10303-21;` terminator) is silently lost, and the receiver reports a file that is structurally short by one record. The cousin defect is a missing newline between the last DATA-section record and `ENDSEC;` — `..);ENDSEC;` with no separator at all is allowed by the grammar but trips lexers that scan to end-of-line for an `ENDSEC` keyword. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file missing trailing newline", "last record dropped on load", "ENDSEC on same line as last record".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: tokenise on `;` alone; treat EOF as a valid record-and-section terminator if the preceding `;`-terminated record has been seen. Never require a trailing newline. Lexers that scan line-by-line should be replaced or wrapped with a `;`-aware preprocessor. Do not reject missing-trailing-newline files.
notes: Companion to Le056 / Le057 (other EOR variants). **See also**: Le054, Le056, Le057. Synonyms: "no newline at EOF in STEP", "ENDSEC without preceding newline", "POSIX-incomplete final line in Part-21".
reproducer: a file whose byte stream ends `..#19=EDGE_LOOP('',(#18));ENDSEC;END-ISO-10303-21;` with NO trailing `\n` and NO newline between the last record and `ENDSEC;`. The fixture is byte-exact at EOF.
sender: deduced — producers that write the file body byte-for-byte without an explicit final newline; some streaming writers that flush before the trailing `\n` is queued
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP file missing newline before ENDSEC", "no trailing newline at EOF"
title: Final record before `ENDSEC;` lacks trailing newline at EOF

category: §12.1a encoding/strings (sub-class: Ed.2 vs Ed.3 default-encoding mismatch on PRODUCT.name)
description: A producer emits Ed.2-style STEP where `'ä'` appears as raw byte `0xE4` inside the string literal; schema-legal under the Ed.2 default of ISO-8859-1. The current reader assumes Ed.3 UTF-8, sees an isolated continuation byte, and either replaces with `?`, drops the character, or (in older builds) overruns into the next byte and corrupts the string. The producer's intent is preserved on disk; the receiver mangles it on import.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; inspect `FILE_DESCRIPTION`'s `implementation_level` and conformance class to determine edition; on Ed.2, decode high-bit bytes as ISO-8859-1; on Ed.3, decode as UTF-8 and reject isolated continuation bytes with `E_BAD_UTF8`.
notes: **See also**: Le002, Le021. Synonyms: "bug in OCC with german letter", "umlaut in PRODUCT.name garbled", "ISO-8859-1 ä misread as UTF-8 by STEP reader", "high-bit byte mis-decoded in part name".
reproducer: `#100=PRODUCT('Schr\xe4gverzahnt','','',(#101));` — the bytes `0xE4` should decode to `ä` per Ed.2 default; UTF-8-only readers misinterpret.
sender: German-locale CAD authoring tools (Catia / NX / Solid Edge German installs) that emit Ed.2 STEP with raw ISO-8859-1 bytes for `PRODUCT.name` like `'Schrägverzahnt'`.
sources: bug-reporter language: "bug in OCC with german letter", "umlaut in part name appears as garbled bytes", "ä emitted as raw 0xE4 misread as UTF-8". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: German umlauts in `PRODUCT.name` mis-decoded by reader (Latin-1/UTF-8 confusion)

description: Truncated downloads omit the closing `END-ISO-10303-21;`; concatenated dumps emit it twice; some generators substitute `END_ISO_10303_21;` (underscores), `END-ISO-10303;` (drops part number), or append trailing garbage after the marker.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject missing/duplicated end marker; tolerant mode may accept the underscore variant with a warning. Trailing bytes after the marker must be ignored, never appended to the previous entity.
notes: **See also**: Ad038. Synonyms: "missing END-ISO-10303-21 marker", "truncated STEP file no end marker", "STEP closes with END_ISO_10303_21 underscores", "duplicate END marker in STEP", "trailing garbage after end marker".
reproducer: file ending with `ENDSEC;` and no `END-ISO-10303-21;`; or two `END-ISO-10303-21;` lines; or `END_ISO_10303_21;` substitution.
title: Missing or malformed closing marker `END-ISO-10303-21;`

description: A `HEADER`/`DATA`/`ANCHOR`/`REFERENCE`/`SIGNATURE` section runs into the next section keyword without an intervening `ENDSEC;` (or an `ENDSEC` token without trailing semicolon). Confuses parsers expecting strict bracketing.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject with line-numbered diagnostic naming the offending section.
notes: Synonyms: "missing ENDSEC between sections", "STEP HEADER runs into DATA", "ENDSEC token without semicolon", "section keyword without ENDSEC", "STEP section terminator missing".
reproducer: `HEADER;..FILE_SCHEMA(('IFC4'));DATA;#1=A();END-ISO-10303-21;` (no `ENDSEC;` before `DATA;`); or `HEADER;..ENDSEC<newline>DATA;` (semicolon missing).
title: Missing `ENDSEC;` between sections

description: ISO 10303-21 requires exactly one each of FILE_DESCRIPTION, FILE_NAME, FILE_SCHEMA, in that order. Real files appear with FILE_SCHEMA omitted, FILE_NAME twice, FILE_DESCRIPTION/FILE_NAME swapped, or DATA before HEADER.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject with "missing required header entity X" or "header section out of order"; never null-deref the schema pointer.
notes: **See also**: Lh005. Synonyms: "FILE_SCHEMA missing from HEADER", "FILE_NAME twice in HEADER", "DATA before HEADER in STEP", "header records out of order", "duplicated header entity".
reproducer: `HEADER; FILE_NAME('a.stp','..',(''),(''),'','',''); FILE_DESCRIPTION((''),'2;1'); ENDSEC;` (no FILE_SCHEMA); or `ISO-10303-21; DATA; #1=A(); ENDSEC; END-ISO-10303-21;` (no HEADER at all).
sender: hand-edited or partially-generated files; minimalist exporters (W033 echo)
title: HEADER section missing one of the three required entities (FILE_DESCRIPTION / FILE_NAME / FILE_SCHEMA), wrong order, or duplicated

description: FILE_NAME requires 7 attributes; FILE_DESCRIPTION 2; FILE_SCHEMA 1 (a list). Real-world failures: extra attribute appended to FILE_NAME, empty parameter lists where attributes are required, FILE_SCHEMA written with a single string in place of a list of strings.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject with a precise "attribute count mismatch" diagnostic naming the field.
notes: **See also**: Lh004. Synonyms: "FILE_NAME wrong number of attributes", "FILE_SCHEMA arity mismatch", "FILE_DESCRIPTION extra attribute", "header record with too few parameters", "FILE_SCHEMA single string instead of list".
reproducer: `FILE_NAME('a','b',('c'),('d'),'e','f','g','h');` (8 args; expected 7); or `FILE_DESCRIPTION();` (0 args).
title: FILE_DESCRIPTION/FILE_NAME/FILE_SCHEMA arity mismatch (extra or missing attributes)

description: FILE_SCHEMA's argument is a LIST OF STRING and must be written `FILE_SCHEMA(('AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN'));`; generators that emit `FILE_SCHEMA('AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN');` are non-conformant.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject; lenient mode may auto-promote to a list with a warning.
notes: **See also**: Lh007, Lh008, Lh009. Synonyms: "FILE_SCHEMA without double parentheses", "schema written as single string not list", "FILE_SCHEMA('AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN') instead of list", "FILE_SCHEMA list missing outer parens", "schema name not in list-of-string".
reproducer: `FILE_SCHEMA('AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN');`
title: `FILE_SCHEMA` written without the required double parentheses (list of strings)

description: `FILE_SCHEMA` carries `('AP203_CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN','AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN')`. Most receivers consume only the first; some pick the most-capable; behavior is implementation-defined and divergent.
expected_kernel_behavior: warn; pick the most-capable supported schema deterministically; do not crash. Document which one was chosen.
notes: Validation observed: silent-empty (no shape produced) rather than the cited divergent-pick behavior. Specific divergent-pick code path may not be exercised at fixture scale; the kernel-mishandling-by-silent-acceptance still demonstrates the defect class (implementation-defined behavior on multi-schema lists). **See also**: Lh006. Synonyms: "multiple schemas in FILE_SCHEMA", "FILE_SCHEMA lists AP203 and AP214 together", "two schema names in one FILE_SCHEMA", "STEP picks wrong schema from multi-list", "compound FILE_SCHEMA confuses receiver".
occ_behavior_note: silent-empty (no shape produced) rather than the cited divergent-pick behavior. Specific divergent-pick code path may not be exercised at fixture scale; the kernel-mishandling-by-silent-acceptance still demonstrates the defect class (implementation-defined behavior on multi-schema lists).
reproducer: `FILE_SCHEMA(('AP203_CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN','AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN'));` or with embedded comments inside the parentheses.
sender: producers targeting multiple AP versions (e.g. AP203 + AP214)
title: Multiple schema names listed inside a single FILE_SCHEMA

description: Two separate `FILE_SCHEMA` lines in HEADER. Last-write-wins vs. first-write-wins behavior diverges across implementations, leading to silent schema mis-binding.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject; exactly one FILE_SCHEMA permitted.
notes: **See also**: Lh006. Synonyms: "duplicate FILE_SCHEMA records", "two FILE_SCHEMA lines in HEADER", "conflicting schema names in header", "second FILE_SCHEMA overrides first", "schema declared twice with different names".
reproducer: `HEADER; FILE_DESCRIPTION((''),'2;1'); FILE_NAME(..); FILE_SCHEMA(('AP203_CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN')); FILE_SCHEMA(('AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN')); ENDSEC;`
title: Duplicate `FILE_SCHEMA` records with conflicting schema names

description: FILE_SCHEMA value is `''`, mixed-case (`'AutomotiveDesign'`), uses a non-canonical long form (e.g. `_MIM` instead of `_MIM_LF`), names an internal vendor schema, or comma-separates multiple schemas inside one string instead of using a LIST.
expected_kernel_behavior: case-fold to upper for compare; reject the comma-in-string variant; warn-and-fall-back-to-best-fit on unrecognized names.
notes: **See also**: Lh006. Synonyms: "empty FILE_SCHEMA value", "mixed-case schema name", "vendor schema in FILE_SCHEMA", "comma-separated schemas inside one string", "unrecognised schema name".
reproducer: `FILE_SCHEMA(('AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN_MIM'));` (instead of `_MIM_LF`); `FILE_SCHEMA(('AutomotiveDesign'));`; `FILE_SCHEMA(('AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN, IFC2X3'));` (one string, two names).
title: Blank, mis-cased, or unrecognized schema name

description: FILE_DESCRIPTION's `implementation_level` must be one of the canonical conformance codes `'1;1'`, `'2;1'`, `'3;1'`, `'4;1'`, `'4;2'`, `'4;3'`. Real files contain `'1.0'`, `'2;1;1'`, `'2.1'`, the empty string, or vendor branding strings (`'Simulia 2018'`). Overlong values can additionally trigger fixed-buffer overflows in legacy translators.
expected_kernel_behavior: warn-and-tolerate when the value is recognizable; reject overlong values; default to class 1 with a warning if unparseable. Validate length before copy into any fixed-size buffer.
notes: **See also**: Le020. Synonyms: "non-canonical implementation_level in FILE_DESCRIPTION", "STEP conformance code wrong format", "vendor branding in implementation_level", "1.0 instead of 1;1 in header", "implementation_level overflow".
reproducer: `FILE_DESCRIPTION((''),'1.0');`, `FILE_DESCRIPTION((''),'Simulia 2018');`, or `FILE_DESCRIPTION(('x'),'AAAA…(2 KiB)…');` to exercise the overflow case.
title: `FileImplementationLevel` non-canonical value

description: FILE_NAME's timestamp attribute must be ISO-8601 (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[±hh:mm]`). Producers emit RFC 822 dates, locale-formatted (`27/12/2003 11:57`, `08/13/2014`), epoch integers, or empty strings.
expected_kernel_behavior: Warn and accept: lexically valid as STRING; semantic layer warns; do not reject (block import) on non-conformant timestamp.
notes: **See also**: Lh012, Lh013. Synonyms: "FILE_NAME timestamp not ISO-8601", "RFC 822 date in STEP header", "STEP timestamp 27/12/2003 format", "epoch integer in FILE_NAME timestamp", "locale-formatted date in header".
title: `FileTimeStamp` not in ISO-8601 form

description: Per spec the timestamp attribute is a STRING. Some generators write it without surrounding apostrophes: `FILE_NAME('out.stp',2013-10-24T12:12:06,..);`. The bare token tokenizes as identifiers/numbers and fails grammar.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject with "expected STRING at attribute 2" pointing at the unquoted token; offer strict/lenient toggle that re-quotes ISO-8601-shaped tokens with a warning.
notes: **See also**: Lh011. Synonyms: "unquoted timestamp in FILE_NAME", "STEP date without apostrophes", "bare timestamp parses as identifier", "FILE_NAME date not a STRING", "timestamp tokenizes as numbers".
sender: older stepcode versions (#267)
title: Unquoted timestamp in FILE_NAME (timestamp not a STRING)

description: Producer pulls the FILE_NAME timestamp from the system clock rather than honoring a user-supplied datetime. Breaks reproducible builds (e.g. AUR packagers, CI artefact comparisons, downstream LibrePCB content hashes).
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: writer must honor an explicit timestamp parameter when given; default to current time only when absent.
notes: Producer-side defect, but the resulting headers are a recognizable wild-corpus class. **See also**: Lh011. Provenance tier: runtime-only; bytes alone cannot demonstrate non-determinism; the defect is that the timestamp was generated from the system clock rather than a user-supplied parameter. Demonstrating this requires comparing two writer invocations (or a writer-with-explicit-timestamp behavioral test), not a static file. Synonyms: "non-deterministic STEP build timestamp", "system-clock timestamp pollutes FILE_NAME", "reproducible build broken by STEP timestamp", "different timestamps each export", "CI artefact differs only by STEP date".
reproducer: `export_step(b, "box.step", timestamp=t)` and confirm FILE_NAME's timestamp matches `t`.
sender: build123d export_step (also CadQuery #1396)
title: Non-deterministic / build-time timestamp pollution

description: ISO 10303-21 reserves header keywords without `!` for the standard. Vendor-specific HEADER entities must begin with `!` to avoid collision with future spec entities. Files appear with bare `VENDOR_INFO(..)` or similar.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject the bare keyword; lenient mode may treat unknown header keywords as ignorable with a warning.
notes: **See also**: Lh017. Synonyms: "vendor HEADER entity without bang prefix", "user-defined header missing exclamation mark", "VENDOR_INFO bare without !", "non-spec header entity collides with future spec", "custom HEADER record name not prefixed".
reproducer: `HEADER; FILE_DESCRIPTION((''),'2;1'); FILE_NAME(..); FILE_SCHEMA(('AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN')); VENDOR_INFO('SolidWorks 2024'); ENDSEC;`
title: User-defined HEADER entity not prefixed with `!`

description: Edition 3 allows additional header entities beyond the required three (`FILE_POPULATION`, `SECTION_LANGUAGE`, implementation-private entries). Strict Edition-1/2 readers reject any header entity beyond the canonical three; tolerant Edition-3 readers must accept them.
expected_kernel_behavior: accept any number of extra header entities under Edition 3; warn for unknown names; reject under strict Edition-2.
notes: Synonyms: "FILE_POPULATION header record", "Edition 3 extra header entities", "SECTION_LANGUAGE in HEADER", "Ed.2 reader rejects FILE_INFO", "Edition 3 header beyond required three".
reproducer: append `FILE_INFO('Report Date','2025-04-21 18:16:37', ..);` between FILE_SCHEMA and ENDSEC.
title: Edition-3 extra header entities (`FILE_INFO`, `FILE_POPULATION`, `SECTION_LANGUAGE`, …)

cross_oracle_note: pure-Python Part-21 validator rejects (reject(E_UNRESOLVED_REFS)); OCCT silently accepts (load is `empty`). OCC auto-heals a spec-level violation. Synonyms: "bang-prefixed entity in DATA section", "user-defined entity rejected by regex", "!FOO entity in DATA", "schema reader rejects ! prefix", "STEP entity name with exclamation mark".
description: ISO 10303-21 §11 reserves names beginning with `!` for user-defined entities. Schema-driven readers whose keyword regex is `[A-Z][0-9A-Z_]*` reject them outright instead of treating them as opaque user types.
expected_kernel_behavior: lex `!`-prefixed identifiers as keywords; reject by schema validation OR pass through as a generic-entity placeholder.
notes: Cross-oracle: pure-Python Part-21 validator rejects (reject(E_UNRESOLVED_REFS)); OCCT silently accepts (load is `empty`). OCC auto-heals a spec-level violation. Synonyms: "bang-prefixed entity in DATA section", "user-defined entity rejected by regex", "!FOO entity in DATA", "schema reader rejects ! prefix", "STEP entity name with exclamation mark".
title: User-defined entity name with `!` prefix in DATA section

description: ISO 10303-21 keywords are upper-case. Hand-edited files routinely contain lower-case or mixed-case (`Cartesian_Point`) entity names. Implementations that combine case-insensitive lookup of internal keywords with case-sensitive comparison of attribute-binding names produce two divergent parses for the same file.
expected_kernel_behavior: per ISO, entity names canonicalize to upper-case before binding; pick one rule (case-insensitive throughout) and apply uniformly. Lenient mode may auto-uppercase with a warning.
notes: **See also**: Lh030. Synonyms: "lowercase keyword in STEP file", "ifcperson instead of IFCPERSON", "cartesian_point in lowercase", "mixed-case entity name", "STEP entity not all caps".
title: Lower-case keyword (`ifcperson`, `cartesian_point`, `ENTITY` etc.)

description: HEADER claims one schema (e.g. `IFC4`, `AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN`/AP214, `AP242_…` Ed.2) but DATA uses entity names that exist only in another schema or another edition (e.g. `IFC2X3_PROJECT` in an IFC4 file; `ROUND_HOLE` in an AP214 file; post-Ed.3 hole-feature entities under an Ed.2 header).
expected_kernel_behavior: reject with a diagnostic naming the offending entity-name vs. claimed schema; offer a schema-name override flag. Parse based on entity-name availability, not header schema name; warn on mismatch.
notes: **See also**: Le027, Lh031. Synonyms: "FILE_SCHEMA disagrees with DATA entities", "AP214 entity in IFC4 file", "schema name mismatches entity types", "entity not in declared schema", "STEP DATA uses entities from another schema".
reproducer: `FILE_SCHEMA(('IFC4'));` with body `#1=IFC2X3_PROJECT(..);` — or hand-edit FILE_SCHEMA of an Ed.3 file to claim Ed.2.
title: FILE_SCHEMA names a schema that disagrees with entity types in DATA

description: Within one DATA section each `#N` may appear on the LHS at most once. Concatenating two STEP files with overlapping IDs, or merging sub-files without renumbering, produces duplicates. Silent overwrite causes semantic divergence; in C++ implementations, freeing the first instance while references still point at it transitions to use-after-free.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject with `E_DUPLICATE_INSTANCE_ID` before constructing the second instance; never silently overwrite or free-then-reuse.
notes: **See also**: Ad038, Lh024. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts duplicate instance IDs (typically last-write-wins) without diagnostic; kernel mishandling; the catalog above forbids silent overwrite. Synonyms: "duplicate instance ID in DATA", "#42 defined twice in STEP", "concatenated STEP files have ID collision", "two definitions of same #N", "instance ID overwrites previous".
reproducer: `DATA; #10=PRODUCT('a','a','',(#11)); #10=PRODUCT('b','b','',(#12)); ENDSEC;` or `#19=IFCPROJECT(..); #19=IFCSITE(..);`
title: Duplicate instance ID (`#N=..` defined twice within one DATA section)

description: stepcode tolerates `# 12 = ENT(..)` and even `# /*c*/ 12 = ENT(..)`; the IfcOpenShell Lark grammar rejects whitespace between `#` and digits. ISO 10303-21 §5.6 declares `#NNN` a single token, so spaces inside it are non-conformant. Treating tab as a separator inside an identifier produces silent corruption (`#1<TAB>2` becomes `#12`).
expected_kernel_behavior: strictly reject whitespace/comment inside `#NNN`; tolerant readers may accept whitespace between tokens but never inside identifiers, and must warn rather than silently merge digits.
notes: **See also**: Ls038. Synonyms: "whitespace between # and digits of instance ID", "tab between hash and number in #ID", "comment inside instance reference", "# 12 with space in STEP", "stepcode tolerates space inside ID".
reproducer: `# 12 = IFCPERSON(..);` or `# /* note */ 12 = IFCPERSON(..);` or `#1\t2 = …`.
title: Whitespace, tab, or comment between `#` and digits of an instance ID

description: Edition 3 allows multiple `DATA;…ENDSEC;` sections, each with its own `#NNN` namespace; cross-section references use `@section_name#N` syntax. Tools targeting Edition 1 either fail at the second `DATA;` or silently flatten namespaces, causing collisions when `#10` appears in both sections.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept N≥1 DATA sections; scope `#N` IDs per-section; resolve cross-section references via the proper Ed.3 syntax; never flatten namespaces across sections. Must not silently flatten.
notes: **See also**: Ad080, Lh022. Synonyms: "#NNN reused across DATA sections", "Ed.3 multi-section ID collision", "two DATA sections share #10", "namespace flattened across sections", "STEP multi-section reference broken".
reproducer: `HEADER;..ENDSEC;DATA;#10=PRODUCT(..);ENDSEC;DATA('extra',('AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN'));#10=APPLICATION_CONTEXT('..');ENDSEC;END-ISO-10303-21;`
title: Reuse of `#NNN` across different DATA sections (Ed.3 multi-section)

description: Edition 3 introduces `@NNN` value-instance identifiers (e.g. `@1=POSITIVE_LENGTH_MEASURE(..)`) alongside `#NNN` entity-instance identifiers. The two integer namespaces are disjoint: `#1` and `@1` are distinct instances. Files that put a `@NNN` value-instance reference where a `#NNN` entity-instance reference is required (or vice versa), or that use the `@`-prefix syntax in plain Edition-2 contexts, break readers that collapse the two namespaces into one map and silently merge unrelated objects.
expected_kernel_behavior: maintain two separate dispatch tables; reject if an attribute slot expects `#NNN` but the value reference is `@NNN` (or vice versa).
notes: Synonyms: "mixing #NNN and @NNN in same STEP", "value-instance reference where entity expected", "@1 used as #1", "Ed.3 disjoint namespaces confused", "@NNN at #NNN slot".
reproducer: `#1=PRODUCT(..); @1=POSITIVE_LENGTH_MEASURE(2.5); #2=ITEM_DEFINED_TRANSFORMATION('',$,@1);`
title: Mixing `#NNN` (entity) and `@NNN` (value) namespaces (Ed.3)

cross_oracle_note: pure-Python Part-21 validator accepts (`accept`); OCCT rejects (`reject`). OCC enforces stricter framing than the spec text requires. Synonyms: "ANCHOR section in Edition 2 reader", "REFERENCE section unknown", "SIGNATURE section ignored", "Edition 3 sections fail in old reader", "STEP Ed.3 sections rejected".
description: Edition 3 introduces three optional sections: ANCHOR (named external entry points), REFERENCE (named external links via URI), SIGNATURE (digital signature). `implementation_level` becomes `'4;1'`. Older Edition-2 readers either fail to parse the sections, or strip and re-parse, or warn-and-skip; behavior is implementation-defined.
expected_kernel_behavior: under Ed.3, accept and pass through; warn on SIGNATURE that cannot be validated; under strict Ed.2, reject with a clear edition-mismatch diagnostic.
notes: Cross-oracle: pure-Python Part-21 validator accepts (`accept`); OCCT rejects (`reject`). OCC enforces stricter framing than the spec text requires. Synonyms: "ANCHOR section in Edition 2 reader", "REFERENCE section unknown", "SIGNATURE section ignored", "Edition 3 sections fail in old reader", "STEP Ed.3 sections rejected".
reproducer: `HEADER;..ENDSEC;ANCHOR;<a>=#1;ENDSEC;DATA;..` or add a SIGNATURE section after DATA.
title: Edition-3 ANCHOR / REFERENCE / SIGNATURE sections present in Edition-2 readers

description: ANCHOR entries reference `#NNN` form; entries using non-numeric tokens after `#` (e.g. `<#42@x>='product';`) violate the grammar.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject the entry with a precise diagnostic; do not abort the whole file.
notes: **See also**: Lh026, Lh028. Synonyms: "non-numeric # in ANCHOR entry", "ANCHOR with bad instance ID syntax", "malformed entity reference in ANCHOR", "ANCHOR section grammar violation", "anchor target ID not a number".
reproducer: `ANCHOR; <part_anchor>=#42@x; ENDSEC;`
title: Malformed entity ID inside an ANCHOR entry (non-numeric `#`)

cross_oracle_note: pure-Python Part-21 validator rejects (reject(E_UNRESOLVED_REFS)); OCCT silently accepts (load is `empty`). OCC auto-heals a spec-level violation. Synonyms: "ANCHOR points at undefined #NNN", "anchor references missing instance", "filtered instance still in ANCHOR", "ANCHOR forward reference unresolved", "STEP anchor names ghost entity".
description: ANCHOR may reference data instances, but every `#NNN` it names must eventually resolve in some DATA section of the same file. Generators emit anchors for instances that were filtered out of the DATA section.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as undefined reference after the two-pass declare/resolve phase; tolerant mode may keep the file but mark the anchor as broken.
notes: Cross-oracle: pure-Python Part-21 validator rejects (reject(E_UNRESOLVED_REFS)); OCCT silently accepts (load is `empty`). OCC auto-heals a spec-level violation. Synonyms: "ANCHOR points at undefined #NNN", "anchor references missing instance", "filtered instance still in ANCHOR", "ANCHOR forward reference unresolved", "STEP anchor names ghost entity".
reproducer: `ANCHOR; <part_anchor>=#100; ENDSEC; DATA; #1=PRODUCT(..); ENDSEC;` (no `#100` defined).
title: Forward reference inside ANCHOR section to undefined data instance

description: Multi-schema FILE_SCHEMA with embedded comments inside the schema-name list (`FILE_SCHEMA(('CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN' /* legacy */, 'AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN'))`) or with vendor-specific extensions confuses naive header parsers.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: parse FILE_SCHEMA via the same robust string-literal tokenizer as DATA; choose the most-capable supported schema; never fall back to byte-level regex on the raw header.
notes: Synonyms: "comment inside FILE_SCHEMA list", "vendor extension in schema name list", "whitespace in FILE_SCHEMA element", "FILE_SCHEMA with embedded comment", "schema-name list malformed".
reproducer: `FILE_SCHEMA(('CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN' /* legacy */, 'AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN'));`
sender: CAD Exchanger CHANGES v3.24.8 ("improved parsing of FILE_SCHEMA headers")
title: Schema name in FILE_SCHEMA has whitespace, comments, or vendor extensions inside the list

description: Several Recommended Practices specify lower-case keyword strings as canonical attribute values (e.g. `'composite'` on `geometric_tolerance_relationship`). Producers that emit these in mixed or upper case break receivers that string-compare strictly.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept (case-insensitive match for documented RP keyword values on import); warn; emit canonical lower-case on export.
notes: Adjacent to Lh018 but specifically about RP-defined string attribute values rather than Part-21 keywords. **See also**: Lh018, Pmi043. Synonyms: "lower-case enum value in name field", "Recommended Practices keyword case mismatch", "composite spelled in mixed case", "STEP attribute string-compare fails on case", "RP-defined keyword not lower-case".
reproducer: `GEOMETRIC_TOLERANCE_RELATIONSHIP('Composite',..);` instead of `'composite'`.
title: Lower-case `name` field values where Recommended-Practices keywords are defined

description: OCCT auto-detects I-DEAS-style non-manifold encoding by substring-matching the FILE_NAME `preprocessor_version` field. Misses other I-DEAS variants whose preprocessor string differs; flags false positives on tools whose preprocessor mentions "I-DEAS".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept by detecting non-manifold encoding from the entity graph (e.g. presence of `NON_MANIFOLD_SURFACE_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION`), not from a substring of header metadata.
notes: **See also**: Lh019. Synonyms: "I-DEAS auto-detect by FILE_NAME substring", "preprocessor_version string match brittle", "false-positive non-manifold detection", "STEP receiver inferring vendor from header", "originating-system substring detection".
reproducer: file with `FILE_NAME(..,..,(''),(''),'I-DEAS Master Series 11','','');` versus a renamed variant.
sender: I-DEAS variants (and any tool whose preprocessor string changes)
title: Header recognition relies on FILE_NAME originating-system substring (I-DEAS auto-detect)

description: ISO 10303-21 distinguishes `#NAME`/`@NAME` (uppercase identifier, refers to a schema-defined constant) from `#NNN`/`@NNN` (refers to an instance). Tools occasionally emit `#PI` thinking it is a literal alias when the schema defines no such constant, producing an unresolved-reference error.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as undefined constant with a diagnostic that distinguishes "constant not in schema" from "instance not defined".
notes: Synonyms: "#NAME constant reference where #NNN expected", "@NAME used as instance reference", "schema constant in STEP DATA", "#PI as alias not resolved", "constant reference unresolved".
reproducer: `#1=DIRECTION('',(#PI,0.,0.));` where `PI` is not a schema-defined constant.
title: Constant reference (`#NAME`/`@NAME`) used where instance reference required

byte_assertions: contains(b"DATA('geometry'") or contains(b"DATA('pmi'") or contains(b'@geometry#') or contains(b'@geom#')
description: Edition-3 introduces named DATA sections (`DATA('section_name')`) and cross-section references of the form `@section_name#NNN` to refer to instance NNN inside a different section. Edition-2 readers (the majority) recognise only `DATA;` (no name) and a single anonymous data section. Such readers either ignore the section name (collapsing all instances into one global pool, where `#NNN` may collide between sections) or choke on the `@` syntax.
expected_kernel_behavior: parse named DATA sections and resolve `@name#NNN` cross-references against the named section; reject duplicate section names. Edition-2-only kernels should reject the file rather than silently collapse handles.
notes: **See also**: Lh024. Synonyms: "cross-section reference @section#NNN", "Ed.3 named DATA section reference", "Ed.2 reader rejects @section#NNN", "named DATA section unsupported", "multi-DATA section cross reference".
reproducer: two named DATA sections `'geometry'` and `'pmi'`; an instance in `'pmi'` references `@geometry#2`.
sources: 16-iso-spec ISO 10303-21 Ed.3 §7 (multi-section data, cross-section reference syntax)

A REFERENCE in another file pointing at the duplicated name resolves nondeterministically.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject duplicate anchor names with a diagnostic; or, if a tolerant policy is chosen, document the deterministic disambiguation rule (first-wins / last-wins) and warn.

description: Edition-3 permits user-defined header entities prefixed with `!` (e.g. `!COMPANY_INFO`). The order, duplication, and unknown-record rules are weakly specified. description: Edition-3 FILE_POPULATION records declare a 'population' (a named subset of instances) whose closure is determined by a separate marker or by section boundary. When the marker is missing or misspelt, instances appear to belong to multiple populations or to none. Consumers diverge on whether to treat the open population as covering the whole DATA section or to discard the population designation.
expected_kernel_behavior: parse FILE_POPULATION metadata and either apply the named population to the entire DATA section deterministically or reject the unterminated population with a diagnostic; do not silently apply to an arbitrary subset.
notes: **See also**: Lh016. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts the unterminated `FILE_POPULATION` record with no diagnostic; kernel mishandling; the catalog above forbids silent application to an arbitrary subset. description: Edition-3 multi-DATA-section files may reuse `#NNN` in different sections; intra-section references default to the local section. A producer may emit a bare `#NNN` inside one section that should resolve against another (intent unclear), or copy/paste a reference forgetting the `@name` prefix. The receiver resolves to the wrong instance silently.

notes: **See also**: Lh016. **OCC behavior**: silently picks one timestamp without surfacing the conflict; kernel mishandling; the catalog above forbids silent preference. description: Edition-3 named DATA sections allow a cross-section reference `@section#NNN`. A producer that organises its model into a foundation section plus a derived section can emit `@derived#10` whose definition is itself `@foundation#20`. A receiver that does not eagerly resolve transitive cross-section references either presents the user with the indirection-handle (a placeholder pointing at another reference) or short-circuits and skips the indirection. The two outcomes diverge geometrically. Bug-reporter language: "cross-section ref through another ref", "STEP file has chained cross-section pointers".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: resolve transitive cross-section references to their concrete instance before geometry uses them; or, if a placeholder model is preferred, document the deferred-resolution policy and warn-and-accept when the chain is followed.
notes: **See also**: Lh033, Lh039. Synonyms: "chained cross-section reference", "@s1#10 resolves to @s2#20", "transitive @section reference", "STEP cross-section chain", "multi-hop named-section reference".

sources: 16-iso-spec ISO 10303-21 Ed.3 §7 (named DATA sections, cross-section reference syntax)
title: Cross-section reference resolves through chain (`@s1#10` defined as `@s2#20`)

description: Edition-3 cross-section references `@name#NNN` resolve against the section whose `DATA('name')` declaration matches `name`. A producer that misspells the section name in a cross-reference (`@geomtry#5` for `@geometry#5`), or refers to a section that was renamed during refactoring, or copies records from another file without updating the section name, leaves a dangling reference. Receivers diverge: strict ones reject, lenient ones substitute null and load the rest, some search alternative sections in declaration order and silently bind to a wrong instance.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject the unresolved cross-reference with a precise diagnostic naming the missing section and the referencing instance; never silently bind to a same-named instance in a different section.
notes: **See also**: Lh033, Lh039. Synonyms: "misspelled section name in cross-reference", "@geomtry instead of @geometry", "STEP @section name typo", "renamed section reference broken", "cross-reference to non-existent section".

description: ISO 10303-21 mandates that HEADER contain at minimum FILE_DESCRIPTION, FILE_NAME, and FILE_SCHEMA records (in that order). A pathological writer emits a HEADER section consisting of only `/* */` block comments; the required records are absent. Spec-conforming readers cannot determine the file's edition, encoding declaration, or schema name; they must reject. Lenient readers may invent default metadata (assume Edition-2, ISO-8859-1, AP203) and proceed, hiding the producer-side failure. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file has empty header", "no FILE_SCHEMA in file", "header is just comments", "schema unknown".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject the file with a diagnostic naming each missing required record; do not invent default metadata to allow downstream import.
notes: Distinguishable from Lh043 (comments-inside-string). **See also**: Lh037, Lh042. Synonyms: "HEADER contains only comments", "STEP header missing required records", "FILE_DESCRIPTION absent from header", "comment-only HEADER section", "empty HEADER with /* */ only".
reproducer: a Part-21 file whose HEADER section is `HEADER; /* exported by build pipeline */ /* metadata unavailable */ ENDSEC;` (no FILE_DESCRIPTION / FILE_NAME / FILE_SCHEMA), followed by a normal DATA section.
sender: deduced — writer pipelines that compose the HEADER section as a comment-only placeholder during a partial export or when the metadata source is unavailable
sources: 16-iso-spec ISO 10303-21 §6.2 (required HEADER records: FILE_DESCRIPTION, FILE_NAME, FILE_SCHEMA)
bug-reporter language: "STEP file has empty header"
title: HEADER section contains only `/* */` comments and no required records

description: ISO 10303-21 spells the framing keywords `ISO-10303-21`, `HEADER`, `DATA`, `ENDSEC`, and `END-ISO-10303-21` exclusively in upper case. A producer that emits any of these in lower or mixed case (`header;`, `data;`, `endsec;`) violates the framing grammar. Strict parsers reject at the first mis-cased keyword; lenient parsers fold case and proceed. The lenient reading hides the producer defect and allows nonconforming files to circulate. Bug-reporter language: "STEP keywords lower-case", "data; not DATA;", "lower-case ISO-10303-21".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject; framing keywords are case-sensitive in the spec text. A tolerant case-fold may be offered as an opt-in compatibility mode.
notes: Distinct from Le027 (8-bit / case-insensitive lexer); Le027 is lexer-side tolerance for entity-type keywords; Lh047 is the framing keywords specifically. Synonyms: "lowercase data; instead of DATA;", "lowercase STEP framing keywords", "header; in STEP file", "endsec; lowercase", "STEP framing keyword case wrong".
reproducer: a Part-21 file with `header;`, `data;`, `endsec;` instead of `HEADER;`, `DATA;`, `ENDSEC;`.
sender: deduced — writers built from a generic EXPRESS-instance serialiser that lower-cases all identifiers, or hand-rolled writers that confuse the EXPRESS reserved-word case-insensitivity rule with Part-21 keyword case
sources: 16-iso-spec ISO 10303-21 §6.2 (keywords ISO-10303-21, HEADER, DATA, ENDSEC, END-ISO-10303-21 are upper-case)
title: Lower-case section keywords (`data;` instead of `DATA;`)

category: §12.1b header structure & instance numbering (sub-class: pipeline / I/O API)
description: The STEP reader's public API takes a filesystem path and internally `fopen`s it. A consumer that has the STEP content in memory (downloaded from object storage, unzipped from a `.stpz` wrapper, or read from a pipe) is forced to spill it to a temporary file first; which fails on read-only / chrooted hosts and adds I/O cost. The bug class is "API expects path; offers no stream entry point", and the on-disk file content is well-formed; the defect is in the reader's I/O contract.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; provide an `istream`-based read entry point; never require a seekable filesystem path. Document that producers may call the stream-based API directly.
notes: **See also**: Pf022. Synonyms: "STEP reader requires file path", "no in-memory STEP import", "cannot read STEP from std::istream", "API needs filesystem path".
reproducer: well-formed minimal STEP file (10-line cube). The catalog entry documents that consumers must spill to disk because the reader has no `Read(std::istream&)` overload.
sender: Server-side / sandboxed pipelines that hand the kernel a `std::istream` or memory buffer rather than a filesystem path.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP support C++ streams for import", "reader requires a filesystem path", "no way to import from in-memory buffer". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: STEP reader cannot consume a non-seekable stream (in-memory / pipe / network)

description: Distinct from Wr057 — this is the *reader side* of the same architecture class. The OCCT wrapper's entity-table reader assumes little-endian on disk; on big-endian hosts it reads malformed entity-IDs and drops shapes from the data section. The file content is well-formed; the wrapper layer's byte-order assumption is wrong.
expected_kernel_behavior: explicit endianness handling in the wrapper's binary buffers; CI matrix on at least one big-endian arch.
notes: Synonyms: "cascadio endianness s390x", "OCCT wrapper big-endian byte-order", "STEP shapes dropped on big-endian", "cascadio tests fail s390x wrong endianness", "OCCT binding endian bug".
reproducer: `REPRESENTATION_RELATIONSHIP('endian_drop','',#9005,#9005)` — a self-referencing rep-rel that the wrapper drops on big-endian.

title: Big-endian / s390x byte-order in OCCT wrapper drops shapes

description: A reader's data state is "Unloaded"; the file was opened but the entity table was never populated (e.g., parser bailed silently after the header). category: §12.1c (sub-class: virtual-dispatch fall-through, umbrella over stub manifestations)
description: BRL-CAD step-g virtual-dispatches every subtype through `LoadONBrep`; the base implementation prints to stderr and returns false. Any subtype the importer does not specifically override (e.g. `SeamCurve`, `CompositeCurve`, `BoundedPCurve`, `CompositeCurveOnSurface`, `CurveBoundedSurface`, `RectangularCompositeSurface`, `SurfacePatch`, `CartesianTransformationOperator`, `Polyline`) falls through and gets dropped without caller-side knowledge that geometry was lost. The diagnostic prints to stderr only and never propagates as an error code; callers cannot distinguish full success from partial drop. Fixture demonstrates the pattern with `SEAM_CURVE` since cylinders almost always carry one.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject; every stubbed dispatch must escalate to a `STEP_LOAD_ERROR` that propagates to the top-level converter; the converter must exit non-zero when any subgraph reachable from a referenced `ADVANCED_BREP_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION` returned false. Distinct from In013 (the kernel-actor "no actor" case): here the actor exists but is a stub.
notes: **See also**: Gn038, Twi100, Twi101, Gs057, Gs058, U045, In013, Pf037. Synonyms: "step-g LoadONBrep not implemented umbrella", "virtual-dispatch fall-through silently drops geometry", "stderr-only diagnostic for missing subtype", "BRL-CAD step-g cannot escalate stub-misses to error".
reproducer: a `SEAM_CURVE` referenced from a cylinder host; step-g's `SeamCurve::LoadONBrep` stub returns false and the seam geometry is lost.
sender: deduced from BRL-CAD step-g source survey (umbrella for specific manifestations Gn038, Twi100, Twi101, Gs057, Gs058, U045).
sources: BRL-CAD `src/conv/step/step-g/Curve.cpp` base stub `std::cerr << "Error: ::LoadONBrep(..) not implemented for " << entityname
bug-reporter language: "step-g LoadONBrep not implemented", "STEP subtype silently dropped", "BRL-CAD reader cannot diagnose which type was lost".
title: `LoadONBrep` virtual-dispatch fall-through umbrella (BRL-CAD step-g)

description: ISO 10303-21 grammar requires every REAL to carry a decimal point (`1.`, `1.0`, `0.5`). Generators that print integer values into REAL slots emit `1` where `1.` is required (e.g. `IFCDIRECTION((1,0,0))`). stepcode warns and salvages via `istringstream >> double`; strict readers reject. Implementors Issue 003 records the original disagreement: integers must not be followed by a dot, REALs must be.
expected_kernel_behavior: Strict reject by default; lenient mode auto-promote INTEGER → REAL with a warning. Never silently coerce.
notes: A primary cause of integer-vs-real type-coercion bugs. **See also**: Ad049, Ls002, Ls003, Ls004, Ls005, Ls006, Ls009. **OCC behavior**: silently coerces the integer to a REAL with no diagnostic; kernel mishandling; the catalog above forbids silent coercion. Synonyms: "REAL with no decimal point", "integer where REAL required", "1 written instead of 1.", "DIRECTION coords missing dots", "STEP REAL missing trailing period".
title: REAL literal missing mandatory decimal point

description: Grammar requires at least one digit before the dot. `.5` is not legal; `0.5` is. C/Python `%g` formatters frequently emit bare `.5`.
expected_kernel_behavior: Strict reject; lenient readers commonly accept implicit zero.
notes: **See also**: Ls001. Synonyms: "REAL with no digit before decimal", ".5 instead of 0.5 in STEP", "leading-dot REAL literal", "%g formatter emits .5", "missing zero before decimal".
title: REAL literal with no digit before the decimal point

description: ISO 10303-21 specifies upper-case `E` for the REAL exponent; lower-case `e`, embedded whitespace (`1.5 E+3`), or `+` sign in the exponent (`1e+18`) are non-conforming. Locale-aware printers also produce these.
expected_kernel_behavior: Lex `[+-]?\d+(\.\d*)?([eE][+-]?\d+)?` permissively; emit warning for non-canonical subsets.
notes: **See also**: Ls001. Synonyms: "lowercase e in REAL exponent", "1e+18 instead of 1E+18", "whitespace in REAL exponent", "STEP exponent has plus sign", "non-standard exponent in STEP".
title: Lower-case `e` exponent or whitespace around exponent

description: Some legacy Fortran-fronted exporters (older I-DEAS, CADAM converters) emit `1.0D5` instead of `1.0E5`. ISO 10303-21 only allows `E`/`e`.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject with diagnostic "exponent must be 'E', got 'D'".
notes: **See also**: Ls001. Synonyms: "Fortran D exponent in STEP", "1.0D5 instead of 1.0E5", "legacy Fortran writer emits D exponent", "I-DEAS D-exponent REAL", "CADAM D-style exponent".
title: Fortran-style `D` exponent (`1.0D5`)

description: Some generators write `+1.0` for positive REAL. The Part-21 BNF arguably disallows leading `+` for INTEGER but admits it for REAL; uniform handling preferred.
expected_kernel_behavior: Accept signed reals and integers uniformly; never silently strip the sign.
notes: **See also**: Ls001. **OCC behavior**: silently strips the leading `+` sign with no diagnostic on the surrounding context; kernel mishandling; the catalog above expects uniform handling without sign-stripping. Synonyms: "plus sign on positive REAL", "+1.0 in STEP literal", "explicit positive sign on numeric", "STEP rejects leading plus", "INTEGER with explicit plus".
title: Explicit positive sign on numeric literal (`+1.0`)

description: Modern languages tolerate `1_000_000`. Some in-house exporters borrow this and emit `IFCREAL(1_000.0)`. ISO 10303-21 disallows underscores in numerics.
expected_kernel_behavior: Strict reject with clear "underscore not permitted in numeric literal".
notes: **See also**: Ls001. Synonyms: "underscore in numeric literal", "1_000_000 in STEP REAL", "digit grouping in STEP number", "Python-style underscore in STEP", "thousands separator inside number".
title: Numeric literal with embedded underscore digit-grouping

description: `1.0E+999999` parsed via `strtod` yields `inf`; `NaN` results from malformed inputs. Geometry pipelines that compare via `<`/`>` then violate sort invariants in STL containers.
expected_kernel_behavior: Clamp magnitude or reject non-finite where geometry expects finite.
notes: **See also**: Ad014. Synonyms: "1.0E+999999 overflows to infinity", "STEP REAL becomes inf", "NaN from STEP", "infinity in geometry pipeline", "non-finite REAL breaks sort".
title: Float literal with extreme exponent / non-finite real

description: Spec permits leading zeros and a leading sign on INTEGER but no `0x` hex or interpretation of leading zero as octal. Some tools emit `0x10` or interpret `010` as octal-8.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject hex/octal; accept leading `+` and zeros per spec.
notes: **See also**: Ls001. Synonyms: "hex literal in STEP integer", "0x10 in STEP", "octal interpretation of 010", "STEP integer with 0x prefix", "non-decimal integer literal".
reproducer: `#1=POSITIVE_INTEGER_VALUE(0x10);`
title: Integer literal with hex/octal forms

description: Multiple-inheritance entities are encoded as parts whitespace-separated inside outer parens; `#1=( A() B() C() )`. The external mapping requires alphabetic leaf order; a writer that emits leaves in arbitrary order produces a record that compliant readers should warn about (not reject).
expected_kernel_behavior: Accept space-separated record list; sort internally for dispatch; preserve order on round-trip; warn on non-alphabetic input but do not reject.
notes: **See also**: Ls047, Ls048. Synonyms: "complex entity leaves out of order", "multiple-inheritance leaves not alphabetic", "STEP complex record wrong order", "leaf order divergent from external mapping", "complex entity ordering error".
reproducer: `#10=( CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT('DEG',#9) NAMED_UNIT(*) PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT() );` (well-formed) and the same with leaves reordered, e.g. `#20=( PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT() NAMED_UNIT(*) CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT('DEG',#9) );`.
title: Complex / multiple-inheritance entity record: non-alphabetic leaf ordering

description: Two distinct empty-list forms exist: a zero-attribute entity `#1=ABSTRACT_PT()` and an empty typed parameter `IFCMEASURE(())`. Lexical layer accepts `#1=PRODUCT();` but the schema expects N attributes.
expected_kernel_behavior: Lex layer accepts `()` as zero-argument record; semantic layer must reject if schema requires N>0 with "0 attributes, expected N". Reject zero-argument typed parameters unless the schema explicitly permits.
notes: **See also**: Ad015. Synonyms: "empty parameter list versus null", "PRODUCT() with no attributes", "zero-attribute STEP entity", "schema expects attributes but none provided", "empty parens for typed parameter".
reproducer: `#1=BOUNDED_SURFACE();` versus `#2=IFCMEASURE(IFCLENGTHMEASURE());`
title: Empty parameter list `()` versus typed empty parameter

description: `*` denotes derived/inherited attribute; `$` denotes null OPTIONAL value. Generators substitute one for the other. Inside aggregate elements only `$` is permitted as a "no value" placeholder; `*` is an attribute-level marker only. Some senders also emit a value for a derived slot instead of `*`.
expected_kernel_behavior: Schema-aware kernel cross-checks `*`/`$` against the attribute kind in EXPRESS; reject `*` inside list elements; emit "expected `*` (derived)" rather than a generic type error.
notes: Synonyms: "dollar versus star in STEP attribute", "* used where $ expected", "$ used in derived slot", "untyped parameter confusion", "STEP null vs derived marker".
reproducer: `#1=SI_ENERGY_UNIT((#2),*,$,.JOULE.);` vs `#1=SI_ENERGY_UNIT((#2),$,$,.JOULE.);`; `#1=POLYLINE('',(*,#10,#11));` (`*` inside list).
title: Untyped (`*`) attribute used where derived not declared / `$` confused with `*`

description: A list of attributes lacks a comma separator. SFA reports `"Expecting ',', found _3DV instead."`
expected_kernel_behavior: Strict reject with precise location diagnostic.
notes: Synonyms: "missing comma between STEP attributes", "Expecting comma found _3DV", "STEP attribute separator dropped", "two attributes adjacent without comma", "comma-less attribute list".
reproducer: `#1=CARTESIAN_POINT('p' (0.,0.,0.));` (missing comma after `'p'`).
title: Missing comma between attribute values

description: `(a,,b)` leaves an attribute slot empty. Correct null is `$`, derived is `*`. Empty slot is a generator bug. Parsers that map positional slots without re-checking arity may construct the entity with one fewer attribute, leading to uninitialised fields.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject with "expected parameter, found ','"; do not silently treat empty slot as `$`.
notes: **OCC behavior**: silently treats the empty slot as `$` (omitted) and proceeds; kernel mishandling; the catalog above forbids silent slot-equivalence. Synonyms: "double comma in STEP aggregate", "(a,,b) empty slot", "STEP entity attribute slot empty", "empty parameter slot in entity", "consecutive commas in attribute list".
title: Double comma / empty parameter slot

description: Aggregates do not permit trailing commas. JS/Python-influenced generators emit `(1.,2.,3.,)`. Recursive-descent grammars that accept it append a default-constructed element, mismatching schema-declared count.
expected_kernel_behavior: Strict reject; lenient strip and warn.
notes: Synonyms: "trailing comma in STEP aggregate", "(1.,2.,3.,) extra comma", "JS-style trailing comma in STEP", "extra comma at end of list", "aggregate ends with comma".
title: Trailing comma at end of aggregate

description: Each `ENDSEC` must be followed by a semicolon. Files sometimes carry `ENDSEC` followed directly by a newline and the next section keyword.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject in strict mode; lenient may accept and warn.
notes: Synonyms: "ENDSEC without trailing semicolon", "STEP ENDSEC missing semicolon", "section terminator no semicolon", "ENDSEC followed by newline only", "STEP ENDSEC newline before next keyword".

`HEADER;
..
ENDSEC
DATA;`

description: First non-whitespace token must be `ISO-10303-21;` (case-sensitive, hyphens, no leading whitespace, no BOM). Real files prepend UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`), use lowercase, miss the trailing semicolon, double the hyphens (`ISO--10303-21`), or wrap in an XML envelope.
expected_kernel_behavior: Strict reject; lenient strip UTF-8 BOM, uppercase-compare keyword, warn. Reject UTF-16/UTF-32 BOMs with clear error.
notes: **See also**: Le001. Synonyms: "missing opening ISO-10303-21 line", "STEP file no magic header", "lowercase iso-10303-21", "double-hyphen in ISO-10303-21", "BOM before STEP magic".
reproducer: `\xEF\xBB\xBFISO-10303-21;\nHEADER;..` or `iso-10303-21\nHEADER;..`
title: Missing or malformed opening magic line `ISO-10303-21;`

Synonyms: "garbage after STEP end marker", "log lines after END-ISO-10303-21", "concatenated STEP files", "data after STEP terminator", "stray DATA after end marker".

expected_kernel_behavior: Stop reading at the first end marker; treat trailing bytes as warning and discard. Reject second `DATA` at top level.

Synonyms: "garbage after STEP end marker", "log lines after END-ISO-10303-21", "concatenated STEP files", "data after STEP terminator", "stray DATA after end marker".

description: Edition 1 had inline SCOPE/ENDSCOPE delimiters; Editions 2/3 removed them but legacy translators still emit them. EXPORT lists also appeared inside ENDSCOPE in Ed.1. Implementors Issues 001/002 record the disagreement on whether modern processors must parse SCOPE blocks.
expected_kernel_behavior: Strict Ed.2/Ed.3 reject; lenient skip-to-matching-ENDSCOPE without aborting; emit a single informational warning per file.
notes: Synonyms: "legacy SCOPE block in STEP", "Edition 1 SCOPE/ENDSCOPE", "EXPORT list in STEP", "old-style scope delimiters", "Ed.1 scope blocks in modern STEP".
title: Legacy SCOPE/ENDSCOPE blocks (Edition 1) and EXPORT lists

description: A `/* .. */` comment containing an apostrophe is rejected because the comment-skip routine and a separate string-literal recognizer share a regex/scanner that mis-pairs the in-comment apostrophe with the next apostrophe in the file.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: comments scanned to next `*/` independent of any string state; apostrophe inside comment is opaque.
notes: Synonyms: "apostrophe inside STEP comment misread", "comment containing single quote breaks parser", "comment apostrophe paired with later quote", "STEP comment quote desyncs scanner", "in-comment apostrophe confuses lexer".
reproducer: `/* plane angle is 'degree' as non-SI unit */` placed between header and DATA.
title: Apostrophe inside `/* .. */` comment misread as string delimiter

description: ISO 10303-21 comments do not nest. A naive scanner that re-fires on inner `/*` (or fails to require both `*` and `/` consecutively for close) desynchronizes when comments contain Windows paths or URLs.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: only `*/` ends a comment; `/*` within a comment is literal text. After the first `*/` everything else is code.
notes: Synonyms: "nested comment in STEP", "Windows path inside STEP comment breaks scanner", "URL in STEP comment opens nested comment", "/*/ inside STEP comment", "comment nesting confusion".
reproducer: `/* path C:/foo/bar */` and `/* outer /* inner */ should still be comment */`
title: Forward-slash inside `/* .. */` comment treated as nested-comment open

description: stepcode hardcodes an 8 KiB ceiling on comment body length. Files with multi-page log banners exceed this and trip rejection.
expected_kernel_behavior: Comment length unbounded (memory-bound only); never silently truncate.
notes: Synonyms: "STEP comment exceeds buffer", "8KB comment limit", "multi-page log banner in STEP", "long comment rejected by stepcode", "huge STEP comment overflows buffer".
reproducer: Single `/* .. */` containing >8192 characters before first `DATA;` instance.
title: Comment longer than implementation buffer

description: ISO 10303-21 §5.2 says LF, CR, TAB, FF are ignored characters; §5.6 says only SPACE, comments, and print directives separate tokens. Strict reading: `#1\t=\tCARTESIAN_POINT(..)` after tab-removal becomes `#1=CARTESIAN_POINT(..)`, but `#1<TAB>2` would become `#12`. Real-world parsers tolerate any ASCII whitespace as a separator. Defects: split keyword `FILE _SCHEMA`, internal whitespace inside `#NNN` references, files with `\r`-only line endings, `\f` between attributes, long-line wrapping inside an instance.
expected_kernel_behavior: Treat any of `\t \f\r\n` as whitespace separator (matches user expectation); preserve line/column counting across line-ending conventions; warn on TAB inside an identifier; accept print-control directives `\F\` and `\N\` as zero-width separators where token separator is allowed; reject embedded whitespace inside `#N` (between `#` and digits).
notes: **See also**: Le028. Synonyms: "tab as STEP token separator", "FF as token separator", "tab between # and =", "ignored char inside STEP token", "whitespace handling in STEP scanner".
reproducer: `FILE _SCHEMA(('AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN'));`, `# 12 = IFCPERSON(..);`, file with CR-only line endings, `#1=IFCPOINT(\F\(0.,0.,0.));`
title: Whitespace handling: tab/CR/LF/FF as token separators or ignored chars

byte_assertions: contains(b'.LENGTHUNIT,') or contains(b'.true.') or contains(b'(TRUE)') or contains(b'."LEFT".')
description: ISO 10303-21 enum literals are `.IDENT.` where IDENT is an EXPRESS-conformant identifier (uppercase letters and digits only). Defects: missing closing dot, lower-case body, digit-leading body, quoted body (`."LEFT".`), missing leading dot.
expected_kernel_behavior: Strict reject; lenient mode may case-fold the identifier but the dots are non-negotiable.
notes: **See also**: Ls035. Synonyms: "STEP enum missing dotted delimiters", "lowercase enum body", "missing leading dot on STEP enum", "quoted enum value", "STEP enum value malformed".
reproducer: `#1=IFCSIUNIT(*,.LENGTHUNIT,$,.METRE.);` (missing closing dot after LENGTHUNIT); `#2=DIRECTION_FLAG(.true.);`; `#3=DIRECTION_FLAG(TRUE);`
title: Enumeration value missing dotted delimiters or with bad casing

description: `EDGE_CURVE.same_sense` is a BOOLEAN (`.T.`/`.F.`). Passing `.U.` (the LOGICAL UNKNOWN value) at this slot conflates LOGICAL with BOOLEAN. Some readers default to `true`, leaving an uninitialised bool that produces non-deterministic edge direction (regression on gcc 4.9 noted in OCCT 0029944).
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject the value (or default to `.T.` with an explicit warning); never leave the BOOLEAN uninitialised.
notes: **See also**: Ad044, Ls034, Ls049, Ls050. Synonyms: "dot-U at BOOLEAN slot", "LOGICAL value in BOOLEAN attribute", "same_sense given .U.", "STEP boolean given UNKNOWN", "uninitialised bool from .U.".
reproducer: `EDGE_CURVE('',#12,#13,#14,.U.);` — `.U.` in the BOOLEAN `same_sense` slot.
title: Boolean attribute given `.U.` (LOGICAL UNKNOWN at BOOLEAN slot)

byte_assertions: contains(b'"0dead"') or contains(b'"4DEAD"') or contains(b'"FF"') or contains(b'"3DEAD"')
description: ISO 10303-21 BINARY syntax is `"<n><hex>*"` where `<n>` is `0`–`3` indicating unused bits in the final hex digit; hex digits are uppercase, even-count is required. Defects: lower-case hex (`"0dead"`), wrong leading nibble (`"4DEAD"` or `"FF"`), missing leading nibble, odd hex-digit count (`"3DEAD"`).
expected_kernel_behavior: Strict reject malformed forms; in particular enforce leading nibble in 0.3 and even hex-digit count. Lenient mode may accept lowercase but warn.
notes: Synonyms: "malformed BINARY literal in STEP", "binary literal lowercase hex", "wrong leading nibble on BINARY", "odd hex-digit count in STEP binary", "BINARY missing leading nibble".
reproducer: `BINARY_VALUE := "0DEAD";` (good) vs `"0dead";` vs `"4DEAD";` vs `"FF";` vs `"3DEAD";`
title: Binary literal `"…"` malformed (bit-count nibble or hex case)

description: ISO 10303-21 requires positive non-zero instance IDs. `#0` is invalid.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject `#0` with `E_INSTANCE_ID_RANGE`; continue parsing the remainder of the section rather than skipping it.
notes: **See also**: Lh023, Ls051, Ls052. Synonyms: "instance ID #0 invalid", "STEP entity numbered zero", "zero instance ID rejected", "#0 as definition or reference", "non-positive STEP instance ID".
title: Instance ID `#0` (must be positive non-zero)

description: Parser copies entity name into a fixed-size identifier buffer; classic strcpy overflow. ISO conformance class permits long names but not unbounded. Embedded `-` (hyphen) in identifiers is also disallowed (`BS7752-1`).
expected_kernel_behavior: Maximum identifier length per ISO conformance class (e.g. 256 chars); reject overflow before allocation. Reject `-` in identifiers; lenient mode may map to `_`.
notes: Synonyms: "very long STEP entity name", "fixed-buffer overflow on long name", "hyphen in STEP identifier", "BS7752-1 entity name rejected", "STEP entity name with dash".
title: Excessively long entity name

description: Unlike C, Part 21 does not concatenate adjacent string literals. `'foo' 'bar'` is two strings, not one. Generators that line-wrap long strings by writing two consecutive literals corrupt the data when the position expects exactly one STRING.
expected_kernel_behavior: When grammar expects a single STRING, reject. When position is `LIST OF STRING`, accept as two list elements (warn — likely unintended).
notes: Synonyms: "adjacent STEP string literals", "two strings line-wrap into one slot", "C-style string concatenation in STEP", "STEP string concatenation not allowed", "consecutive literals corrupt data".
reproducer: `FILE_DESCRIPTION(('first part' ' second part'),'2;1');`
title: String concatenation across consecutive literals (not allowed)

description: Control directives like `\X\`, `\S\`, `\F\`, `\N\` are valid only inside `'..'` string literals. Tools that pre-process content textually sometimes leave directives in BINARY values, ENUMERATION names, or between top-level tokens.
expected_kernel_behavior: Strict reject; lenient strip and warn.
notes: Synonyms: "X escape outside string literal", "STEP control directive in BINARY", "directive in enumeration name", "backslash X in non-string slot", "control directive between top-level tokens".
title: Print/control directives appearing outside string-literal context

byte_assertions: contains(b'syntax error') or contains(b'two distinct syntax errors')
description: A STEP reader parses a malformed file, accumulates syntax errors internally, then reports a generic "parsing failed" status to the caller. Detailed line / column / entity information is logged to stderr but not returned via API. Tools that wrap the reader (via Python / command-line) cannot present diagnostics to users. Typical fixture: two entities with distinct lexical syntax errors; e.g., one with an unclosed parenthesis and another with a missing string-literal quote.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject with structured diagnostics: reader returns a structured diagnostic list with file location, entity ID, and error text per error. Must not silently swallow syntax errors.
notes: **See also**: Ad088. Synonyms: "STEP parser error message inaccessible", "syntax error not surfaced to caller", "unclosed paren error swallowed", "parser warnings don't reach API", "STEP error log not exposed".
reproducer: STEP file with two distinct syntax errors (e.g., unclosed parentheses, missing quotes) at lines 100 and 200; caller obtains status only.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0031481 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: STEP parser syntax error messages inaccessible to caller (e.g., entities with unclosed parentheses and missing string quotes)

description: The Part-21 grammar requires the leaves of a complex entity record (`#1=( A() B() C() )`) to be separated by whitespace, not commas. A writer that emits commas (carrying habit from argument lists) produces a token that a strict reader must reject.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject comma-separated leaves in strict mode; lenient mode may accept-with-warning.
notes: **See also**: Ls010, Ls048. Synonyms: "complex entity leaves separated by commas", "multiple-inheritance leaves with comma separators", "STEP complex record uses commas not whitespace", "comma in complex entity rejected", "complex entity grammar violation".
