description: In a face's parametric (UV) domain, the outer `EDGE_LOOP`'s start and end vertices do not coincide within face tolerance, so the contour does not partition the plane (Jordan-curve failure). Typical pattern: face on a `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` whose seam edges each carry pcurves referenced via separate `DEFINITIONAL_REPRESENTATION`s that do not align; a gap remains at the u=2π vs u=0 seam between consecutive `ORIENTED_EDGE`s. Caused by missed seam edges on periodic surfaces, or by corrupt pcurves with gaps.
expected_kernel_behavior: connect the wire endpoints via period-shifting / vertex-merging / seam-insertion as appropriate, or reject as malformed when the gap exceeds the working tolerance budget.
notes: **See also**: Gp020, Gp028, Gs012, Twi020. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant. Synonyms: "edge_loop not closed in UV", "Jordan curve violation across periodic seam", "outer wire fails to close in parametric domain", "renderer falls back to isolines instead of triangulating", "face contour open across cylinder seam".
reproducer: Face on a cylinder, omit the seam edge so the outer wire is open in UV; renderers fall back to isolines instead of triangulating.
title: `EDGE_LOOP` contour not closed in UV (Jordan-curve violation across periodic-surface seam)

description: A pass that splits closed periodic faces / solids (full `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE`, `TOROIDAL_SURFACE`) along their seams produces new edges whose pcurves do not satisfy the same-parameter invariant — pcurve and 3D curve disagree at the same parameter value. Typical pattern: an `EDGE_CURVE` between vertices (10,0,0) and (-10,0,0) on a cylinder traverses the seam from u=0 to u=π in 3D, but the pcurve `LINE` is parameterised over [0, 1] instead of [0, π] — same UV path, different parameterisation, so the seam/branch handling is wrong. A topology checker reports invalid edges. The splitter returns a topologically inconsistent intermediate state.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: a face-splitter must restore the same-parameter invariant on the new edges before returning, or reject the operation. Returning an invalid intermediate burdens every caller.
notes: **See also**: Gp022, Twi032. Synonyms: "closed face splitter leaves invalid edges", "split-along-seam produces same-parameter violations", "topology checker flags edges after splitting cylinder", "face splitter returns invalid intermediate geometry", "splitting cylinder along seam breaks edge invariant".
reproducer: Take a full cylinder solid; split along its seam; run a topology checker — invalid edges flagged. Recompute same-parameter on the result — becomes valid.
title: Closed-face splitter leaves new pcurves out of sync with 3D curves on `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE`

description: A wire bounding a face on a periodic `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` (or torus, etc.) traverses the U=0 / U=2π seam, but the input does not include the seam edge that would carry the wire from one side of the seam to the other. Typical signature: pcurve `LINE` trim range (e.g. starts at u=5.5 with length 1.28) corresponds to a different angular interval on the cylinder than the 3D vertex positions imply (vertex angles around -0.78 rad and +0.50 rad), so pcurve and 3D-vertex angular positions disagree. Downstream shell composition sees an open contour in UV even though the wire is closed in 3D.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect that the wire crosses the seam and insert the seam edge automatically, or reject as malformed.
notes: **See also**: Gp026. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant. Synonyms: "wire crosses cylinder seam without seam edge", "missing seam edge on periodic surface wire", "pcurve range vs vertex angle disagree at seam crossing", "cylinder face wire spans U=0/U=2π without explicit seam", "open contour in UV from missing seam edge".
reproducer: STEP face where an outer wire of a cylindrical face crosses the U=0/U=2π seam direction without an explicit seam edge.
title: Wire crosses periodic-surface seam without an explicit seam edge (pcurve trim range vs vertex angular position mismatch)

description: After a period-shift pass on a revolved face's wire, the wire endpoints land in an inconsistent parameter band — some pcurve endpoints in `[0,2π]`, others in `[2π,4π]` — even though all should sit in a single period band. The inconsistency blocks subsequent triangulation, which expects a single coherent parameter window.
expected_kernel_behavior: a period-shift pass must produce a self-consistent UV band for all wire endpoints, or refuse the shift when no consistent band exists. A post-condition check on the band coverage catches the inconsistency.
notes: **See also**: Gs019. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant. Synonyms: "period-shift fix leaves wire across multiple bands", "wire endpoints in inconsistent UV bands after period adjust", "triangulation blocked by mixed-band pcurves", "revolved face period shift fails to converge", "pcurve endpoints scattered across periods after healing".
reproducer: Face on a `SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION` whose pcurves require shifting by 2π; run the period-shift pass; attempt to mesh.
title: Period-shift fix on revolved face leaves wire in inconsistent UV band, blocks meshing

description: PRO/E exports (identifiable by `originating_system` 'PRO/Engineer …' in `FILE_NAME`) contain pcurves with sharp bends, typically authored as degree-1 `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` in `.POLYLINE_FORM.` with vendor-specific interior knot multiplicities. These vendor-shaped B-spline pcurves must be protected from generic intersection-fix routines that would otherwise corrupt them. A specialized "bend-pcurve" pass holds the pcurve fixed while neighbors are adjusted.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; recognize PRO/E sender and route bent pcurves through the protective branch.
notes: **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({heal}). Kernel-bug witnessed: catalog asks for healing; OCC neither heals nor rejects; the input is dropped on the floor without diagnostic. Synonyms: "PRO/E polyline-form pcurve gets corrupted by intersection healer", "bent B-spline pcurve from PRO/Engineer", "pcurve sharp bend killed by generic ShapeFix", "polyline pcurve degree-1 with vendor multiplicities", "wire intersection fix damages PRO/E pcurve".
reproducer: PRO/E STEP file with a face whose pcurve has a sharp bend; run generic ShapeFix wire intersection healing; observe pcurve corruption.
sender: PRO/E (`PRO7978.igs`, `PRO10107.stp`)
title: Bent / polyline-form `B_SPLINE` pcurve from PRO/E IGES requires protective handling

description: After an IGES BRep round-trip (or other translator path), a cylindrical face appears with two distinct but identically-defined `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` instances (e.g. `#20` and `#21`) where each `ADVANCED_FACE` uses one copy; analytic identity is lost. A single 3D edge then has two pcurves on these supposedly-same surfaces; duplicate surface definitions and aliased pcurves create confusion, and pcurves stored against the second copy disagree with those against the first even though geometrically identical.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; canonicalize duplicate analytic surfaces post-IGES; re-bind pcurves to the canonical surface.
notes: **See also**: Gn023, Gp016. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({heal}). Kernel-bug witnessed: catalog asks for healing; OCC neither heals nor rejects; the input is dropped on the floor without diagnostic. Synonyms: "duplicate CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE instances after IGES BRep round-trip", "cylinder analytic identity lost", "two copies of same cylindrical surface", "duplicate analytic surfaces after IGES round-trip", "pcurves on supposedly-same cylinder disagree".
reproducer: Cylindrical face → IGES BRep → re-import; check that all faces of the cylinder share the same `Geom_CylindricalSurface` handle.
title: Cylinder represented twice as duplicate `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` instances loses analytic identity

description: A B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS has an internal knot whose multiplicity equals the degree, producing only C0 continuity at that parameter. Downstream meshers, fillet/chamfer engines, and IGES exporters that assume at least C1 mis-handle the discontinuity and emit kinks where the source intended a smooth join.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect the C0 break and either split the curve into two C∞-internal pieces, raise the knot multiplicity to enforce a true G1+ join, or report the discontinuity as a quality metric so downstream tools can handle it explicitly.
notes: Same defect applies to pcurve splitting on host surfaces. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({heal}). Kernel-bug witnessed: catalog asks for healing; OCC neither heals nor rejects; the input is dropped on the floor without diagnostic. Synonyms: "B-spline curve has C0 internal break", "interior knot multiplicity equals degree creates kink", "downstream tools cannot ingest C0 spline", "knot multiplicity=degree produces visible cusp", "B-spline kink at interior knot".
reproducer: Degree-2 B-spline whose knot vector is `(0,0,0, 0.5,0.5,0.5, 1,1,1)` — multiplicity 3 at u=0.5 forces C0; control polygon does not have collinear neighbors at the breakpoint.
title: B-spline curve has C0 internal break that downstream tools cannot ingest

description: A `COMPOSITE_CURVE` lists multiple segments that are intended to form a single continuous curve. Segment N's last 3D point sits at a distance of several millimetres from segment N+1's first 3D point; far beyond any reasonable connectivity tolerance. The composite curve is not actually connected; treating it as one curve produces invalid downstream geometry.
expected_kernel_behavior: report the connectivity defect with the offending segment indices and 3D gap; either bridge the segments by inserting a connecting curve, snap endpoints, or refuse to treat the aggregate as a single curve.
notes: Similar defect class to `Twi-` wire connectivity but at the curve-aggregate level. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({heal, reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: catalog allows either heal or reject; OCC silently accepts the bad input without doing either. Synonyms: "composite curve segments don't meet", "gap between consecutive composite curve segments", "composite_curve has disconnected segments", "segment N+1 starts far from segment N's end", "composite curve connectivity check fails".
reproducer: Two LINE-based EDGE_CURVEs whose vertices are at `(5,0,0)` and `(5.005,0,0)` respectively. Both edges share a wire but the kernel must report a 5e-3 disconnect.
title: Composite curve segments do not meet within connectivity tolerance

description: An edge on an analytic surface (cylinder, cone, sphere, torus, plane) carries a 3D space curve but no 2D pcurve. To trim the surface, the kernel must project the 3D curve into UV. Some senders never emit pcurves, expecting the consumer to compute them; the projection must remain same-parameter and may resolve to an analytic 2D primitive (line in UV) where the geometry permits.
expected_kernel_behavior: synthesize the missing pcurve via projection, validate same-parameter consistency afterwards, and emit an analytic 2D line where the underlying surface admits one (e.g., on cylinders, spheres). Alternatively, refuse the edge and require a sender that supplies pcurves.
notes: Distinct from a *bad* pcurve (Twi-class). Also see Gp019 (edge without pcurve). **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({heal, reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: catalog allows either heal or reject; OCC silently accepts the bad input without doing either. Synonyms: "edge has no parametric curve", "pcurve absent on face edge", "tessellator fails on edge with no UV curve", "kernel must project 3D curve onto surface", "edge without 2D representation needs synthesis".
reproducer: A vertical EDGE_CURVE on a CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE running from `(R,0,0)` to `(R,0,h)` with only a 3D LINE representation, no SURFACE_CURVE pcurve.
title: Edge has 3D curve but no pcurve, requiring projection onto host surface

description: A 2D-curve-shift routine intended for periodic surfaces is invoked on a planar (non-periodic) surface. The routine shifts the pcurve by the surface's "period"; but on a non-periodic surface the period is undefined, returning zero or NaN. The pcurve becomes invalid.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject as precondition error: pcurve-shifting only runs on surfaces flagged periodic; non-periodic surface invocation is a precondition error.
notes: **See also**: Twi084, Gp008. Synonyms: "pcurve shift on non-periodic surface", "period shift applied to planar surface returns NaN", "pcurve shift routine misfires on plane", "shift-by-period on non-periodic surface degenerates", "shifting pcurves on flat surface gives invalid result".
reproducer: Planar face with a wire whose pcurves were emitted with U values outside the face's parametric range. Healer applies a shift; on planar surface the shift is degenerate.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0028595 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Pcurve shifting on non-periodic surface produces wrong result

description: A projection of a 3D curve onto a surface produces a 2D curve that extends infinitely in the parametric domain instead of being bounded to the input curve's parameter range. Downstream consumers (face-bound check, mesher) read the unbounded curve and either crash or produce infinite tessellation.
expected_kernel_behavior: projection range matches input range exactly; never produce unbounded pcurves from bounded inputs.
notes: **See also**: Gp035. Synonyms: "pcurve projection produces unbounded line", "projection emits infinite parameter range", "bounded 3D curve becomes infinite pcurve after projection", "unbounded pcurve crashes mesher", "projection range doesn't match input curve range".
reproducer: 3D curve segment with parameter range `[0,1]`; project onto plane. Resulting pcurve has parameter range `[-∞, +∞]`.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0026198 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Pcurve projection produces infinite line instead of bounded

description: An edge's vertex point in 3D and the pcurve evaluated at the corresponding parameter disagree beyond vertex tolerance. The edge passes 3D-curve-vs-vertex check (because 3D curve does match vertex) but fails 2D-pcurve check.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject if either fails: vertex-pcurve consistency check separate from vertex-3D-curve check; both must pass independently.
notes: **See also**: Twi060, Twi088, Twi059. Synonyms: "vertex 3D point and pcurve disagree at endpoint", "pcurve evaluation at edge endpoint differs from vertex", "vertex-pcurve consistency check fails", "edge passes 3D check but fails 2D check", "UV at parameter doesn't lift to vertex 3D position".
reproducer: Edge with vertex V at `(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)`; 3D curve is a line from `(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)` to `(2.0, 0.0, 0.0)`. Pcurve on the hosting face evaluates at parameter 0 to UV `(0.5, 0.0)` whose 3D image is `(1.05, 0.0, 0.0)` — beyond vertex tolerance.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0025634 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Vertex 3D point and pcurve do not match within tolerance

description: A 3D B-spline curve, closed (first control point == last), is projected onto a surface to compute a pcurve. The projection algorithm walks the curve with discontinuity at the closing seam; the resulting pcurve has a wild excursion near the seam, parameter range no longer matches the input curve's range.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: closed-curve projection treats the seam as a continuity constraint; pcurve range matches input range; no spike. Must not silently produce spike.
notes: **See also**: Gp037, Twi088. Synonyms: "pcurve projection unstable on closed B-spline", "spike in pcurve at closure seam", "closed-curve projection has wild excursion at seam", "projection of closed B-spline produces wrong parameter range", "pcurve bumps near closing seam of periodic curve".
reproducer: Closed B-spline curve (degree 3, 8 control points with first == last); project onto plane. Pcurve has spike at seam parameter.
title: Pcurve projection unstable on closed B-spline curve

category: §12.2a pcurve defects (sub-class: writer-emitted pcurves disagree with 3D)
description: When pcurves are emitted alongside 3D curves on `EDGE_CURVE`, every receiver re-projects them to verify consistency. The writer's pcurve, computed by a separate pass after the 3D curve is fixed, often disagrees with the 3D curve at the edge tolerance; a re-import yields edges that drift off the surface, faces with `BRepCheck_InvalidEdgeOnSurface` errors, or sewing failures. The community workaround is to disable pcurve emission entirely; the kernel-side bug is that the two representations are not co-fitted.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; pcurves must be co-fitted with the 3D curve so that surface-evaluated pcurve and 3D curve agree within the edge tolerance; if they cannot be fitted, omit the pcurve and let the receiver re-project.
notes: **See also**: Gp028, Tfa023. Synonyms: "STEP writer pcurves disagree with 3D curves", "disable writing pcurves to STEP and IGES by default", "edge tolerance violated by writer pcurve", "pcurve drift after STEP round-trip".
reproducer: STEP file with `SURFACE_CURVE` carrying both a 3D curve and a `PCURVE` whose 2D parametric curve evaluates ~ε off the 3D curve when projected onto the surface. Receiver reports edge-on-surface tolerance violation.
sender: OCCT's STEP writer when configured to emit pcurves (`write.surfacecurve.mode = 1`).
sources: bug-reporter language: "disable writing pcurves to STEP and IGES by default", "pcurves and 3D curves disagree on round-trip", "writer-emitted pcurves cause downstream failures". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Pcurves emitted by default duplicate / contradict the surface 3D curve

description: Midspan 3D curve point (5,0,0) maps to PCURVE point (5.1,0,0) — 0.1 mm divergence exceeding edge tolerance 0.001 mm. Geometry: PLANE host; 3D LINE from (0,0,0) to (10,0,0); PCURVE B-spline.
expected_kernel_behavior: CheckCurve3dWithPCurve sample-point inspection detects the mismatch and flags the edge for healing or healing-time analysis.

description: SURFACE_CURVE has no PCURVE `(*)`. Some FixAddPCurve branches bypass plane-trivial PCURVE construction when geometry or downstream healing requires explicit parametric representation. Geometry: PLANE host; 3D LINE from (0,0,0) to (5,0,0); empty SURFACE_CURVE.associated_geometry list.
expected_kernel_behavior: FixAddPCurve should construct a trivial PCURVE (identity map) but plane-bypass branch skips it, leaving the edge without parametric curve data.

description: Reversing parametric direction without re-evaluating knot domain leaves stale multiplicity data. Naive range flip keeps knot structure intact even though parameter direction is inverted. Geometry: PLANE host; 3D LINE from (0,0,0) to (10,0,0); PCURVE B-spline degree 2, knots (0.0, 0.5, 1.0), control points (0,0), (3.333,2.5), (6.667,5.0), (10,7.5).
expected_kernel_behavior: FixReversed2d attempts to reverse PCURVE but the knot-vector corruption causes wrong parameter mapping during edge reconstruction.

description: Both endpoints and interior point are equidistant from probe point. Project's endpoint-bias returns endpoint distance even when interior local-min is the true projection. PCURVE maps to wrong parameter bounds. Geometry: PLANE host; 3D B-spline arc degree 2 with inflection at midspan; PCURVE B-spline.
expected_kernel_behavior: Project returns suboptimal projection result, causing downstream healers to misalign PCURVE parameter mapping or report stale boundary conditions.
title: Endpoint-bias projection picks wrong candidate when multiple equidistant points exist.

description: FixSameParameter copies EDGE_CURVE to new TEdge but preserves old range bounds. Kernel-bug witnessed: catalog wants a warning to surface; OCC accepts without any diagnostic. Synonyms: "duplicate knot value at non-end", "B-spline U knot vector has consecutive equal interior knots", "knot multiplicity not bumped despite repeated value", "two equal interior knots with multiplicity 1 each", "BSpline surface knot vector has bogus repeated entries".

Synonyms: "rational B-spline weights count doesn't match poles", "weights array length differs from control points", "NbWeights ≠ NbControlPoints", "NURBS curve weight vector wrong length", "rational BSpline missing weight or has extra weight".
occ_behavior_note: silent-empty (the malformed complex-instance entity is dropped at parse without a diagnostic) rather than the cited heal-or-crash. description: A circle is converted to a NURBS representation when exporting to a format that does not natively support analytic curves. The NURBS expression of a circle requires rational weights (control-point weights of `(1, 1/√2, 1, 1/√2, 1, ..)`); writer emits weights but forgets to mark the curve `RATIONAL_B_SPLINE_CURVE`. Reader treats it as uniform-weight, producing a polygonal approximation instead of an exact circle.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject untagged rationals: every B-spline with non-uniform weights must be tagged `RATIONAL_B_SPLINE_CURVE` (complex entity); receivers check the tag before applying weights. Must not silently accept missing tag.
notes: **See also**: Gn014. Synonyms: "rational B-spline missing RATIONAL flag", "circle as NURBS without rational marker", "weights present but RATIONAL_B_SPLINE_CURVE entity tag missing", "untagged rational B-spline imports as polygonal", "circle exact-NURBS form misses rational complex entity".
reproducer: B-spline curve, degree 2, 9 control points, knots `(0,0,0, 0.25,0.25, 0.5,0.5, 0.75,0.75, 1,1,1)`, weights `(1, √2/2, 1, √2/2, 1, √2/2, 1, √2/2, 1)`. Missing `RATIONAL_B_SPLINE_CURVE` complex-entity marker.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0006542 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Circle translated to NURBS form with rational weights but missing weight metadata

description: A `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS` V knot vector violates the non-decreasing invariant by containing a strictly descending pair (e.g. `(0.0, 0.6, 0.4, 1.0)`; 0.6 then 0.4). A compliant reader must reject the surface with a diagnostic naming the offending index.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject the surface with a diagnostic naming the offending index; never silently accept.
notes: **See also**: Gn001, Gn003. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); catalog disallows silent-accept. Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers enforcing the spec must reject (or surface a diagnostic); silent acceptance defeats the catalog's stated invariant. Synonyms: "B-spline knots non-monotonic", "V knot vector strictly descending", "BSpline surface knot vector not non-decreasing", "knots violate non-decreasing invariant", "knot value smaller than prior in BSpline surface".
reproducer: `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS` whose `v_knots` array contains a value strictly less than the prior value.
title: `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS` V knot vector strictly descending

description: A `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` with legitimate poles but a knot vector that collapses to one unique value (e.g. `knots = (0., 0.)` with multiplicities `(4, 4)`). The unique-knot count is 1, so the parametric range is empty and translation throws an exception.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject the curve with a precise diagnostic; emit a warning; continue translating the remainder of the file.
notes: **See also**: Gn001, Gn003. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject, warn-and-proceed}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant. Synonyms: "B-spline surface single distinct knot", "BSpline knot vector collapses to one unique value", "empty parametric range from collapsed knots", "all knots equal produces empty domain", "BSpline curve with degenerate knot vector throws".
reproducer: `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS('',3,(#20,#21,#22,#23),.UNSPECIFIED.,.F.,.F.,(4,4),(0.0,0.0),.UNSPECIFIED.);`
title: BSpline curve whose knot vector collapses to a single unique value

description: `BOUNDED_PCURVE` is a degenerate subclass whose role is to give a bounded version of an otherwise infinite parametric basis curve. step-g loads the entity into the in-memory model fine, but the LoadONBrep path falls through to the base-class stub which prints `"not implemented for BoundedPCurve"` and returns false. Trims referencing a `BOUNDED_PCURVE` in their `associated_geometry` list lose the parametric curve in the ON_Brep representation, so the trim becomes 3D-only and is later re-projected numerically (introducing drift). Distinct from Gn019 (coincident-control-point degeneracy): this is a *type-dispatch* defect rather than a degeneracy.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; `BoundedPCurve::LoadONBrep` must defer to its underlying definitional basis curve and reparameterise to the bounded subrange; if unhandled, emit `W_BOUNDED_PCURVE_FALLBACK` and project from 3D.
notes: **See also**: Gn019, Twi100, Twi101. Synonyms: "BOUNDED_PCURVE LoadONBrep stub", "step-g BOUNDED_PCURVE drop", "BOUNDED_PCURVE subtype unimplemented".
reproducer: `#41=BOUNDED_PCURVE('bp_on_plane', #14, #40);` referenced from a `SURFACE_CURVE.associated_geometry`. step-g loads the entity; LoadONBrep stub returns false.
sender: Producers that emit a bounded re-parametrisation of an otherwise infinite parametric basis curve.
sources: BRL-CAD `src/conv/step/step-g/Curve.cpp` `LoadONBrep` base stub `"::LoadONBrep(..) not implemented for <entity>"`
`BoundedPCurve` is a non-overriding subclass that inherits the stub
bug-reporter language: "BOUNDED_PCURVE dropped on import", "step-g subtype unsupported", "BOUNDED_PCURVE falls through to base-class stub".
title: `BOUNDED_PCURVE` LoadONBrep stub (BRL-CAD step-g)

description: A user requests a B-spline approximation of a non-rational curve (e.g., a polynomial of high degree) within tolerance ε. The approximation algorithm does not converge; the residual remains above ε after the maximum number of refinement iterations. Bug-reporter language: "approximation didn't converge", "B-spline fit failed", "tolerance too tight for fit".
expected_kernel_behavior: Return the partial result with the achieved residual reported; or reject.
notes: Synonyms: "fit didn't converge". Bytes alone are insufficient to demonstrate this defect; needs sibling input fixture. Tagged provenance_tier: runtime-only. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant.
reproducer: A `LINE` evaluated at densely-sampled points; request a B-spline approximation through these points within tolerance below the kernel's working precision.
sender: deduced — OCCT uncovered-class sweep
title: Curve approximation cannot meet the requested tolerance

description: A surface property query (tangent in U, V, or normal) at a specific UV parameter returns "undefined" because the surface partial derivatives vanish there (a pole, a degenerate corner). Bug-reporter language: "surface tangent undefined", "normal not computable", "pole on surface".
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject with status: return the undefined status to the caller; do not return a NaN or arbitrary unit vector. Must not silently accept.
notes: Common cause of NaN propagation when the caller assumes Defined. Bytes alone are insufficient to demonstrate this defect; needs sibling input fixture. Tagged provenance_tier: runtime-only. Synonyms: "surface tangent undefined", "normal not computable", "pole on surface returns LProp_Status.Undefined", "surface partial derivatives vanish at parameter", "U-tangent zero at sphere pole".
reproducer: An `SPHERICAL_SURFACE`; query the U-tangent at `v = π/2` (the pole). The U-tangent is zero.
sender: deduced — OCCT uncovered-class sweep
title: Surface tangent / normal undefined at a parameter (LProp_Status.Undefined)

description: A `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` declares `closed = .T.` and the first/last control points coincide, but the start and end tangents differ in sign; meaning the curve closes positionally but the tangent has a sharp reversal at the closure point (a cusp). Bug-reporter language: "closed B-spline has cusp", "closure tangent reversed", "C0 closure but no C1".
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject the smooth-closure claim; or open the curve at the cusp.
notes: Bug-reporter synonyms: "B-spline cusp at closure", "tangent jump at periodicity". Bytes alone are insufficient to demonstrate this defect; needs sibling input fixture. Tagged provenance_tier: runtime-only. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({heal, reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: catalog allows either heal or reject; OCC silently accepts the bad input without doing either. Synonyms: "B-spline cusp at closure", "tangent jump at periodicity", "closed B-spline has reversed end-tangent", "closure tangent reversed", "C0 closure but no C1 on closed BSpline".

Synonyms: "pcurve and 3D curve disagree by measurable distance", "edge representation gap", "pcurve drift", "CheckCurveOnSurface reports max distance exceeds tolerance", "pcurve diverges from 3D curve mid-edge".

sender: deduced — OCCT uncovered-class sweep

description: Some vendors encode reversed face orientation by emitting a `TOROIDAL_SURFACE` with negative `major_radius` (and/or negative `minor_radius`, or `minor > major`). Translators that take the radius value at face value compute the wrong geometry; translators that only check sign produce partially wrong shapes.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; interpret negative-radius torus as orientation flip; reject only when the absolute dimensions are physically impossible.
notes: Recurs across OCCT bug R001 (bug11857) and Mantis 0026376; maintainer-acknowledged orientation pathology in J010. **See also**: Gs036, Tsh035. Synonyms: "torus negative major radius", "TOROIDAL_SURFACE has negative MajorRadius", "SolidWorks negative-radius torus orientation marker", "Pro/E torus with sign-flipped radius", "torus radius negative encodes face flip".
reproducer: `TOROIDAL_SURFACE('',axis2,major:=10.0,minor:=-2.0)` referenced by an `ADVANCED_FACE`; or major_radius negative and SameSense interpreted by writer as flip.
sender: SolidWorks 2014 (and earlier), Pro/E Wildfire 5.0
title: TOROIDAL_SURFACE with negative MajorRadius (SolidWorks/Pro-E orientation marker)

description: A STEP `TOROIDAL_SURFACE` with minor radius equal to or exceeding major radius collapses the analytic torus into a self-intersecting "lemon" (minor > major, no central hole) or "apple" (minor = major, single pinch point at the centre). Receivers that assume `minor < major` produce overlarge bounding boxes, mis-handle seam insertion, or import a revolved-shape variant inverted.
expected_kernel_behavior: accept the analytic surface and treat its parameter range correctly for seam insertion and bbox computation, or reject as malformed (a kernel that requires `minor < major` should refuse rather than silently mis-bound).
notes: Synonyms: "torus minor radius greater than major (lemon shape)", "apple torus minor equals major", "self-intersecting torus no central hole", "lemon-shape torus collapses bounding box", "TOROIDAL_SURFACE with minor_radius >= major_radius".

title: Degenerate (lemon/apple) torus where minor_radius >= major_radius

description: Pcurves of an entire wire on a `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` (or other periodic surface) are shifted by an integer multiple of the surface period; for example a pcurve `LINE` whose start U coordinate is 12.566 (= 4π) on a radius-5 cylinder, more than 2π outside the canonical [0, 2π) seam range. The wire's UV image is correctly shaped but offset by 2π (or 4π) in U from where it should be. The whole contour is in the wrong period band; a re-alignment pass that does not produce a single coherent band leaves the wire un-meshable.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect the period-shift and re-base the wire's pcurves into a canonical / contiguous band. The post-condition is that all wire endpoints land in one period; otherwise the fix has not converged and a downstream mesher will reject the band.
notes: Synonyms: "pcurve U coordinate outside [0,2pi) seam range", "whole wire shifted by 4pi on cylinder", "wire pcurves in wrong period band", "pcurve U far outside canonical range", "cylinder pcurves all offset by full periods".

STEP-imported wires from poor curve discretization or grazing intersections. Healing passes can address each, but tolerance can balloon.

description: A `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS` whose control net has interior rows transposed or that traverse U in opposite directions, so the Jacobian flips sign within the parameter range; a folded / non-injective surface parametrisation. Typical shape: a degree 3×2 surface with a 4×3 control net and clamped knot multiplicities like (4,4) U and (3,3) V where two interior rows swap order. Common output of poorly-trimmed offset surfaces or Boolean-derived subdivision surfaces.

notes: **See also**: Gn025, Twi041. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts the folded BSpline surface and uses it without re-fit or diagnostic; kernel mishandling; the catalog above forbids silent acceptance. description: Mesh-to-BRep tools fit `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS` patches per triangle and stitch them; near sharp creases the patches' trim curves self-intersect or overlap. Typical shape: an `EDGE_LOOP` containing two diagonal `EDGE_CURVE`s — for example one running (0,0)→(10,10) and another (0,10)→(10,0) — which cross in UV at the centre and do not share endpoints, so the wire loop is two disjoint crossed diagonals. Output STEP loads but every later Boolean fails.

description: A face's outer or inner `EDGE_LOOP` has segments that cross each other in surface UV parameter space, even when 3D positions look fine; a bow-tie / self-crossing quadrilateral. Typical shape on a planar face: an `EDGE_LOOP` visiting four vertices where two diagonal `EDGE_CURVE`s ((0,0)→(10,10) and (10,0)→(0,10)) are interleaved with axial edges, producing a bow-tie in the face's UV plane. CADfix has a dedicated repair flow; failure in UV closure means the contour does not partition the plane (Jordan-curve violation).

description: Family of degenerate `ADVANCED_FACE` defects: spot (face collapses to a point, e.g. from Pro/E export rounding), strip (one parametric direction is near-zero), pin / sliver (extreme aspect ratio; for example a rectangle on a `PLANE` 100 units wide but only 1e-7 units tall, width many orders of magnitude smaller than length and within distance tolerance), and zero-area faces with collinear vertices. The underlying surface may be well-defined; the face's trim collapses the area.

description: A `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` (or surface) whose interior knot multiplicity equals the curve / surface order produces only C0 continuity at the join; a visible cusp / kink on an otherwise smooth curve. Typical shape: a degree-3 B-spline with 7 control points that peak at y=2 and immediately drop to y=-2 with an interior knot of multiplicity 3. Downstream CAD/CAM/CAE tools assume at least C1; after format conversion, neighbouring faces show G0/G1/G2 discontinuities at shared edges that were smooth in the source.
expected_kernel_behavior: split the curve / surface at the continuity drop, report the discontinuity as a quality warning, or refuse to claim a smoother continuity than the data supports.
notes: **See also**: Gn012. Synonyms: "B-spline curve C0 cusp at interior knot full multiplicity", "BSpline curve has visible kink", "knot multiplicity equals order produces C0 join", "G0/G1/G2 discontinuity at shared edge", "rational B-spline patches show tangent break".
reproducer: BSpline curve with internal knot of multiplicity equal to order producing a G0-only spot; or two adjacent faces emitted as `RATIONAL_B_SPLINE_SURFACE` patches whose tangent planes at the shared edge differ by more than the resolution tolerance.
title: `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` C0 cusp / kink at interior knot of full multiplicity (C1 expected)

cross_oracle_note: pure-Python Part-21 validator accepts (`accept`); OCCT crashes (`signal(11)`). The crash is on the kernel side; the file is spec-conformant Part-21.
description: When a 3D helix on a `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` is projected to the surface's parametric domain, the projection ought to yield an analytic 2D `LINE` segment — the helix unwraps cleanly onto a straight UV path. The actual translator either emits an empty `SURFACE_CURVE.associated_geometry` list (no pcurve at all on a non-trivial helical 3D `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` `EDGE_CURVE`), or emits a BSpline approximation with poor accuracy — losing the analytic-line representation and inflating tolerance budgets downstream.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect that the projected pcurve is collinear in UV and emit it as a 2D `LINE` pcurve, or reject as a translation-quality issue. A normal-distance closeness check is sufficient for the elementary-surface family.
notes: Cross-oracle: pure-Python Part-21 validator accepts (`accept`); OCCT crashes (`signal(11)`). The crash is on the kernel side; the file is spec-conformant Part-21.
reproducer: Edge whose 3D curve is helix on cylinder, no pcurve attached; reference from face on `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE`.
title: Helix on `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` mis-projected: pcurve missing or BSpline-approximated (analytic line lost)

description: An edge appears to be a seam edge — two faces meeting along what looks like a periodic-surface boundary — but the underlying surface is not actually periodic. Common signature: a `SURFACE_CURVE` with `master_representation` set to `.PCURVE_S1_AND_S2.` whose `associated_geometry` list contains the same `PCURVE` reference twice (e.g. `(#46, #46)`), claiming two pcurves on two surfaces but using one pcurve for both slots. Healing logic must distinguish true periodic seams from coincidental shared edges to avoid spuriously splitting or merging.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; verify periodicity flag and parametric distance before treating as seam; do not insert seam-degenerate edge.
notes: Synonyms: "pseudo-seam edge surface_curve has same pcurve twice", "looks like seam but surface not periodic", "PCURVE_S1_AND_S2 with duplicate pcurve reference", "seam-like edge on non-periodic BSpline surface", "false seam from coincidental shared edge".
reproducer: Two faces on same non-periodic BSpline surface that happen to share a long curve along U=const, where the U-range does not wrap.
sender: bm4_al_eye.stp #53710
title: Pseudo-seam edge: `SURFACE_CURVE` claims `PCURVE_S1_AND_S2` but lists same pcurve twice

description: A `TRIMMED_CURVE` or `EDGE_CURVE` claims `[first, last]` parameter range outside the curve's natural domain or with `last < first`. Translator and downstream evaluation must normalize.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; clamp/wrap parameter values into natural domain; if `last < first`, swap or wrap modulo period.
notes: **See also**: Gp007. Synonyms: "curve last parameter less than first", "trimmed_curve has reversed parameter range", "EDGE_CURVE first/last out of natural domain", "trim_2 less than trim_1 on circle", "PARAMETER_VALUE last smaller than first".
reproducer: `TRIMMED_CURVE` over a unit-radius `CIRCLE` with `trim_1=PARAMETER_VALUE(2π)`, `trim_2=PARAMETER_VALUE(0)` and `sense_agreement=.T.`.
title: Curve with last < first parameter range

description: After local edits (face translation, blend suppression, partial defeaturing) an edge's stored 3D curve no longer matches the geometric intersection of its two host faces. Edge survives as topology but its curve is stale, leading to large tolerances or visible cracks. TransMagic's "edges for the geometry do not match the surfaces that they are edges for"; also applies to translator output where edges deviate from cylinder/cone surfaces beyond tolerance.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; `rebuild-edge` re-intersects host faces and rebuilds vertices; reproject curve onto surface, or replace with surface intersection.
notes: **See also**: Tsh042, N024. Synonyms: "edge geometry inconsistent with adjacent faces actual intersection", "edges for the geometry do not match the surfaces", "stale edge curve after face translation", "edge deviates from cylinder beyond tolerance", "edge curve doesn lie on host surface intersection".
reproducer: `ADVANCED_FACE` on `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` of radius 10 mm whose `EDGE_CURVE` is a `LINE` 0.5 mm radially off the cylinder.
title: Edge geometry inconsistent with adjacent faces' actual intersection

description: A single `ADVANCED_FACE` ends up with two `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` entries — typically both referencing the same `EDGE_LOOP` — when the schema permits only one. Equivalently, the same outer wire is stored twice in the parametric domain so two pcurves trace the same contour. Common cause: rehosting a face onto a new supporting surface and reprojecting all 3D edges, without first deduplicating the wire that already describes the contour.
expected_kernel_behavior: a face-construction or rehosting pass must ensure exactly one outer wire per face; merge duplicates or reject. A multiply-traced outer wire produces ambiguous parametric trims.
notes: **See also**: Gp014. Synonyms: "ADVANCED_FACE has two FACE_OUTER_BOUND entries", "duplicated outer contour with overlapping pcurves", "face has two outer wires", "outer boundary stored twice", "rehosting face onto new surface duplicates wire".
reproducer: Take a trimmed face F1 on surface S1; build F2 on different surface S2 by reprojecting every edge of F1 onto S2 without first deduplicating the outer wire.
title: `ADVANCED_FACE` with two `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` entries (duplicated outer contour, overlapping pcurves)

description: A `SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION` whose basis curve is a `LINE` collinear with the extrusion direction is degenerate; it collapses to a line.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject this surface; emit warning; carry on with face omission.
notes: **See also**: Gs036. Synonyms: "surface of linear extrusion direction parallel to basis line", "extruded curve collapses to line", "SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION degenerate basis", "extrusion vector colinear with LINE basis", "surface collapses because direction matches basis line".
reproducer: `SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION` with basis `LINE` and `extrusion_axis` direction parallel to LINE.dir.
title: Surface-of-linear-extrusion whose direction is parallel to its basis line

description: Trim curves on `TOROIDAL_SURFACE` and NURBS surfaces produce sharp, chaotic border meshes while the interior of the patch is regular. Typical signature: a pcurve on a `TOROIDAL_SURFACE` is a `TRIMMED_CURVE` over an `ELLIPSE` in (u,v) parametric space. Tessellator falls back to coarse parametric sampling on the trim curve while the rest of the patch uses chordal-error sampling. Affects tube.stp and similar trimmed `TOROIDAL_SURFACE` / bicubic NURBS faces with `TRIMMED_CURVE` defined via `PCURVE`.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; apply chordal-error refinement to trim curves consistently with surface refinement.
notes: Synonyms: "trim curves on torus produce jagged tessellation borders", "TRIMMED_CURVE on ELLIPSE pcurve", "border mesh chaotic on TOROIDAL_SURFACE", "tessellator falls back to coarse parametric sampling on trim", "tube.stp jagged trim curve mesh".
reproducer: STEP `TOROIDAL_SURFACE` or bicubic NURBS face plus `TRIMMED_CURVE` defined via `PCURVE`; tessellate with default size factor.
title: Trim curves on `TOROIDAL_SURFACE` / NURBS produce jagged tessellation borders (`TRIMMED_CURVE` on `ELLIPSE` pcurve)

description: Family of single-face topology defects, all characterised by an `EDGE_LOOP` that visits the same `VERTEX_POINT` more than once: pinched face self-touches at a single vertex visited twice by its outer wire (figure-eight); vertex-split face has a boundary vertex visited three times so the loop traces two adjoined triangles sharing a common centre vertex (e.g. six edges all meeting at a centre point (5,5,0)); twisted face has a Möbius-cell-like parametrisation (the parametric region maps to a non-orientable patch); a periodic face represented by a single belt wire collapses to a degenerate pole.
expected_kernel_behavior: split the pinched face at the shared vertex into two manifold faces; re-fit a twisted face's parametrisation if recoverable; insert degenerate edges at poles for the belt-wire-on-periodic case; or reject as malformed when the topology cannot be recovered.
notes: **See also**: Gn025, Tfa010, Twi041. Synonyms: "twisted face EDGE_LOOP revisits shared vertex", "Mobius-cell face pathology", "pinched face self-touches at one vertex", "vertex-split face boundary visits vertex three times", "single vertex visited multiple times by outer wire".
reproducer: Build a planar face whose outer wire visits a shared vertex twice (figure-eight); export.
title: Twisted / pinched / vertex-split face: `EDGE_LOOP` revisits a shared vertex (Möbius-cell pathology)

description: `COMPOSITE_CURVE_SEGMENT.parent_curve` is null (`$`). Translator must drop the null segment with a warning rather than dereferencing `$` as a curve.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; drop the null segment with a warning; never crash.
notes: **See also**: Ad085, Gs054, Gs055. Synonyms: "composite curve segment with null parent_curve", "COMPOSITE_CURVE_SEGMENT.parent_curve is dollar-sign", "null parent in composite curve segment", "dropping null segment with warning", "parent_curve null reference in composite".
reproducer: `COMPOSITE_CURVE_SEGMENT(.CONTINUOUS.,.T.,$)` referenced by a `COMPOSITE_CURVE`.
title: Composite curve segment with null `parent_curve`

description: `DIRECTION` with all-zero direction_ratios (S020); `VECTOR` with zero magnitude (Q057); `axis2_placement_3d` whose `axis` and `ref_direction` are colinear so an orthonormal frame cannot be constructed (S021); `PLANE` whose ref direction is parallel to its normal (W020, degenerate plane causes import crashes).
expected_kernel_behavior: reject the surface/placement; healers may project ref_direction onto plane normal or substitute global Z/X; never crash.
notes: **See also**: Gn010, Gs001, Gs032. Synonyms: "negative-radius zero-magnitude direction or vector", "DIRECTION with all-zero direction_ratios", "zero-magnitude VECTOR", "axis and ref_direction colinear cannot form orthonormal frame", "PLANE ref direction parallel to normal".
reproducer: `DIRECTION('',(0.,0.,0.))` referenced by `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D`; or axis `(0,0,1)` and ref_direction `(0,0,1)`.
title: Negative-radius / zero-magnitude direction or vector

description: A face's supporting surface is built as a finite offset of a surface-of-linear-extrusion (an extruded curve, then offset by a constant distance along its normal). Evaluating an iso-curve (a row of constant U or V) on that composite surface throws an exception in some receivers, because the iso-evaluation logic does not descend through the offset/extrusion wrappers down to the basis curve.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: iso-curve evaluation must work through composite surface wrappers, falling through to the basis curve when the offset is finite. Throwing on legitimate composite surface chains is not acceptable; must not crash or reject valid input.
notes: Validation observed: silent-empty rather than the cited UIso/VIso exception. The exception path is downstream of an extra analysis pass that the validate2 transfer pipeline does not invoke at fixture scale; the kernel-mishandling-by-silent-acceptance still demonstrates the defect class. **See also**: Gn021. Synonyms: "offset of surface-of-linear-extrusion fails iso-curve evaluation", "OFFSET_SURFACE over SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION throws on iso eval", "iso evaluation can not descend through offset wrappers", "composite surface chain fails UIso", "offset extrusion surface evaluation fails".
occ_behavior_note: silent-empty rather than the cited UIso/VIso exception. The exception path is downstream of an extra analysis pass that the validate2 transfer pipeline does not invoke at fixture scale; the kernel-mishandling-by-silent-acceptance still demonstrates the defect class.
reproducer: STEP file with composite surface chain `OFFSET_SURFACE → SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION`; trigger UIso evaluation downstream.
title: Offset of a surface-of-linear-extrusion fails iso-curve evaluation

description: 2D points along a projected pcurve sometimes have a huge jump (>0.95 of UV range) on BSpline surface when 3D points are close; surface near-periodicity not recognized. Self-touching closed BSpline surface where 2D pcurve crosses near the wrap-around boundary.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal — detect jump; insert additional point; adjust by inferred period.
notes: **See also**: Gn033. Synonyms: "pcurve U/V parameter has large jump near periodic boundary on BSpline", "huge jump in pcurve at near-period seam", "near-periodicity not recognized produces UV spike", "self-touching BSpline surface pcurve straddles wraparound", "2D pcurve crosses near-period boundary uncaught".
reproducer: Self-touching BSpline surface with pcurve crossing the near-period; sample pcurve at uniform parameter and observe UV jump > 0.95 of period.
title: Pcurve U/V parameter has large jump near periodic boundary on BSpline

description: Specific feature kinds that exist in source CAD vanish after STEP export — typically because writer's BRep decomposition fails on multi-blend intersections, helical sweeps, or variable-radius blends and silently emits an incomplete shell (zero-volume, missing faces, or only end caps surviving). Common signature: a `SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL` carries only one face — a `SPHERICAL_SURFACE` cap whose `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` is a degenerate `VERTEX_LOOP` at a single equator vertex (one point covers the whole sphere) — with the side walls and other caps missing.
expected_kernel_behavior: accept what is present; rely on validation properties (volume, area, centroid checksums) to detect loss; never silently emit zero-volume body.
notes: **See also**: Tsh004, Tsh006. **OCC behavior**: silently imports the cap-only shell as a zero-volume body without surfacing a checksum-mismatch diagnostic; kernel mishandling; the catalog above forbids silent zero-volume acceptance. Synonyms: "helical sweep silently emitted as incomplete shell", "variable-radius blend missing from STEP", "cap-only face on SPHERICAL_SURFACE with VERTEX_LOOP", "writer drops side walls of helix sweep", "feature kind vanishes after STEP export".
reproducer: Round-trip a model containing variable-radius blend or helix-on-circle sweep through a STEP writer that doesn't support full G2 NURBS reconstruction of the blend.
sender: cadquery hemisphere+cylindrical-cut, helix sweep build123d, Workplane revolve+offset
title: Helical sweep / variable-radius blend silently emitted as incomplete shell (cap-only face on `SPHERICAL_SURFACE` with `VERTEX_LOOP` bound)

description: Curves with very high local curvature (often artifacts of NURBS knot insertion or approximation during translation) that downstream tools — meshers especially — over-resolve or fail to mesh. `B_SPLINE_CURVE` with multi-knots near full-degree multiplicity that produce a near-cusp; `RATIONAL_B_SPLINE_CURVE` with control-point weight ratio above ~1e3.
expected_kernel_behavior: accept geometrically; downstream meshers detect and refuse / heal; archive-stable only if validation properties still match.
notes: **See also**: Gn008. Synonyms: "high-curvature curve cusp from NURBS knot insertion", "B-spline curve near-cusp from full-degree multi-knot", "RATIONAL_B_SPLINE_CURVE weight ratio above 1000", "mesher over-resolves cusp on NURBS curve", "BSpline curve high local curvature artifact".
reproducer: `B_SPLINE_CURVE` with multi-knot near degree multiplicity producing a cusp; reference from `EDGE_CURVE`.
title: High-curvature curve / cusp from NURBS knot insertion

description: A RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_SURFACE is parameterised as an MxN grid of SURFACE_PATCH children. The U parameter spans across all M patches; V across all N. The spec permits non-uniform parameter intervals (one patch occupies U=0.0.7, the next U=0.7.1.0). Many receivers assume uniform spacing and either pass through with the wrong global parameterisation or trip an internal assertion.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: respect each patch's individual parameter interval; if the kernel internally re-parameterises to uniform, it must record the original mapping so isoparametric queries on the composite return the correct point.
notes: Distinct from Gp019 (pcurve-on-RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_SURFACE); this entry is about parameter-grid uniformity, independent of bounding wire. Synonyms: "RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_SURFACE non-uniform patch grid", "composite surface patches with unequal U intervals", "MxN composite surface assumes uniform parameter spacing", "patch occupies non-uniform U interval", "isoparametric query on composite surface returns wrong point".
reproducer: 2x1 RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_SURFACE whose left patch occupies U=[0.0, 0.3] and right patch U=[0.3, 1.0] (non-uniform).
title: `RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_SURFACE` with non-uniform patch grid

description: A CURVE_BOUNDED_SURFACE is a (basis surface, set of boundary curves) where boundary curves are pcurves on the basis. The spec requires the boundary to be a non-self-intersecting loop in parameter space. Producers occasionally emit a boundary whose two segments cross at an interior point (figure-eight / bowtie), yielding two regions where the trim "inside" is ambiguous.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect the self-intersection and either reject as malformed or split the boundary into simple loops with explicit inside/outside designation.
notes: **See also**: Twi-family wire self-intersection entries. Synonyms: "CURVE_BOUNDED_SURFACE bowtie boundary", "self-intersecting boundary on curve-bounded surface", "boundary curves cross in parameter space", "trim inside ambiguous due to figure-eight boundary", "non-simple loop in CURVE_BOUNDED_SURFACE".
reproducer: CURVE_BOUNDED_SURFACE whose basis is a plane and whose boundary is a four-segment COMPOSITE_CURVE forming a self-intersecting bowtie (corners (0,0),(1,1),(1,0),(0,1) connected in that order).
title: `CURVE_BOUNDED_SURFACE` with self-intersecting (bowtie) boundary

description: An OFFSET_CURVE_3D with ref_distance equal to the local radius of curvature creates a cusp at every point of that curvature. The mathematical offset is undefined at such points (the offset point coincides with the curve's center of curvature; 0/0 arises in the offset's first derivative). For a circular basis of radius R, an offset of -R collapses the entire offset to the center.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect collapse / cusp at construction time and either reject the offset as degenerate or treat the result as a point set rather than a curve.
notes: **See also**: Gs048. Synonyms: "OFFSET_CURVE_3D ref_distance equal to radius of curvature creates collapse", "circle offset by negative radius collapses to centre", "offset curve cusp at every point", "0/0 in offset curve first derivative", "offset distance equals local radius produces degeneracy".
reproducer: CIRCLE radius 5.0; OFFSET_CURVE_3D over it with ref_distance = -5.0 → entire curve collapses to center point.
title: `OFFSET_CURVE_3D` with `ref_distance` equal to the basis curve's radius of curvature (collapse)

description: An INTERSECTION_CURVE entity holds the curve of intersection between two surfaces. The spec models the intersection as a single CURVE_ON_SURFACE pair, but in general two surfaces (e.g. a plane and a torus, or two non-coaxial cylinders) intersect along *multiple disjoint branches*. A single INTERSECTION_CURVE entity cannot faithfully represent this; the producer chose one branch arbitrarily, silently dropping the others.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect that the producer's basis curve does not cover the full surface intersection and warn; or reject INTERSECTION_CURVE if the kernel expects a single branch and detect-time analysis disagrees.
notes: **See also**: Gp- pcurve entries. Synonyms: "INTERSECTION_CURVE represents only one branch", "torus-plane intersection has two circles only one stored", "multiple disjoint intersection branches dropped", "single CURVE_ON_SURFACE pair cannot represent multi-branch intersection", "producer chose one branch silently dropping others".
reproducer: TOROIDAL_SURFACE major=10, minor=3; PLANE z=0. The intersection is two concentric circles at radius 7 and 13. The fixture's INTERSECTION_CURVE represents only the outer branch (r=13).
title: `INTERSECTION_CURVE` between two surfaces with multiple disjoint intersection branches, only one represented

description: A SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION sweeps a basis curve about an axis. If the axis crosses the basis curve at an interior point, one side of the curve is swept "inward" while the other is swept "outward", producing a self-intersecting surface that folds through itself near the axis. Distinct from existing entries about co-axial / parallel sweeps; this is the *crossing* pathological case.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect axis-crosses-basis at construction; reject or split the basis at the crossing into two non-crossing sub-curves and revolve each separately.
notes: **See also**: Gn015, Gn016. Synonyms: "SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION axis crosses basis curve at interior point", "basis curve crosses revolution axis", "self-intersecting surface from axis-crossing revolution", "revolution axis through interior of basis line", "surface folds through itself near axis".
reproducer: basis LINE from x=-2 to x=+2 along y=0,z=0; revolution axis = Y-axis at origin. The line crosses the axis at (0,0,0) interior to the basis parameter range.
title: `SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION` whose revolution axis crosses the basis curve at an interior point

description: A SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION sweeps a basis curve along a vector (DIRECTION + magnitude). If the vector magnitude is 0.0, the surface degenerates to the basis curve. The DIRECTION is technically still well-formed (any unit vector) but the VECTOR carries magnitude 0. Distinct from Gs032's parallel-collinear case: there the direction is non-zero but parallel to the basis. Here the magnitude itself is zero.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect zero-magnitude vectors and reject the surface as degenerate (it has no area).
notes: **See also**: Gs032, Gs037. Synonyms: "SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION zero-magnitude vector", "extrusion VECTOR magnitude 0", "extrusion surface degenerates to basis curve", "zero-length extrusion produces no area", "magnitude 0 in VECTOR for extrusion".
reproducer: SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION over a basis LINE with extrusion VECTOR of magnitude 0.0.
title: `SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION` with zero-magnitude extrusion vector

description: AP242 introduces BLENDED_EDGE_SURFACE to represent an edge fillet between two adjacent faces. The blend's radius (or radius profile) is one of the entity's defining attributes. A producer that supports variable-radius fillets but exports through a constant-radius schema may emit two BLENDED_EDGE_SURFACE instances for adjacent edges with mismatched radii at their shared vertex; the receiver sees a 0-thickness gap where they meet.
expected_kernel_behavior: reconcile the radii by transitioning between them through a third spherical / variable-radius patch, or reject as inconsistent.
notes: First entry exercising AP242 BLENDED_EDGE_SURFACE. Synonyms: "BLENDED_EDGE_SURFACE mismatched fillet radii at shared vertex", "two AP242 fillets meet with different radii", "0-thickness gap where blends meet", "blend A radius 1 blend B radius 2 conflict", "constant-radius export of variable-radius fillet creates discontinuity".
reproducer: two CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE blends meeting at the origin: blend A radius 1.0, blend B radius 2.0. At the shared vertex the two fillet surfaces cannot meet smoothly.
title: `BLENDED_EDGE_SURFACE` with mismatched fillet radii at a shared vertex

description: ISO 10303-42 OFFSET_CURVE_2D carries ref_distance (a signed real where sign determines side). When a producer chains OFFSET_CURVE_2D segments around a composite curve and switches sign mid-chain (perhaps to "fix" inside/outside on a concave region), the resulting offset is non-continuous: successive segments do not meet at a shared point.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect the C0 discontinuity at the chain junction and either reject or insert a connecting segment (line, arc) bridging the gap.
notes: **See also**: Gs043. Synonyms: "OFFSET_CURVE_2D ref_distance sign flips mid composite chain", "C0 discontinuity at composite curve junction from offset sign change", "offset side switches mid-chain", "successive offset segments don meet", "ref_distance +1 then -1 on adjacent segments".
reproducer: COMPOSITE_CURVE of two POLYLINE segments wrapped in OFFSET_CURVE_2D each, with `ref_distance` = +1.0 on the first and `-1.0` on the second.
title: `OFFSET_CURVE_2D` with sign of `ref_distance` flipping mid composite-curve chain

description: A B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS has a knot in U (or V) whose multiplicity equals the degree, creating a C0 isoparametric line. Faces on this surface present a kink across the entire isoline; meshing/Boolean tools that assume C1+ produce wrong tangent normals. Some receivers split such surfaces at the C0 line into two sub-surfaces with single-piece continuity.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect C0 isoparametric lines and either split the surface (and propagate splits to bound faces and edges) or report the discontinuity. Splitting must keep edge/wire/face topology consistent.
notes: Surface-side analogue of Gp033. Synonyms: "B-spline surface C0 isoparametric line triggers split", "knot multiplicity equals degree creates C0 isoline", "BSpline surface kink across entire isoline", "split surface at C0 isoline propagates to face/edge topology", "ShapeUpgrade_SplitSurface needed for C0 isoparametric line".
reproducer: A face on a degree-2 B-spline surface whose U knot vector is `(0,0,0, 0.5,0.5,0.5, 1,1,1)`; the face itself is a simple square.
title: B-spline surface has C0 isoparametric line that triggers split-on-import

description: A `TOROIDAL_SURFACE` is emitted with `major_radius` and `minor_radius` swapped (a producer convention from a legacy tool that stored them in opposite order). Reader interprets the values literally, producing a torus with reversed proportions; what should be a thin donut becomes an apple/lemon (minor > major, no central hole).
expected_kernel_behavior: detect inverted-radius case (minor ≥ major is the lemon/apple geometry); flag as suspicious for healers; reject if strict.
notes: **See also**: Gs002. Synonyms: "toroidal surface major/minor radii swapped", "torus stored with reversed radius proportions", "thin donut becomes apple/lemon from swapped radii", "TOROIDAL_SURFACE radius order inverted", "producer wrote major and minor radius in wrong order".
reproducer: `TOROIDAL_SURFACE('',#axis, 0.5, 5.0)` where the intended torus has `major_radius=5.0` and `minor_radius=0.5`. Producer emitted the values reversed.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0032556 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Toroidal surface stored incorrectly: major / minor swapped

description: A sphere is cut by a cylinder; the cut introduces a new edge that crosses the sphere's natural seam. Original sphere had one seam; after the cut, the result has two seams (original + cut), and the pcurves of the second seam are emitted referencing the wrong half of the sphere's parameter domain.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: each seam edge must reference its own parameter domain; never share pcurves across distinct seams.
notes: **See also**: Twi071. Synonyms: "sphere/cylinder cut produces wrong pcurves on second seam", "two seams after Boolean cut have shared pcurve domains", "second seam references wrong half of sphere parameter domain", "Boolean cut introduces new seam with bad pcurves", "cut-through-sphere creates second seam with U=pi issue".
reproducer: Boolean cut: sphere of radius 5 at origin, by cylinder of radius 2 along Z. Result has two seam-like edges; second seam's pcurves reference U=π instead of U=0.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0022535 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Sphere/cylinder cut produces wrong pcurves on second seam

description: A surface of revolution whose basis curve is itself an `OFFSET_CURVE_3D` round-trips through STEP/IGES; the offset relationship is lost; the receiver sees a freshly-evaluated B-spline approximation of the offset curve rather than the original "offset by 0.1 of curve X" representation. Subsequent edits (changing the original X) no longer propagate.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: offset relationships are preserved through export when the receiver schema supports them; AP242 supports offset-based curves. Must not silently drop offset on export.

description: A `SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION` references an `ELLIPSE` as its swept curve and a vertical axis that passes through the ellipse's centre. The resulting analytic surface is degenerate at both poles where the generatrix meets the axis (zero-radius circles). On import, OCCT cannot recover a usable parametric surface; the face appears empty, geometry is dropped silently, or a heal pass replaces the analytic with a high-cost B-spline approximation. Writers should refuse to emit this construction and instead emit two half-spheres / a torus depending on whether the axis is in-plane.
expected_kernel_behavior: warn-and-proceed — detect axis-through-centre construction, emit `W_DEGENERATE_REVOLUTION_AXIS`, and either heal to canonical analytic (sphere / torus) or fall back to B-spline; never silently drop the face.
notes: **See also**: Gs049, A083. Synonyms: "STEP error for ellipse revol shape", "ellipse revolved around its own centre", "SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION poles", "degenerate ellipse-of-revolution surface".
reproducer: `#1=ELLIPSE('',#2,1.0,0.5);` with `#2` an axis placement at the origin; `#10=SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION('',#11,#1);` with `#11` an axis through the ellipse centre. Importer should warn or normalize.
sender: Modellers that emit `SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION` whose generatrix is an `ELLIPSE` and whose axis passes through the ellipse centre.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP error for ellipse revol shape", "revolution of ellipse fails on import", "degenerate surface from ellipse-of-revolution". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)

description: `RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_SURFACE` describes a piecewise-Bezier or piecewise-NURBS quilt with explicit per-patch transition codes. step-g's `Load` parses the segments grid (a `LIST_OF_LIST_OF_PATCHES`) into in-memory SurfacePatch objects, so the entity is recognised — but `LoadONBrep` is a stub that prints `"not implemented"` and returns false. Faces referencing the quilt are dropped without further diagnostic. Algebraically the entity could be promoted to a single `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS` at multiplicity-(degree+1) internal knots, so the drop is doubly avoidable. Distinct from Gs041 (non-uniform patch grid — structural defect) and Tfa036 (face-on-quilt boundary crossing seams): this is the wholesale unimplemented dispatch.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; promote the patch grid to a single `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS` (multiplicity = degree+1 at the internal patch boundaries) and feed the result to the existing BSpline importer; emit `W_RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_PROMOTED` so users know the conversion happened.
notes: **See also**: Gs058, Gs041, Tfa036, Gn018. Synonyms: "RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_SURFACE LoadONBrep stub", "step-g composite quilt unimplemented", "patch quilt face dropped", "promote to NURBS not done", "BRL-CAD step-g RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_SURFACE skipped".
reproducer: `#300=RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_SURFACE('quilt',((#101,#201)));` where `#101` and `#201` are SURFACE_PATCH wrappers around BEZIER patches. step-g LoadONBrep stub drops the face that references `#300`.
sender: Producers that emit a quilt of analytically-defined patches (typical of CATIA's "Surface" workbench output and of legacy AP203 files from CAD systems whose internal representation is patch-based rather than NURBS-based).
sources: BRL-CAD `src/conv/step/step-g/RectangularCompositeSurface.cpp` `Load` parses the segments grid into SurfacePatch objects, but `LoadONBrep` is a stub printing `"::LoadONBrep(..) not implemented for <entity>"`
bug-reporter language: "RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_SURFACE drops face on import", "step-g composite quilt unsupported", "patchwork quilt silently lost".
title: `RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_SURFACE` LoadONBrep stub (BRL-CAD step-g)

category: §12.2c surface / curve degeneracies (sub-class: patch continuity metadata lost)
description: Even when the consumer **does** intend to promote a `RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_SURFACE` (Gs057) to a single B-spline, the patch-by-patch continuity metadata (`u_transition` / `v_transition` and the per-patch `u_sense` / `v_sense` direction flags) carries information the receiver needs to perform that promotion correctly: a `CONT_SAME_GRADIENT_SAME_CURVATURE` boundary must be promoted with multiplicity = degree-2 knot at the patch boundary; a `DISCONTINUOUS` boundary must be promoted with multiplicity = degree+1. step-g parses both attributes into the in-memory model and then never reads them back; the receiver re-evaluates continuity numerically, which both costs CPU and may produce a kink the producer's continuity hint would have prevented.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; every importer that consumes a `SURFACE_PATCH` (whether via `RECTANGULAR_COMPOSITE_SURFACE` or directly) must convert the parsed `transition_code` into the appropriate knot multiplicity at the patch boundary; emit `W_PATCH_TRANSITION_HONORED` recording which transition was applied.
notes: **See also**: Gs057, Gn017. Synonyms: "SURFACE_PATCH transition_code dropped", "step-g ignores patch continuity metadata", "CONT_SAME_GRADIENT_SAME_CURVATURE not applied", "u_sense / v_sense booleans lost", "patch-boundary C2 hint discarded by importer".
reproducer: `#101=SURFACE_PATCH(#100, .CONT_SAME_GRADIENT_SAME_CURVATURE., .CONT_SAME_GRADIENT_SAME_CURVATURE., .T., .F.);`. step-g loads the value but applies it nowhere.
sender: Producers that compose a quilt of patches with explicit continuity guarantees — CATIA Class A surface tools, ICEM Surf, and legacy aero/automotive translators all emit `CONT_SAME_GRADIENT_SAME_CURVATURE` to declare C2 continuity at patch boundaries.
sources: BRL-CAD `src/conv/step/step-g/SurfacePatch.cpp` `Load` reads `u_transition`, `v_transition` (Transition_code enum: `DISCONTINUOUS` / `CONTINUOUS` / `CONT_SAME_GRADIENT` / `CONT_SAME_GRADIENT_SAME_CURVATURE`) and `u_sense` / `v_sense` BOOLEANs into class members
`LoadONBrep` is a stub printing `"not implemented"` and returning false
bug-reporter language: "SURFACE_PATCH transition_code dropped on import", "C2 continuity hint lost by step-g", "u_sense / v_sense booleans not applied".
title: `SURFACE_PATCH` `transition_code` / `u_sense` / `v_sense` parsed but ignored (BRL-CAD step-g)

description: A shell's per-face `same_sense` flags and edge orientations form a non-orientable assembly: there is no choice of "outward" that propagates consistently around the shell's edge graph. A Möbius-strip-like topology emerges; when the kernel walks face-to-face across shared edges, the sense flips after a closed loop. Common fixture pattern: an OPEN_SHELL whose ADVANCED_FACEs all sit on the same PLANE while one face's same_sense flag is flipped relative to its neighbour, producing a non-orientable face arrangement. Bug-reporter language: "Möbius shell", "kernel says shape is non-orientable", "cannot determine inside vs outside", "flipped face same_sense breaks orientation".
expected_kernel_behavior: Detect non-orientability via parity-walk of orientation flags; reject the shape, or split the shell into orientable pieces and warn.
notes: Distinct from Tsh008 (mis-oriented but orientable). The defect here is intrinsic, not an importer mistake. Synonyms: "Möbius shell", "kernel says shape is non-orientable", "cannot determine inside vs outside", "flipped face same_sense breaks orientation", "no consistent normal direction possible".
reproducer: An OPEN_SHELL of three rectangular `ADVANCED_FACE` entries (often all on the same PLANE) connected end-to-end into a closed loop. The third face's `same_sense=.F.` is set so that, when traversed in the closed loop, the orientation reverses.
sender: deduced — OCCT uncovered-class sweep
title: Shell whose orientation flags admit no globally consistent normal (Möbius-like)

Or the inverse: an edge is tagged smooth but the two surfaces meet at an angle. Bug-reporter language: "edge continuity wrong", "smooth edge marked sharp", "fillet edge marked as crease", "duplicate cylinders should share one surface".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: recompute regularity from face normals; correct the tag.
notes: Affects downstream meshing and shading. Provenance tier: runtime-only; bytes alone cannot demonstrate this defect; STEP edge entities have no continuity-tag attribute, so the "C0 vs G1" mistagging exists only as kernel-internal regularity state populated during the regularity-encoding pass. The static fixture encodes only the geometric trigger (two cylinders meeting tangentially). A behavioral test against the regularity-encoder is the appropriate venue. Synonyms: "edge continuity wrong", "smooth edge marked sharp", "fillet edge marked as crease", "duplicate cylinders should share one surface", "regularity tag disagrees with measured smoothness".
reproducer: Two ADVANCED_FACEs on two CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE entities that are duplicates (same axis, same radius) sharing a tangent edge, with the edge marked `C0` in the source model. (In STEP this is implicit in face tessellation tools but not in the entity graph; the reproducer is geometric — surfaces meet smoothly.)

title: Two ADVANCED_FACEs on duplicate CYLINDRICAL_SURFACEs share a smooth (G1) edge mis-tagged as a sharp crease
