expected_kernel_behavior: writer validates `EDGE_LOOP` closure before emission; receivers should sew open boundaries when a missing edge is reconstructable from adjacent geometry, or warn.
notes: **See also**: P015. Synonyms: "lettering bottoms not closed", "text feature pocket floor missing", "embossed text exports as non-solid", "EDGE_LOOP one edge short on STEP export".
reproducer: STEP solid with 3 small rectangular pocket-floors where one pocket-floor face's `EDGE_LOOP` has 3 edges instead of the required 4 — a missing edge produces an open-bound floor.
sender: FreeCAD with Draft-text or Sketcher-derived text features applied as Pad/Pocket on a surface.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP Export does not contain all the geometry", "Gear16 looks OK in FreeCAD and passes geometry check but exports to a non-solid", "all the bottoms of the lettering is not closed".
title: Lettering bottoms not closed in exported STEP (text-on-surface non-solid result)

category: §12.3c faces / sewing / free bounds (sub-class: ambiguous boundary semantics)
description: The `CURVE_BOUNDED_SURFACE.implicit_outer` BOOLEAN slot has two valid states under the schema (`.T.` — natural surface boundary is implicitly the outer loop; `.F.` — every boundary in the `boundaries` list is explicit). step-g's `getBooleanAttribute` accepts a third state, `BUnset`, which leaves the receiver unable to choose between the two valid interpretations. Because `LoadONBrep` is a stub anyway the immediate symptom is silent face-drop; but even when LoadONBrep is implemented, the absence of a default for `.U.` means the importer has no defined behaviour. The schema-strict reading is to reject; a forgiving reader could heal by computing whether the listed boundaries cover the surface domain and inferring `implicit_outer` automatically.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject — emit `E_AMBIGUOUS_IMPLICIT_OUTER` and refuse the entity; alternatively heal by inspecting whether the listed boundaries cover the surface's natural domain and inferring the flag, with `W_INFERRED_IMPLICIT_OUTER` diagnostic.
notes: **See also**: Tfa038, Twi091, Gs042. Synonyms: "CURVE_BOUNDED_SURFACE implicit_outer unset", "STEP face implicit_outer .U. silently dropped", "step-g BUnset boolean defaults to drop", "ambiguous outer-boundary semantics", "BOOLEAN attribute .U. accepted but undefined".
reproducer: `#80=CURVE_BOUNDED_SURFACE('cbs_face', #14, (#70), .U.);`. step-g loads `implicit_outer = BUnset` and the LoadONBrep stub drops the face.
sender: Hand-edited fixtures and a small population of fuzzed AP203 files where the producer left `implicit_outer` unspecified; also some early Inventor STEP exports that emitted `.U.` literal rather than `.T.`/`.F.`.
sources: `LoadONBrep` is a stub printing `"not implemented for <entity>"`
bug-reporter language: "CURVE_BOUNDED_SURFACE implicit_outer unset", "STEP face with unknown implicit_outer flag dropped", "step-g cannot decide outer-boundary handling".
title: `CURVE_BOUNDED_SURFACE.implicit_outer = .U.` (unset BOOLEAN) leaves boundary semantics ambiguous (BRL-CAD step-g)

description: Conical face with apex below wire bounds. When apex V parameter sits outside wire V-range and isUDecrease=false, apex curve direction and conditional wire reversal produce inconsistent orientation. Wire reversal triggered at line 3204 but apex curve construction does not account for actual wire topology.
expected_kernel_behavior: OCCT healing should detect apex positioning, build correct downward apex curve, and reverse wire orientation consistently. Failure: wire reversal applied but apex curve direction remains inconsistent.
reproducer: Cone geometry with semi-angle ~0.52 rad, apex at V=-1; wire wrapping cone at V=1..3 with non-decreasing U. FixPeriodicDegenerated applies apex curve construction and conditionally reverses wire when apex below wire lower bound.
title: ShapeFix_Face.FixPeriodicDegenerated apex-curve direction

description: Pin-face (spot face) with vertices clustered near origin. Wire-existence check (isWir=true) insufficient to guarantee all face edges belong to wire topology. Tolerance-drift on vertex replacement: computed tolerance may leave original vertices outside enclosing sphere when tolerance is not scaled consistently.
expected_kernel_behavior: Kernel should validate wire existence exhaustively (all edges in face belong to wire), then compute vertex mean with tolerance scaling that encloses all originals. Failure: tolerance drift allows vertices outside enclosing ball.
reproducer: Spot face on plane with 3 vertices clustered at ~0.001 unit radius from origin; one vertex at tol=0.001, another at tol=0.0001. Mean position computed without tolerance weighting; tolerance closure fails to enclose all vertices.
title: ShapeFix_FixSmallFace.ReplaceVerticesInCaseOfSpot coherence

description: Strip-face shared-edge construction with asymmetric endpoint-pair merging. V1 merged to V3 (dev < tol), but V2 not merged to V4 (dev > tol), creating degenerate edge with one matched vertex and one unmatched. Asymmetry arises from sequential V1 vs V3 check followed by independent V2 vs V4 check.
expected_kernel_behavior: Kernel should either merge both endpoint pairs or neither. Asymmetric merging produces degenerate shared edge that breaks strip-face topology.
reproducer: Two edges E1=(V1,V2) and E2=(V3,V4) where dev(V1,V3)=0.00005 (<tol), but dev(V2,V4)=1.5 (>>tol). V1 merged to V3; V2 remains unmerged; shared edge created with (V3, V4) semantics violated.
title: ShapeFix_FixSmallFace.ComputeSharedEdgeForStripFace asymmetry

description: Face with two identical edges [E, E] at FORWARD orientation in single 2-edge wire. Orientation mismatch detection (line 2876) fails to recognize that both edges are identical at same orientation, allowing coincident-edge pattern to pass unmerged.
expected_kernel_behavior: When E1==E2 and both at FORWARD, wires should be merged into single wire. Failure: orientation sensitivity rejects merge even though orientations match.
reproducer: Single PLANE face with 2-edge wire containing identical edge E at FORWARD orientation twice. Pattern should trigger merge but orientation check at 2876 does not correctly identify matching orientation.
title: ShapeFix_Face.FixWiresTwoCoincEdges orientation detection

description: MakeFacesOnPatch receives single non-WIRE loop (e.g., VERTEX). Fast-path check at line 2985 (loops.Length==1 && !WIRE) returns early, promoting residual loop as face without proper topology resolution. Fallback resolution ambiguous when loop type is not WIRE.
expected_kernel_behavior: Kernel should distinguish between single-WIRE (valid, construct face) and single-non-WIRE (error, abort or fallback with diagnostic). Failure: non-WIRE loop bypass leads to unresolved topology.
reproducer: Patch with single degenerate loop; single-edge WIRE loop passed through. Type-checking shortcut skips root-finding; residual loop promoted without face construction.
title: ShapeFix_ComposeShell.MakeFacesOnPatch fallback resolution

cross_oracle_note: OCCT caches singularity state; re-computation may fail on modified surfaces. Synonyms: "toroidal pinch-point undetected", "torus minor radius degeneracy", "singularity cache miss on periodic surface".
description: A toroidal face whose minor radius approaches zero creates a "pinch" singularity where opposite surface points coincide. The singularity detector must recognize this degenerate locus; incomplete classification allows pinched geometries to pass validation unchecked, producing unpredictable healing outcomes downstream.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal: classify pinch as boundary singularity and mark for extra scrutiny; reject: if pinch radius falls below configured tolerance
notes: Cross-oracle: OCCT caches singularity state; re-computation may fail on modified surfaces. Synonyms: "toroidal pinch-point undetected", "torus minor radius degeneracy", "singularity cache miss on periodic surface".
title: ShapeAnalysis_Surface.ComputeSingularities toroidal-pinch

description: A B-spline surface marked periodic in U direction must close geometrically: start and end isoparametric curves coincide. The closure checker caches results but may skip revalidation when the surface is trimmed or modified. A face on a geometrically open but periodically flagged B-spline exhibits incorrect winding classification if the closure test is bypassed.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal: validate closure consistency; reject: if closure flag contradicts geometric evaluation
notes: Periodic B-spline closure testing often relies on knot periodicity rather than evaluating actual curve endpoints. Synonyms: "B-spline periodic flag ignored", "open B-spline masquerades as closed", "U-periodic surface endpoint gap".
title: ShapeAnalysis_Surface.IsUClosed bspline-periodic-u

category: §12.3c faces (sub-class: gap detection in free bounds)
description: Free bounds (unclosed edges after face healing) are analyzed for gaps and notches. The notch checker computes arc length between consecutive edge endpoints; a gap smaller than parametric precision but larger than geometric tolerance indicates a healing-recoverable discrepancy. Incomplete re-validation after healing may miss newly opened gaps.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal: re-check free bounds after each healing pass; reject: if gap persists beyond configured threshold
notes: Notch detection depends on curve parameterization; gap magnitude in parameter-space may differ from 3D distance. Synonyms: "free bound gap post-healing", "notch revalidation skipped", "disconnected wire after face fix".
title: ShapeAnalysis_FreeBoundsProperties.CheckNotches gap-after-fix

description: Cylindrical and other periodic surfaces require a seam edge connecting the parametrically discontinuous boundary. A face missing the seam edge exhibits incorrect winding or fails containment checks. The missing-seam fixer detects the gap by analyzing edge coverage across the periodic parameter range; detection may fail if edges are nearly tangent or parameterized asymmetrically.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal: insert synthetic seam edge; reject: if seam-space analysis is ambiguous
notes: Seam detection relies on edge parameter-space analysis; misaligned boundaries or non-conformal parameterization defeat the heuristic. Synonyms: "cylindrical face seam missing", "periodic boundary incomplete", "U=0 to U=2π edge gap".
title: ShapeFix_Face.FixMissingSeam seam-detection

description: A conical surface whose semi-angle approaches zero becomes degenerate at the apex. The degeneracy analyzer identifies apex points by evaluating surface parametrization; missing or incomplete checks allow apex-degenerate faces to proceed without special-case handling, causing downstream curve projections and tangent computations to produce NaNs or infinite curvature.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal: flag apex edge for special handling; reject: if apex point lies outside face domain or is inconsistently parameterized
notes: Cone apex degeneracy manifests as zero-radius circular isocurves; detection requires symbolic surface analysis or numerical sampling. Synonyms: "cone apex point unclassified", "zero-angle cone surface", "degenerate apex in parametric space".
title: ShapeAnalysis_Surface.DegeneratedValues cone-apex-degeneracy

description: A Draft OrthoArray (4-instance grid) emits only one of the four `MAPPED_ITEM` instances. Receivers see only one body where the source authored four. Distinct from A108 because the loss is at the array-level (3 of 4 dropped), not at the mirror-level (1 of 1 dropped).

description: After a healing pass runs, vertex tolerance is larger than the edge tolerance of its containing edge, and edge tolerance is larger than the face tolerance of its containing face; the tolerance hierarchy is inverted. Common file signature: `GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` (or per-shape `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` instances) at three precision levels (face 1e-7, edge 1e-3, vertex 1e-2), with the per-element tolerances increasing as you go down the topology hierarchy. The invariant that a vertex's tolerance disc must fit inside its edge's tolerance disc, and an edge's disc inside its face's, is broken. Downstream Boolean and meshing algorithms rely on this hierarchy and produce incorrect results when it is violated.
expected_kernel_behavior: a healing pass that inflates a sub-shape's tolerance must propagate the inflation upward (vertex bumps edge, edge bumps face) so the hierarchy invariant always holds; or refuse to inflate when propagation would be unsafe.
notes: Canonical real-world regression: OCCT test `tests/bugs/heal/bug329`. Synonyms: "vertex tolerance bigger than edge tolerance", "tolerance hierarchy inverted", "edge tolerance exceeds face tolerance", "tolerance grows down the topology", "vertex disc doesn't fit inside edge disc".
reproducer: Build a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` whose vertices carry confusion-level tolerance, edges 1e-7, faces 1e-7. Run a healing pass with default flags after introducing a sub-tolerance gap. Inspect per-element tolerance after the fix.
sender: any (post-healing regression)
title: Vertex `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` larger than edge / face value (tolerance hierarchy violation)

description: A wireframe gap-fixing pass increases the maximum tolerance carried by edges and vertices to encompass the gap, rather than adjusting the underlying geometry to actually close it. The shape passes a topology check only because tolerance discs now overlap, hiding the real defect. The user-visible symptom is a "fixed" model whose vertex tolerance balls have ballooned to swallow gaps that were never repaired.
expected_kernel_behavior: a gap-fix pass should adjust edge curve endpoints (or insert a bridge edge) so the geometric gap closes; only inflate tolerance when geometry cannot be modified safely; warn when tolerance is inflated.
notes: **See also**: N040. Synonyms: "healer inflates tolerance instead of closing gap", "tolerance balls grow to swallow gap", "fix passes only because tolerance ballooned", "gap hidden behind fattened tolerance", "wire still has gap but model passes check".
reproducer: Wire with consecutive edges whose 3D endpoints differ by 0.001 mm on a model with declared 1e-6 uncertainty. Run a wireframe gap-fix pass.
title: Wireframe gap-fix inflates tolerance instead of bridging the gap

description: When two adjacent faces with the same supporting surface are merged into one (their shared edge is dissolved), the resulting shared vertex inherits a tolerance equal to the worst-case vertex among the merged inputs; e.g. `1e-1` even though one input vertex was `2e-7`. Downstream algorithms then treat points as fuzzy-equal where they were previously precise.
expected_kernel_behavior: recompute tolerance from actual post-merge geometric deviation rather than aggregating the worst input. A merge that takes a previously-precise vertex and balloons its tolerance is a fidelity loss.
notes: **See also**: A019, N040. Synonyms: "merge adopts worst input vertex tolerance", "shared vertex tolerance jumps after merge", "merged vertex inherits 1e-1 from worst neighbor", "face merge bloats fuzzy compare on shared vertex".
reproducer: Two coplanar faces with vertex tolerance 2e-7 and one vertex with tolerance 1e-1 (from prior healing). Apply same-domain face merging.
title: Same-domain face merge inflates shared-vertex tolerance to worst input

description: An `EDGE_CURVE` declares the same-parameter invariant (3D curve and pcurve share parameterisation, `SameParameter=.T.`), but a sampling check shows the maximum point-wise deviation exceeds the declared edge tolerance. Typical pattern: a 3D `LINE` from (0,0,0) to (10,0,0) plus a pcurve `LINE` on a `PLANE` running at v=0.005; the pcurve lifts to a curve offset by 0.005 mm from the 3D curve, but the edge tolerance is only 1e-6. The flag was set without re-validation after a geometry edit, so the metadata claims an invariant the data no longer satisfies; the same-parameter flag is true but curves disagree at sampled values.
expected_kernel_behavior: re-parameterise one curve so the flag is true, drop the flag and inflate edge tolerance to absorb the actual deviation, or reject as malformed. Choice is kernel-design-dependent.
notes: **See also**: N006. Synonyms: "3D curve and pcurve disagree at sampled points", "same parameter flag is true but curves don't match", "edge claims same param but pcurve drifts off 3D", "pcurve offset from 3D curve by 5 microns", "metadata claims invariant data has lost".
reproducer: Build an `EDGE_CURVE` with both 3D BSpline and pcurve. Reproject the pcurve at a different sampling. Set the same-parameter flag without recomputing. Run a topology checker.
title: Edge same-parameter flag asserted but 3D curve and pcurve disagree at sampled parameters (`SameParameter=.T.` lie)

description: Splitting a closed periodic shape (full `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE`, `TOROIDAL_SURFACE`) along its seam produces new edges whose 3D-curve and pcurve parameterisations no longer match — they were inherited from the unsplit edge but split independently. Common signature: a seam `EDGE_CURVE` on a cylinder with a 3D `LINE` from z=0 to z=10 (sense `.T.`) but its pcurve running from v=10 down to v=0 along −V (the `EDGE_CURVE` sense or pcurve direction inverted, e.g. `.F.`) — pcurve and 3D curve have opposite parameterisations across the seam. A topology checker reports invalid edges until a follow-up same-parameter recomputation runs.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: a splitter that produces new edges must restore the same-parameter invariant on those edges before returning, or reject the result. Returning a topologically-invalid intermediate result puts the burden on every caller.
notes: **See also**: N006. Synonyms: "pcurve direction opposite 3D curve after seam split", "split periodic face has reversed pcurve", "edge sense flipped vs pcurve sense across seam", "topology checker reports inconsistent parameterisation after split".
reproducer: Full cylinder solid → split along seam → run topology check; observe invalid edges. Recompute same-parameter; check passes.
title: Splitting a closed periodic face leaves new edges with reversed pcurve vs 3D curve parameterisation

description: A pcurve was reprojected at non-uniform sampling without rebasing its parameter range, so parameter-by-parameter evaluation against the 3D curve drifts. Some receivers compensate by silently inflating edge tolerance to cover the residual deviation, which hides a real geometric gap; the affected edges show up as "hot" (unusually large tolerance) on a tolerance-summary check.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: re-parameterise the pcurve so the same-parameter invariant holds, or reject loudly when the deviation exceeds budget. Silent edge-tolerance inflation discards information.
notes: **See also**: N004, N005. Synonyms: "pcurve and 3D curve out of sync", "non-uniform pcurve sampling drift", "tolerance silently inflated to cover pcurve drift", "edge tolerance unusually hot after reprojection".
reproducer: project a 3D curve onto a host surface with non-uniform spacing; do not rebase parameter; run a topology checker.
title: Pcurve drifts out of sync with 3D-curve parameterisation (geometric flavour)

description: When the imported edge's 3D curve and its endpoint vertices disagree beyond a precision threshold, the translator bumps the vertex tolerance by a constant multiplier (slightly above 1.0×) of the deviation, just enough to make the edge pass invariants. Repeated reads through the same path accumulate the multiplier and bloat tolerance without anchoring it against the file-level uncertainty.
expected_kernel_behavior: cap vertex-tolerance bumps against a multiple of the model's `uncertainty_measure_with_unit`, warn when the bump exceeds that threshold, or reject as malformed.
notes: **See also**: N025. Synonyms: "vertex tolerance bumped by tiny constant multiplier", "translator multiplies tolerance by 1.000001", "tolerance creeps up across repeated reads", "constant multiplier applied to vertex tolerance".
reproducer: AP203 file where a `VERTEX_POINT.cartesian_point` lies 1e-3 from the curve evaluation at the edge's parametric endpoint, on a model with 1e-6 declared uncertainty.
sender: Pro/E PRO8845
title: Vertex tolerance bump factor hard-coded `1.000001 *` on disagreement

description: A self-intersection-resolution pass modifies a pcurve and bumps the affected vertex's tolerance to encompass both the original and the new position. Successive rounds of this pass grow the vertex tolerance ball geometrically (e.g. 1e-7 → 1e-3 in a few iterations), eventually masking real gaps in modelled threads or fillets. The user-visible symptom is a "healed" model whose vertex tolerance balls have swallowed adjacent feature geometry.
expected_kernel_behavior: cap tolerance inflation, warn when a single healing pass inflates a vertex tolerance beyond a stated multiple of the file-level uncertainty measure, or refuse to heal further once tolerance balls overlap adjacent features. Carrying a "healed" provenance flag on inflated tolerances helps downstream consumers reject silent loss of fidelity.
notes: Synonyms: "vertex tolerance grows with each healing pass", "tolerance balloons over time", "tolerance ball swallows neighbor feature after multiple heals", "self-intersection healing keeps inflating tolerance", "vertex range increases monotonically across healers".
reproducer: Face with pcurve self-intersecting within the kernel's confusion tolerance. Apply self-intersection repair repeatedly. Track vertex tolerance per pass.
title: Vertex tolerance inflation by repeated self-intersection healing cascades

description: A vertex's stored 3D point is far enough from the evaluated parametric endpoints of its incident edges that the would-be vertex-tolerance disc spans the entire local feature. The vertex says "I am at point P", but every edge ending at it claims the edge actually ends somewhere else.
expected_kernel_behavior: snap the vertex onto the curve endpoints if within a snap tolerance, inflate vertex tolerance to encompass the dispersion (and warn), or reject as malformed.
notes: Synonyms: "vertex sits far from edge endpoints", "edges end far from their stored vertex", "vertex tolerance disc spans whole feature", "incident edges disagree with vertex position".
reproducer: `EDGE_CURVE` with line `(0,0,0)→(1,0,0)`, vertex at `(0, 0.001, 0)`, declared tolerance `0.0001`.
title: Vertex 3D point lies far from incident-edge curve endpoints (dispersion exceeds tolerance)

description: An `EDGE_CURVE` whose 3D length is less than the bounding vertex tolerances. Typical signature: vertices at (0,0,0) and (5e-5,0,0) — edge length 5e-5 mm — with the global `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` / `distance_accuracy` declared as 1e-4 mm, so vertex tolerance is roughly twice the entire edge length. The two vertex tolerance balls already touch each other; the edge geometry adds nothing and trips Boolean / mesh algorithms.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal — detect by `len(curve) < tol(V1) + tol(V2)`; remove edge or merge endpoints; preserve adjacent edge wires.
notes: **See also**: N011. Synonyms: "edge shorter than its endpoint tolerance", "edge length below vertex range", "vertex sphere covers entire edge", "tiny edge under tolerance disc", "edge geometry adds nothing because vertices already merge".
reproducer: Edge with vertices nearly coincident (gap < tol) and short non-degenerate 3D curve. `IsUClosed`/`IsVClosed` previously returned wrong without a midpoint distance check.
sender: IGES (also affects STEP)
title: `EDGE_CURVE` shorter than vertex tolerance (tiny edge covered by vertices, `distance_accuracy` exceeds edge length)

description: A periodic face needs a seam edge inserted to close its UV bound, but the seam would lie entirely inside an already-existing vertex tolerance ball. Inserting the seam anyway creates a "real" edge of length zero whose endpoints are tolerance-equivalent; violating the invariant that the vertex tolerance ball does not cover any real edge.
expected_kernel_behavior: skip the seam insertion when it would be tolerance-collapsed and bridge with vertex tolerance instead, or rebuild with a smaller vertex tolerance so the seam can exist as a real edge.
notes: **See also**: N010. Synonyms: "zero-length seam edge inserted", "seam ends at coincident vertices", "real edge fits inside vertex tolerance disc", "seam insertion produces zero-length edge".
reproducer: Cylindrical face whose seam falls inside vertex tolerance ball.
title: Seam edge inserted inside an existing vertex tolerance ball produces zero-length edge

description: Programmatically reducing a face tolerance below the actual geometric defect, then running `ShapeFix`, makes the fix algorithm interpret coincident vertex tolerance balls as separate vertices, producing vertex/vertex intersection diagnostics.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; recompute tolerance from current geometry rather than trusting user-set sub-resolution tolerance.
notes: Synonyms: "lowering face tolerance creates vertex/vertex intersection", "ShapeFix sees coincident vertices as separate", "shrinking tolerance triggers spurious intersections".
reproducer: Set face tolerance to `1e-9` on a face whose actual edge gap is `1e-5`, then `ShapeFix_Shape::Perform`.
title: Setting face tolerance to a tiny value then ShapeFix produces vertex/vertex intersections

description: When three or more surfaces meet at a single mathematical vertex, OCCT computes each pairwise edge-edge intersection independently. Floating-point error makes the three candidate vertex coordinates disagree by 1e-9 to 1e-5, so the boolean output emits three almost-coincident vertices and three short edges (or a tiny triangle face) in place of one shared vertex.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; compute the desired vertex by edge-face intersection (one dimension lower) and snap candidate vertices to it; carry an accumulated-error tolerance budget per topological entity.
notes: Synonyms: "three-surface meet point splits into three vertices", "pairwise intersections disagree by 1e-9", "boolean cascade introduces vertex jitter", "single mathematical vertex becomes three near-coincident vertices", "tiny triangle face appears where one vertex should be".
reproducer: Boolean-intersect three half-spaces meeting in one vertex with rotated frames so each pairwise intersection suffers small numerical perturbation.
title: Boolean cascade vertex deviation (independently computed pairwise intersections)

description: An intersection edge that ought to be zero-length persists due to misclassification at the topological filtering step. Both endpoints lie within tolerance of a single corrected position, but the filter treats them as distinct. Typical signature: an `EDGE_CURVE` between vertices at (2e-8,0,0) and (-2e-8,0,0) — length 4e-8 mm — with declared `distance_accuracy` 1e-7 mm, so the two vertices are several times closer than the tolerance and the edge should collapse to a single vertex.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; detect that both endpoints are within tolerance of one common corrected position; collapse the edge to a vertex.
notes: Synonyms: "tiny edge that should have collapsed", "vertex separation below declared tolerance but edge survives", "intersection edge that should be zero-length", "filter doesn't merge near-coincident vertices into one".
reproducer: Two surfaces tangent along a curve with a single contact point; numerical noise produces a short crossing edge near that point.
title: Spurious tiny `EDGE_CURVE` that should have collapsed: vertex separation below declared tolerance

description: Setting OCCT's cascade unit to meters during STEP/IGES read inflates max-tolerance >0.001 (some files balloon AABB to ±1e+100). With unit=`M`, too-small distances are not detected during edge reordering and BSpline segments are missed. Other unit selections (INCH/MIL/UIN/CM/MM/UM) work; `M` does not because the working tolerance scales below kernel resolution.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; compute working tolerance from vertex resolution + surface resolution at each entity, not from a single kernel-wide constant; produce finite geometry equivalent to `MM` import scaled by 1000.
notes: Synonyms: "meters cascade unit inflates tolerance", "unit set to M corrupts geometry", "OCCT meters mode produces 1e+100 bbox", "BSpline segments missed under M unit setting".
reproducer: `param xstep.cascade.unit M; ReadStep D multi_solids.stp; bounding -dump`. Compare with `MM` import scaled by 1000.
title: `xstep.cascade.unit M` meters setting inflates tolerance and corrupts geometry

description: CATIA writes per-edge tolerance values (via `geometric_representation_context_and_global_uncertainty_assigned_context` plus per-edge precisions encoded in the entity attributes) that are 2-3 orders of magnitude larger than the file's default tolerance. Receivers reading only the global tolerance find gaps between adjacent faces and treat the body as an open shell.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; respect per-edge tolerance metadata; do not collapse to a single document tolerance. Tag every edge/vertex with its own tolerance budget.
notes: **See also**: U028. Synonyms: "CATIA per-edge tolerance much larger than file default", "edges carry their own precision values", "shell looks open because reader missed per-edge tolerance", "global tolerance too tight vs per-edge values".
reproducer: CATIA-emitted STEP with file tolerance 0.0001 mm but specific edges using 0.005 mm tolerance metadata.
sender: CATIA V5/V6
title: Edge tolerance 2-3 orders of magnitude > file tolerance (CATIA per-edge precision)

description: Many STEP exporters emit `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` with a constant field-default value (e.g. 0.027352…) rather than a true measure of producer-side precision. Receivers that take this value as document tolerance get bad joins and false gaps when the real geometry is accurate to 1e-6.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; cap reported tolerance against geometric tightness measured from the actual model; offer override; default to `read.precision.val` parameter when uncertainty is missing or implausible.
notes: **See also**: N019. Synonyms: "uncertainty value looks like template default", "constant 0.027352 tolerance from exporter", "uncertainty is fixed default not real precision", "writer emits placeholder tolerance value".
reproducer: STEP with `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(LENGTH_MEASURE(0.027352…), …, 'distance_accuracy_value', '')` on geometry actually accurate to 1e-6.
title: `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` populated with a fixed field-default value (untrustworthy)

description: When a STEP file's `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT` lacks the `GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` leaf — for example carries only `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` and no `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` for the model — OCCT silently falls back to the `read.precision.val` parameter. Models from such files all share whatever precision the user happened to configure, regardless of source.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal — emit explicit "no uncertainty context" diagnostic; require user to confirm fallback; do not silently default.
notes: **See also**: U025. **OCC behavior**: silently falls back to the configured working precision with no diagnostic; kernel mishandling; the catalog above forbids silent default. Synonyms: "no UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE in file", "model precision falls back to user setting", "tolerance silently inherits read.precision", "GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT lacks uncertainty leaf".
reproducer: STEP file lacking `*_AND_GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` complex entity; reference only bare `geometric_representation_context`.
title: `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT` missing `GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` leaf → fall back to read.precision

description: An `OFFSET_SURFACE` built on a `PLANE` (or other base surface) whose offset distance is below the importer's working tolerance; typical signature: offset 5e-5 mm with the face's `EDGE_CURVE`s sitting at z=5e-5 to lift onto the offset surface. BRL-CAD's `step-g` importer hard-codes `m_tolerance = 1e-3` for edges and trims rather than reading the file's `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` / `representation_context.length_measure`. Models requiring tighter tolerance lose feature fidelity; offset surfaces barely separated from their base plane are crushed back into the base plane.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal — read accuracy from `geometric_representation_context_with_uncertainty` and propagate to edge/trim tolerances; never hard-code.
notes: **See also**: N017. Synonyms: "importer hard-codes 1e-3 tolerance ignoring file", "offset surface flattens into base", "BRL-CAD step-g ignores file uncertainty", "tiny offset surface lost because hard tolerance".
reproducer: AP203 file with `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(LENGTH_MEASURE(0.000001), …, 'distance_accuracy_value', '')` imported via step-g.
title: `OFFSET_SURFACE` with sub-tolerance offset (fixed-tolerance importer hard-codes 1e-3)

description: KiCad hard-codes a `BOARD_OFFSET = 0.05 mm` constant on every component's `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D`, floating components above the board surface to avoid Z-fighting in viewers. Downstream MCAD tools that build enclosure geometry against the PCB top face see consistent 0.05 mm misalignment that doesn't correspond to any physical clearance.
expected_kernel_behavior: accept; surface a flag warning "consumer-applied placement offset detected" when small uniform Z offsets across many child instances are present.
notes: Synonyms: "KiCad PCB components float 0.05 mm above board", "hard-coded board offset misaligns components", "PCB to MCAD pipeline shifts parts by 0.05 mm", "every component placed slightly above PCB top".
reproducer: Export any KiCad PCB to STEP. Inspect the `MAPPED_ITEM` for any footprint-attached 3D model: its `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` location's Z is shifted 0.05 mm relative to the board top face.
sender: KiCad pcbnew STEP exporter
title: Coordinate-system origin offset: hard-coded BOARD_OFFSET 0.05mm in PCB→MCAD pipeline

description: KiCad VRML export places Z=0 at the board *center*; STEP export places Z=0 at the board *bottom*. Downstream tools mixing the two formats see components shifted by half-board-thickness, even though both come from the same producer.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; when a producer with known origin-convention drift is detected (via `FILE_DESCRIPTION` heuristics), warn and offer re-anchoring.
notes: Synonyms: "VRML uses board center, STEP uses board bottom", "Z=0 differs between formats from same producer", "components shifted by half board thickness across formats".
reproducer: For a 1.6 mm board, export both VRML and STEP from the same KiCad project. Inspect the bounding box and assembly origin in each.
sender: KiCad pcbnew (VRML vs STEP exporters)
title: VRML/STEP origin convention mismatch within same producer

description: STEP files emit an `EDGE_CURVE` whose underlying `LINE` is parallel-displaced from the line that actually passes through both vertex points. Direction is correct; position is offset. Translator must shift the line so it passes through both vertices, preserving direction.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; replace the line so it passes through both vertices, preserving original direction.
notes: **See also**: Gs021. Synonyms: "edge LINE doesn't pass through its vertices", "line direction correct but offset", "translator must shift line to vertex points", "underlying line parallel to actual edge".
reproducer: VERTEX_POINT A at `(0,0,0)`, VERTEX_POINT B at `(10,0,0)`, EDGE_CURVE referring to LINE whose `pnt`/`dir` give a parallel line offset by 0.001 mm.
sender: FPX Expert 2013 (PCB design system)
title: `EDGE_CURVE` based on `LINE` displaced from true vertex position

description: After local edits (face translation, blend suppression, partial defeaturing), an edge's stored 3D curve no longer matches the geometric intersection of its two host faces. Typical signature: two `PLANE` instances exist — the original at z=0 and the edited one at z=0.01 — but an `EDGE_CURVE` between them still references a 3D `LINE` at z=0, the pre-edit plane. The edge survives as topology but its curve is stale, leading to large tolerances or visible cracks.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; `rebuild-edge` re-intersects host faces and rebuilds vertices; vertex-freezing flag handles near-tangential cases.
notes: **See also**: Gs030. Synonyms: "edge curve stale after face moved", "LINE is at old position after face translate", "edit moved face but edge geometry didn't follow", "two planes exist but edge still on old one", "edge curve doesn't match host face intersection".
reproducer: Translate one host face of an edge by a small offset without rebuilding the edge; compare `BRepAdaptor_Curve(edge)` to `IntPatch_Intersection(s1, s2)` — they diverge.
title: `EDGE_CURVE` 3D `LINE` stale relative to translated host `PLANE` (rebuild-edge case)

description: Imported B-reps regularly contain pairs of vertices and edges that the designer intended to be the same but which sit a few microns apart due to translator round-off. Coordinates agree to 1e-4 but topology stores them as distinct entities; a "crack" rather than a "gap" because geometric distance is zero by some metrics yet topology is broken.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; stitch by spatial proximity within tolerance; merge duplicate vertices and split/reconcile edges.
notes: **See also**: N007. Synonyms: "vertices coincide spatially but topology distinct", "coincident edges not shared after translation", "topology cracks despite zero distance", "coordinates equal but vertices not the same entity".
reproducer: STEP file from translator A whose two adjacent `ADVANCED_FACE`s each instantiate their own `VERTEX_POINT` for the corner; coordinates agree to 1e-4.
title: Coincident-but-not-shared vertices/edges (cross-translator round-off)

description: The three production kernels (Parasolid, ACIS, CGM) define validity differently. ACIS may export a body with a tolerant edge of tolerance 5e-4; Parasolid demands geometric intersection within 1e-6 and rejects the edge. What was a single shared vertex in the source becomes two vertices in the target — or vice versa — depending on the receiving kernel's snap rules.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; tag every edge and vertex with a per-entity tolerance; rebuild face/edge adjacencies up to that tolerance; only error if re-intersection demonstrates the relation cannot be established.
notes: **See also**: Tsh001. Synonyms: "body valid in ACIS but rejected by Parasolid", "kernel-specific tolerance bookkeeping", "tolerant edge accepted in source rejected in target", "kernels disagree on what counts as one vertex".
reproducer: Export an ACIS body that uses a tolerant edge with tolerance 5e-4 to STEP; import into a Parasolid pipeline that demands geometric intersection within 1e-6.
title: Cross-kernel topology rejection: source-valid, target-invalid by tolerance bookkeeping

description: gmsh user sets `Geometry.OCCTargetUnit = "M"`, but a STEP `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` of r=1 h=10 in MILLI-METRE units gets imported as r=1000 h=10000 (the ×1000 scaling is applied unexpectedly). Common signature: a small 1 mm-radius cylinder with vertex coordinates like (0, 0.001, 0) and declared `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` 1e-6 mm; relative precision is at the working-tolerance boundary, so any unit conversion glitch is immediately visible. The setting is honored when the file enters via `importShapes` but skipped when via `importShapesNativePointer`. Different geometries from the same producer require different `OCCTargetUnit` values to mesh.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; always apply target-unit conversion at the OCC→consumer boundary, regardless of the entry path.
notes: Synonyms: "gmsh OCCTargetUnit silently ignored", "small mm cylinder imported with x1000 scale", "different geometries need different OCCTargetUnit settings", "importShapesNativePointer skips unit conversion".
reproducer: STEP with `LENGTH_UNIT()NAMED_UNIT(*)SI_UNIT(.MILLI.,.METRE.)`; load via OCC C++ then hand to gmsh via pointer interface.
title: Small-mm `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` with target-unit mismatch (gmsh `OCCTargetUnit` silently ignored on `importShapesNativePointer` path)

description: When the STEP model's `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT` carries no `LENGTH_UNIT` in its `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` — for example only `PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT` and `SOLID_ANGLE_UNIT` are present, and no `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` is attached — the user-configured `xstep.cascade.unit` is silently ignored. The reader uses an internal default and the model arrives at unexpected scale.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; apply user-provided unit as fallback when the model itself does not declare one.
notes: Synonyms: "model has only angle units no length unit", "length unit missing from context", "cascade.unit ignored when LENGTH_UNIT absent", "GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT has no length unit".
reproducer: STEP file lacking explicit unit declaration; set user `xstep.cascade.unit` and observe the effect (or lack thereof).
title: `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT` missing `LENGTH_UNIT` (only angle units present) → user-configured cascade.unit ignored

description: A STEP file written in inches is silently treated as millimetres because the `LENGTH_UNIT` declaration is parsed inconsistently. Many possibilities exist for declaring units (named units, conversion-based units, context-dependent units) and OpenCascade-based readers default to mm. Result: a 2 inch feature appears 50.8 mm in source vs 2 mm in target; a 25.4× error.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; resolve full unit-conversion chain to a single SI scale factor; reject if ambiguous; never default silently.
notes: **See also**: U006. Synonyms: "inches silently treated as mm", "25.4x scale error on import", "inch model arrives 25.4 times too small", "LENGTH_UNIT inch parsed as default mm".
reproducer: SolidWorks STEP with `( LENGTH_UNIT() NAMED_UNIT(*) SI_UNIT($,.METRE.) )` plus a conversion-based wrapper for inches; receiver reads the wrapper as identity.
sender: SolidWorks (inch units), Onshape (workspace inches)
title: Inch-units silent treatment as mm (25.4× scale error)

description: A surface that mathematically is a `PLANE` / `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` / `CONICAL_SURFACE` / `SPHERICAL_SURFACE` / `TOROIDAL_SURFACE` / `SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION` is stored as a generic `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS`. Common shape: a quarter cylinder modelled as a degree-2-by-1 B-spline with a 3×2 control net plus a small declared canonicalisation tolerance (e.g. 1e-6). Feature recognition (hole/shaft detection), unfolding, CAM tool-axis derivation, DXF/SVG export, and GD&T tools all degrade silently because they cannot ask the surface for its radius or axis. Canonical-recognition tolerance (how tightly the BSpline must fit the analytic form) is rarely exposed.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; `convert-to-canonical` / `ShapeCustom_BSplineRestriction` with a tolerance recovers the analytic form; reject canonicalization if recovered surface deviates beyond user-supplied tolerance, since otherwise watertightness is lost.
notes: **See also**: Pmi041, Gn014. Synonyms: "cylinder stored as B-spline instead of analytic", "feature recognition can't find hole as B-spline", "analytic surface lost as NURBS", "kernel doesn't recognize quarter cylinder", "B-spline that should be cylinder or plane".
reproducer: Import a STEP from a system that always writes NURBS; query a "cylindrical" face's `BRepAdaptor_Surface::GetType()` — returns `GeomAbs_BSplineSurface` instead of `GeomAbs_Cylinder`.
title: Quarter `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` stored as `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS` (canonical recognition tolerance budget)

description: G0/G1/G2 discontinuities introduced when neighbouring faces are re-parametrized into different surface types during translation. Tangent-plane jumps appear at shared edges that were smooth in the source. Translation re-fits surfaces independently; tangent agreement is not a constraint of the per-surface fit.
expected_kernel_behavior: accept; report as quality warning; archive-stable only if validation properties (volume, area) still match within tolerance.
notes: **See also**: M026, M027. Synonyms: "tangent jump at shared edge after translation", "G1 broken across faces after import", "smooth surfaces become creased on round-trip", "translator re-fits surfaces and loses tangent continuity".
reproducer: Convert a Catia procedural blend to STEP — the blend often becomes several `RATIONAL_B_SPLINE_SURFACE` patches whose tangent planes at shared edges differ by more than the resolution tolerance.
title: Surface discontinuities introduced by translation (G0/G1/G2 break at shared edges)

description: STEP file uses an AP242 tolerance entity (e.g. `RUNOUT_TOLERANCE_WITH_VALUES`, `UNEQUALLY_DISPOSED_GEOMETRIC_TOLERANCE`, `RUNOUT_ZONE_DEFINITION` with `RUNOUT_ZONE_ORIENTATION_REFERENCE_DIRECTION`) that the importer drops because it isn't in its parser. Repeated fixes across HOOPS releases prove this class is large and ongoing.
expected_kernel_behavior: accept gracefully; at minimum preserve the raw entity through round-trip; do not crash; warn on unknown subtype.
notes: Synonyms: "AP242 tolerance entity dropped on import", "GD&T tolerance lost in translation", "RUNOUT_TOLERANCE not parsed", "tolerance frame missing after STEP read".
reproducer: AP242 file containing `RUNOUT_ZONE_DEFINITION` etc.; importer that only knows AP214.
sender: AP242 PMI emitter (Creo MBD, NX MBD, SolidWorks MBD)
title: Tolerance type entity coverage: AP242 tolerance entities dropped on import

description: `STEP_SHAPE_TOLERANCE_VALUE` lower/upper bounds may be encoded via plain `length_measure_with_unit`, via `StepRepr_ReprItemAndMeasureWithUnit`, or via the AP242 complex form `(LENGTH_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT() MEASURE_REPRESENTATION_ITEM() MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(…) REPRESENTATION_ITEM(''))`. Readers that hard-code a single subtype fail; OCCT had 21 reader classes affected.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept all variants; go through `StepRepr_ReprItemAndMeasureWithUnit::GetMeasureWithUnit` polymorphic accessor; never assume one form.
notes: **See also**: N034. Synonyms: "tolerance measure encoded multiple ways", "reader handles only one tolerance subtype", "polymorphic measure-with-unit confuses parser", "AP242 complex form for tolerance value not read".
reproducer: NIST PMI examples (nist_ctc_01.nist_stc_10 ap242-e1/e2) with magnitudes wrapped in the complex form.
title: Tolerance value polymorphic encoding (`MeasureRepresentationItem` vs plain measure)

category: §12.4 (sub-class: tolerance type entity coverage / PMI numeric)
description: `PLUS_MINUS_TOLERANCE` recorded with `upper_bound < lower_bound` or `upper_bound == lower_bound` or with bound expressed via `descriptive_representation_item` / `plane_angle_measure_with_unit` instead of `length_measure_with_unit`. SFA tooling flags these as warnings; many CAD systems silently accept and ignore.
expected_kernel_behavior: warn or auto-swap; reject the wrong-type case.
notes: **See also**: N033. Synonyms: "upper tolerance bound less than lower", "PLUS_MINUS_TOLERANCE has equal bounds", "tolerance bound uses wrong measure type", "angle measure used for length tolerance".
reproducer: `PLUS_MINUS_TOLERANCE(TOLERANCE_VALUE(LENGTH_MEASURE(0.005), LENGTH_MEASURE(-0.005)),..);` with values swapped.
title: `+/-` tolerance bounds inverted, equal, or wrong measure type

description: Some CAD systems ignore tolerance values that lack an explicit decimal-place qualifier even if a global default precision is set. The fallback hierarchy is: precision at tolerance value → precision at nominal value → global default. Receivers that don't walk the chain show wrong-precision tolerance.
expected_kernel_behavior: accept; fall through the precision hierarchy correctly; emit warning when default is needed.
notes: **See also**: Pmi008. Synonyms: "tolerance ignored without decimal-place qualifier", "default precision not picked up", "tolerance value shown wrong precision", "fallback chain broken for precision qualifier".
reproducer: Dimension with nominal value `5.0`, tolerance `+0.01/-0.01`, but no `precision_qualifier` on either the value or the nominal, and no global default.
title: Default tolerance precision: missing decimal-place qualifier

description: The relative centroid threshold (deviation / model size) breaks down when the bounding-box space diagonal is below ~20 mm at 0.02 mm model accuracy: a 0.1% threshold becomes smaller than the modeling tolerance, so even valid round-trips fail validation.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; select the absolute-mm centroid threshold whenever model size is below 20 mm.
notes: Synonyms: "centroid check fails on small models", "0.1 percent threshold below modeling tolerance", "valid round-trips fail centroid validation", "centroid validation too strict for small parts".
reproducer: Build a part whose bounding-box space diagonal is 5 mm. Provide a centroid GVP. Apply both relative and absolute thresholds.
title: Centroid validation breaks down when relative threshold goes below modeling tolerance

description: After format conversion the endpoints of adjacent 3D curve segments along a wire no longer meet within geometric tolerance; a class introduced *by translation*, not present in the native model. Source seam tolerance 1e-3 through a kernel that demands 1e-5 leaves position, cross-tangent, and cross-curvature gaps.
expected_kernel_behavior: bridge the segment endpoints by adjusting curve endpoints (or inserting connecting curves) so the wire is geometrically connected within the receiving kernel's working tolerance; or reject as a translation-fidelity issue.
notes: Synonyms: "curve segments don't meet after conversion", "wire gaps introduced by translation", "tangent gaps after kernel translation", "LOTAR exchange leaves wire breaks".
reproducer: Concatenated `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` segments where end control points of segment N do not equal start control points of segment N+1 within `geometric_representation_context` tolerance.
title: Curve gaps between adjacent segments after format conversion (LOTAR exchange defect)

description: Adjacent faces are not "approximately equal" to an interval solid: the maximum gap between any two trimmed surfaces along their shared edge exceeds the chosen interval radius. Without this guarantee the boundary reconstruction is not provably gap-free; the model is effectively non-watertight for any tolerance below the maximum gap.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; reconstruct an interval solid that bounds both surfaces in a tube of radius ε; if no such tube exists, refine geometry until it does.
notes: Synonyms: "face-pair gap exceeds interval bound", "model not watertight by interval-solid metric", "shared edge gap larger than interval radius", "interval-solid validity violated".
reproducer: Two B-spline trims along a shared edge whose maximum Hausdorff distance is 5×ε in a model with declared tolerance ε.
sources: 15-academic L044 (Patrikalakis, Sakkalis, Shen, Math of Surfaces IX 2000)
title: Patrikalakis interval-solid violation: face-pair gap exceeds bound

description: A healing pass touches every sub-shape and inflates edge/vertex tolerances even on those whose existing tolerance already covers the actual deviation. Common file signature: `GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` carries two `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` entries — a native 1e-6 mm precision and a post-fix "over-bumped" 1e-3 mm — a 1000× bump applied across the whole model after a healing pass on two consecutive edges sharing a single vertex. Combined with an in-place mutation mode, the input shape itself is silently bloated. The user-visible symptom is a healed model whose tolerance discs grew across every feature, even features that were valid to begin with.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: only inflate tolerance when the actual deviation requires it; default to non-mutating (copy-on-write) input handling. Must not silently inflate.
notes: **See also**: N040. Synonyms: "healer inflates tolerance 1000x on already-good shapes", "post-fix tolerance bloated everywhere", "tolerance jumped from 1e-6 to 1e-3 after heal", "healing pass touches every subshape", "uniform tolerance bloat after fix".
reproducer: Pass a shape whose deviations are all within current tolerance through a full healing pass. Compare per-vertex tolerances before and after.
title: Healing pass over-eagerly inflates tolerances 1000× on sub-shapes that needed no fix (post-fix `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` bloat)

description: Salome's "Limit Tolerance" forces the tolerance of a shape's vertices/edges/faces back down to a user-given value. When tolerances were inflated by upstream tools to hide real gaps, clamping back down re-exposes those gaps as topology defects (now-disconnected vertices, open wires). Typical file signature: two `GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` entries — a bloated 1e-3 mm pre-clamp tolerance and a tight 1e-6 mm post-clamp value — together with two consecutive edges whose shared `VERTEX_POINT` coordinates differ by ~5e-4 mm (e.g. (10.0005,0,0) vs (10,0,0)), so the gap was within the bloated tolerance but exceeds the clamped one.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal cautiously; clamp tolerances; re-run validity checks; report newly-exposed gaps to the user before continuing.
notes: **See also**: N002, N003, N039. Synonyms: "clamping tolerance re-exposes gaps", "Limit Tolerance breaks supposedly healed model", "open wires reappear after tolerance clamp", "vertices that were merged drift apart at lower tolerance".
reproducer: STEP with bloated tolerances after multi-tool import; apply Limit Tolerance with target equal to original `uncertainty_measure_with_unit`.
title: `Limit Tolerance` clamp re-exposes gaps that bloated tolerances were hiding (Salome)

description: Manifold tracks an ε (the maximum vertex-perturbation that would suffice to make the mesh strictly non-overlapping). Cumulative transform / Boolean error inflates ε beyond the input scale. Subsequent Booleans become unstable. User must either rebuild from cleaner data or call `SetTolerance` to widen and `Simplify`.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; track per-mesh ε explicitly; expose to caller; refuse Boolean when ε exceeds a fraction of model size.
notes: **See also**: Pf021, Pf023. Synonyms: "epsilon grows past input scale", "Manifold validity epsilon balloons", "cumulative transform error inflates epsilon", "boolean unstable after epsilon grew".
reproducer: Apply a chain of 50 Boolean operations to a Manifold mesh; query `GetEpsilon()` between operations; observe monotone growth.
title: Manifold ε-validity contract: cumulative transform error inflates ε beyond input scale

description: When OCCT computed a curve's bounding box for self-intersection detection, it used too few sampling points; near-tangent intersections were missed. step-g hits the inverse: sampling p-curves with <2 points produces degenerate trims.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; use density-of-discretization correlated with curve curvature for bbox; never rely on a fixed sample count; enforce minimum sample count ≥ 2 on degenerate inputs.
notes: **See also**: Pf006. **OCC behavior**: the validity-checker does not flag the near-tangent edge intersections missed by coarse bbox sampling; tier-3 valid-flag should be ignored for this entry. The reader most likely silently fixes or ignores the missed self-intersection on import. Synonyms: "self-intersection missed by sparse sampling", "coarse bounding box check misses near-tangent", "p-curves with too few samples cause degenerate trims", "near-tangent curves miss intersection due to undersample".
reproducer: STEP wire on planar face containing two near-tangent edges; bbox-based intersection test with default sample count misses the crossing.
title: Self-intersecting wire from coarse-discretization bbox check (sample-count too small)

description: For two shapes that demonstrably intersect (their volumes clearly overlap), the minimum-distance query returns a small but nonzero value (e.g. 6e-5 or 0.083) instead of zero. The distance algorithm samples corner points and edge endpoints but does not verify true intersection, so a transverse intersection between two interior surfaces is missed.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: a minimum-distance query between two intersecting bodies must return zero (or a value smaller than the kernel's working precision); when sampling reports a near-zero distance, the kernel should fall back to a true intersection test rather than reporting the sample value.
notes: Synonyms: "distance query says gap but parts overlap", "shapes overlap but distance is nonzero", "distance algorithm misses interior intersection", "min distance returns 6e-5 for clearly intersecting solids".
reproducer: 4 cylinders intersecting a main part; compute pairwise minimum distance.
title: Shape-to-shape distance reports nonzero gap for clearly intersecting parts

description: Stable identifiers assigned to entities (faces, edges) for change tracking and PMI binding are regenerated by intermediate tools, breaking PMI references; a tolerance frame referencing face #47 in a source file no longer resolves after round-trip because the receiver renumbered topology.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: preserve persistent IDs (UUIDs in `name_attribute` or `APPLIED_IDENTIFICATION_ASSIGNMENT`) verbatim during read+write; generate new IDs only for newly created entities. Must not silently regenerate IDs.
notes: **See also**: A011, A028, Pmi001, Pmi057, Pmi065. Synonyms: "face IDs renumbered breaks PMI links", "stable IDs lost on round-trip", "tolerance frame loses face reference", "PMI reference no longer resolves after import", "topology renumbered drops persistent identifiers".
reproducer: Round-trip an AP242 file through a viewer that recreates topology; `STEP_id` of every face changes; semantic PMI bound to those IDs becomes orphaned.
title: Persistent IDs lost across editing/translation breaks PMI tolerance attachment

description: Two edges intersect inside their parameter range but the intersection point is within vertex tolerance of one edge's endpoint. A wire-intersection check filters out the intersection because the vertex "owns" that point; leaving an undetected interior intersection that invalidates the wire downstream.
expected_kernel_behavior: edge-intersection report "intersection inside vertex tolerance" as a distinct status; do not silently filter.
notes: **See also**: Twi049, N039. **OCC behavior**: silently filters out the edge-internal intersection with no diagnostic; kernel mishandling; the catalog above forbids silent filtering. Synonyms: "edge-internal intersection ignored", "two edges cross inside parameter range but missed", "intersection check only at endpoints", "vertex tolerance check skips edge interior".
reproducer: Two edges meeting at a `T`-junction: one edge ends at vertex V; the other passes through V's tolerance ball but does not end at V. Edge-intersection check returns "no intersection" because the point is inside V's tolerance.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0024922 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Vertex tolerance under-checked: edge-internal intersection ignored

description: A point-projection-onto-surface routine uses a hard-coded tolerance instead of consulting the input shape's vertex/edge tolerance or the file's declared UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT. When the input context declares tolerance 1e-3, the projection fails because the routine still uses 1e-7. Typical fixture: a free CARTESIAN_POINT at e.g. (0.5, 0.5, 5e-4) sits 5e-4 above a PLANE z=0; within the declared 1e-3 mm context tolerance, but the kernel can't project it.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: projection routines consume the source shape's tolerance; default value is a fallback only when no shape context is available.
notes: **See also**: N039. Synonyms: "projection uses hard-coded internal tolerance", "free point off plane within file tolerance but rejected by hard internal", "internal tolerance ignores file uncertainty", "point projection fails on tolerant face".
reproducer: PLANE z=0 with file-scope tolerance 1e-3; project a free CARTESIAN_POINT at (0.5, 0.5, 5e-4) onto the surface. Routine reports "no projection found" because internal tolerance is 1e-7.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0022826 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Default tolerance projection wrong on non-default tolerance shapes (free CARTESIAN_POINT off PLANE within declared tolerance but beyond hard-coded internal tolerance)

description: Same-domain face-merge logic uses fixed linear and angular tolerances. For a coarse-mesh-derived shape (linear tolerance ~0.1 mm), the fixed thresholds are too tight and merges fail; for a high-precision shape they are too loose and over-merge.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: tolerance-using algorithms accept caller-supplied tolerances or read them from the input shape; never hard-code.
notes: **See also**: N039, Tfa017. Synonyms: "two coplanar faces share an edge but are not unified", "same-plane faces fail to merge", "face merge fails on shared edge", "coplanar adjacent faces left separate", "fixed merge threshold rejects coplanar faces", "merge tolerance not user-specifiable".
reproducer: Two coplanar faces with native vertex tolerance ~0.1 mm, sharing a common edge. Algorithm uses fixed 1e-7 threshold and refuses to merge.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0027729 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Linear and angular tolerance for same-surface face merging not user-specifiable

description: A surface-surface intersection algorithm walks along the intersection curve in fixed-size parameter steps, ignoring the surfaces' tolerances. On a coarse-tolerance shape (1e-3) the steps overshoot the tolerance, producing a coarse polyline that is then mistakenly accepted as the intersection curve.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: walking step adapts to surface curvature and tolerance; emit fewer / more samples to maintain tolerance-bounded deviation.
notes: **See also**: N046. Synonyms: "surface intersection walks with fixed step", "walk step ignores tolerance", "intersection algorithm uses constant initial step", "walking step unrelated to working precision".
reproducer: Two cylinders intersecting at a curve; cylinders have tolerance 1e-3. Algorithm walks at step 1e-7 (way over-sampled, slow) or step 1e-1 (under-sampled, wrong curve).
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0026554 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Walk-line initial step unrelated to tolerance during surface intersection

category: §12.4 tolerance & numerical precision (sub-class: invalid shape on import)
description: A STEP file imports without diagnostic, but `BRepCheck_Analyzer` on the resulting shape returns `BRepCheck_InvalidPointOnCurve` / `BRepCheck_NotClosed` / `BRepCheck_InvalidWire`. The defect is at the boundary between the producer's tolerance and the receiver's: the file is structurally legal, the geometry is "almost" valid, and the reader silently accepts but downstream operations (Boolean, mesh, sewn-shell promotion) fail with cryptic errors. Distinct from M160 (silent-empty); here a shape is produced, but it is not valid.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; auto-bump edge tolerance during import to the maximum of the producer's claimed tolerance and the measured point-on-curve deviation; emit `W_TOLERANCE_BUMPED`. Downstream operations should never see an invalid shape.
notes: **See also**: N015, N028, Twi099. Synonyms: "reading STEP file produces invalid shape", "BRepCheck flags imported shape", "STEP import yields shape that fails Analyzer", "tolerance mismatch between producer and receiver".
reproducer: `EDGE_CURVE` whose end-vertex `CARTESIAN_POINT` is at distance `2e-6` from the curve at the curve's parameter; receiver's edge tolerance is `1e-7`. Reader imports; `BRepCheck` flags.
sender: Producers whose `EDGE_CURVE` end-vertex coordinates do not lie exactly on the underlying curve at the receiver's tolerance, or whose face boundary loops are not perfectly closed.
sources: bug-reporter language: "reading a STEP file produces invalid shape", "BRepCheck reports errors after STEP import", "imported shape fails BRepCheck_Analyzer". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Reading a structurally valid STEP file produces an invalid `TopoDS_Shape`

category: §12.4 tolerance & numerical precision (sub-class: importer ignores file tolerance)
description: `UncertaintyMeasureWithUnit::Load` parses the file's declared tolerance (e.g. 1.0E-6 mm) into the in-memory model, but no downstream BRL-CAD consumer ever reads it back: `AdvancedFace` and the trim/edge tolerance machinery uses a hard-coded `m_tolerance = 1e-3`. This umbrellas the specific manifestation N019 (offset-surface case) into the broader rule: **every** tolerance-sensitive operation in step-g uses the same hard-coded constant, regardless of what the file says. Sub-tolerance features collapse, slivers get crushed, and tight-precision authoring intent is silently downgraded to the importer's working precision.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; every importer must consult the active `GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` and pass the file's tolerance into all edge/face/healing tolerance slots; emit `W_TOLERANCE_FROM_FILE` so users can confirm the value used.
notes: **See also**: N019, U033. Umbrella over N019 (which is the offset-surface specific manifestation). Synonyms: "STEP UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT ignored", "importer hard-codes 1e-3 tolerance", "distance_accuracy_value not consumed", "BRL-CAD step-g ignores file uncertainty everywhere", "tight-precision authoring downgraded to working precision". **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({heal}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers enforcing the spec must heal this fixture.
reproducer: `#13=UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(LENGTH_MEASURE(1.0E-6), #10, 'distance_accuracy_value', '');` plus `#14=(GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT(3) GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT((#13)) GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT((#10,#11,#12)) REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT('','3D'));`. step-g treats every edge with 1e-3 tolerance, ignoring the 1e-6 declared by the file.
sender: Aerospace, optics, and metrology producers that emit `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(LENGTH_MEASURE(<tight value>), MM, …, 'distance_accuracy_value', '')` in `GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` to declare that they author at sub-micrometre precision.
sources: BRL-CAD `src/conv/step/step-g/UncertaintyMeasureWithUnit.cpp` Load stores value with no consumer

bug-reporter language: "STEP file declares 1e-6 mm tolerance, importer uses 1e-3", "UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT ignored", "kernel hard-codes its own tolerance ignoring the file's distance_accuracy_value".
title: File-supplied `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` parsed but never consumed (BRL-CAD step-g)

description: InTolerance filters vertices by tolerance range [valmin, valmax] using an inverted comparison (tol >= valmax) instead of the correct (tol <= valmax). This contradicts the FACE and EDGE branches which correctly use (tol <= valmax), causing in-range vertices to be rejected while out-of-range vertices are selected.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject the inverted comparison; filter vertices with (tol >= valmin && tol <= valmax) consistently with FACE/EDGE branches
reproducer: Call InTolerance(shape, 0.001, 0.002, TopAbs_VERTEX) on a shape with vertices at tol=0.0015 (in-range) and tol=0.005 (out-of-range). Buggy result returns only the 0.005 vertex; correct result returns only the 0.0015 vertex.
title: ShapeAnalysis_ShapeTolerance.InTolerance vertex polarity inversion

description: Direct BRep_TEdge::Tolerance() write at line 1168 bypasses the SetMaxTolerance API cap when computed tolerance exceeds the user-specified limit. The static_cast and raw TShape mutation circumvent the validation that UpdateEdge would perform, violating the API contract that SetMaxTolerance(cap) enforces cap on all merged edges.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject raw tolerance write; enforce SetMaxTolerance cap via UpdateEdge API or nullify edge if tolerance exceeds cap
notes: The `N052.stp` fixture documents the input geometry but the defect only manifests when paired with the `SetMaxTolerance(0.01)` runtime API call above. A passive STEP loader will not trigger the bypass; the consuming test harness must invoke `BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing` with an explicit cap. **See also**: N055.
reproducer: Construct two faces meeting at edges that need sewing with non-trivial discretized-curve tolerance path. Call `BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing sw; sw.SetMaxTolerance(0.01); sw.Add(shape); sw.Perform();` — when computed tolerance (0.05) exceeds cap, raw write at line 1168 creates edge with 0.05 tolerance, bypassing cap. Expected: cap enforcement nullifies edge or rejects computation.
title: BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing.SameParameterEdge SetMaxTolerance bypass

description: AddTolerance accumulates tolerance array myTols[0..2] with asymmetric comparisons: myTols[0] (minimum) checked with > operator (upper-bound semantics) while myTols[2] (maximum) checked with < operator (lower-bound semantics). This inverts the intended meaning of min/max boundaries, causing in-range tolerances to be rejected when the asymmetry dominates.
expected_kernel_behavior: apply symmetric comparisons consistently: both array elements checked with same directional logic relative to bounds
reproducer: Call AddTolerance on shape with edge tolerance 0.0015 and bounds [0.001, 0.002]. Asymmetric comparisons (myTols[0] > cmin vs myTols[2] < cmax) cause nondeterministic rejection despite in-range value.
title: ShapeAnalysis_ShapeTolerance.AddTolerance polarity asymmetry

description: When face parameter evaluation fails or face context is null, CheckVertexTolerance computes vertex tolerance using only single-surface geometry. For vertices shared between multiple surfaces with different curvatures, single-surface evaluation underestimates required tolerance. The computed value accounts only for proximity to one surface, omitting contributions from adjacent surfaces.
expected_kernel_behavior: accept edge if both surfaces available; reject or escalate tolerance if single-surface evaluation only; signal ambiguity
reproducer: Create edge shared between plane and cylindrical surfaces. Vertex at intersection. Call FixVertexTolerance with face context=null. Single-surface (plane only) tolerance computed as 0.001; correct tolerance should be ≥0.002 accounting for both plane and cylinder.
title: ShapeFix_Edge.FixVertexTolerance multi-surface underestimation

description: LimitTolerance permits tmax >= tmin, allowing equality case tmax == tmin. When bounds are equal, newtol selection logic becomes nondeterministic: clamping to tmin vs tmax yields identical result but the invariant tmin < tmax (strict ordering) is violated. Downstream code assumes strict ordering; equality case creates ambiguity in tolerance domain membership.
expected_kernel_behavior: require strict ordering (tmin < tmax); reject or error on tmin == tmax; enforce at API boundary before tolerance selection
notes: The `N055.stp` fixture provides the input shape but the bug is in the `LimitTolerance` API's parameter validation — only a runtime caller passing `tmin == tmax` will exercise the buggy clamp logic. The catalog entry's "Reproducer recipe" line is the canonical paired test. **See also**: N052.
reproducer: Load `N055.stp` then call `ShapeFix_ShapeTolerance st; st.LimitTolerance(shape, 0.002, 0.002, TopAbs_VERTEX);` with the loaded shape. Condition (tmax >= tmin) is satisfied; newtol selection at lines 47-50 cannot decide whether to clamp to tmin or tmax (they are equal). Expected: validation error for tmin >= tmax.
title: ShapeFix_ShapeTolerance.LimitTolerance boundary ambiguity
