description: A CIRCLE entity has radius 5.5; one EDGE_CURVE references it under an identity transform, another under a containing 0.855x scale → effective radius 4.7. Receivers that read the basis radius rather than computing the post-transform radius display the wrong measurement.
expected_kernel_behavior: measure derivation must compute post-transform geometry; never assume basis radius equals world-space radius.
notes: Synonyms: "FreeCAD Quick Measure wrong radius", "shared CIRCLE basis EDGE_CURVE scale", "STEP measure derivation wrong", "circle basis vs containing scale", "Quick Measure 5.5 vs 4.7 radius".
reproducer: CIRCLE('shared_basis_r5_5', plc, 5.5) referenced by two EDGE_CURVEs with a comment documenting the second one's containing-scale.
sources: Pattern-mined from FreeCAD/FreeCAD#17201 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: Quick Measure reports radius `5.5 mm` for a face whose actual radius is `4.7 mm`. Onshape/Fusion read it correctly. The two EDGE_CURVEs share a CIRCLE basis but one is trimmed/scaled inconsistently relative to its containing transformation.
title: Shared CIRCLE basis between EDGE_CURVEs at different scales (radius derivation defect)

description: Two `VERTEX_POINT`s referenced by an end-to-end edge pair are positioned 5e-5 mm apart in 3D. The file declares `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(LENGTH_MEASURE(1.0E-3))`. A receiver honouring the declared tolerance treats the vertices as coincident and the wire as closed. A receiver hardcoding `Precision::Confusion()` (~1e-7) treats the vertices as distinct and the wire as a free-edge defect (also called "naked edge" or "open boundary"). The file is simultaneously valid and invalid depending on tolerance interpretation; a classic round-trip time bomb where re-saving under stricter precision turns a clean import into a leaky shell.
expected_kernel_behavior: produce a consistent result regardless of tolerance setting within the documented operating range; either honour the declared uncertainty and treat the vertices as coincident, or reject the file with a diagnostic naming the gap distance vs. working precision. The result must not silently flip between "closed shell" and "open shell" on tolerance reconfiguration.
notes: **See also**: N001, N010. Symptoms searchable as "STEP file looks. Synonyms: "gap closed at coarse tolerance opens at fine tolerance", "vertex gap depends on which tolerance you measure with", "model passes at 1e-3 fails at 1e-7", "tolerance choice flips connectivity". fine in viewer A but leaks in viewer B", "non-watertight after re-import", "tolerance round-trip regression". **OCC behavior**: silently accepts the file under default working precision and produces the open-shell interpretation without surfacing the gap-vs-tolerance disagreement; kernel mishandling; the catalog above requires a consistent result with diagnostic if interpretation flips.
reproducer: Two `EDGE_CURVE`s sharing an endpoint logically but with separate `VERTEX_POINT`s 5e-5 mm apart; declared `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` is 1e-3. Wrap in a minimal PRODUCT chain so the receiver sees a topology to walk.
title: Sub-tolerance vertex gap that closes at 1e-3 but yawns open at 1e-7

description: Inverse of Tb001. Vertices are 5e-5 mm apart but the file declares `1e-7` uncertainty. A 1e-7 receiver treats them as separate (which the input is honestly representing). A receiver that loosens tolerance to 1e-3 — for example a downstream Boolean engine that uses `tol*1000` for fuzzy operations — folds them together and silently changes the topology (shared edge becomes single edge, two faces become one). The "fix" applied by the lax tolerance receiver actively corrupts the input.
expected_kernel_behavior: produce a consistent result regardless of tolerance setting; if the kernel relaxes tolerance for any operation, it must flag the topology change and not silently merge entities the input declared distinct.
notes: **See also**: Tb001. Searchable as "Boolean op silently merged. Synonyms: "gap closed at fine tolerance grows at coarse tolerance", "coarse tolerance creates gap that fine doesn't see", "1e-3 reader sees gap that 1e-7 doesn't", "tolerance setting changes connectivity". separate features", "two edges became one after import".
reproducer: Two `VERTEX_POINT`s at (0,0,0) and (5e-5,0,0) on separate `EDGE_CURVE`s; `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` is 1e-7. Wrap in PRODUCT chain.
title: Sub-tolerance vertex gap that closes at 1e-7 but inflates at 1e-3

description: A face declares uncertainty 1e-4 mm, an edge declares 1e-5 mm, a vertex declares 1e-6 mm — the OCCT-style invariant `tol(V) <= tol(E) <= tol(F)` holds. The receiver imports the file and internally scales coordinates from mm to m (factor 1e-3). The numeric tolerance values, if naively divided by 1000, become 1e-7, 1e-8, 1e-9 — but if the receiver also applies a working-precision floor (e.g. `max(tol, 1e-9)`), the floor flattens the small ones and inverts the hierarchy. Or the receiver may not scale tolerances at all, leaving them in source units while geometry is in target units. Same input, two different scaling policies, two different post-import hierarchies.
expected_kernel_behavior: produce a consistent hierarchy regardless of internal unit scaling; either rescale tolerances atomically with coordinates, or document a single canonical working-unit and reject input that cannot survive the conversion.
notes: **See also**: N001, U001. Searchable as "tolerance hierarchy. Synonyms: "tolerance hierarchy flips when scaled to meters", "uncertainty values change order under unit change", "vertex/edge/face hierarchy inverts on unit conversion", "scaling breaks tolerance ordering". violated after metric conversion", "STEP unit conversion broke tolerances".
reproducer: A `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` with three `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` records (1e-6, 1e-5, 1e-4) labelled vertex/edge/face. The file's `LENGTH_UNIT` is `.MILLI.METRE.`. Receiver may rescale to `.METRE.`.
title: Vertex-edge-face tolerance hierarchy holds in mm but inverts in m

description: Variant of Tb003 with a non-decimal scale factor. Same hierarchy invariant in mm; the file is converted on import to inches (factor 25.4). Floating-point round-off during the multiplication leaves tolerances at unequal numbers of significant digits, and the strict hierarchy ordering may be violated by ULP-scale drift. A vertex tolerance was 1.000e-6 mm, an edge tolerance was 1.001e-6 mm; after `*25.4` they may end up `2.54e-5` and `2.54254e-5`, but with a kernel that round-trips through `float32` for some fields the equality flips.
expected_kernel_behavior: hierarchy invariant must be preserved across unit conversion; if precision is insufficient to preserve it, reject the input or widen the inflated tolerance to absorb the conversion drift, and emit a warning.
notes: Synonyms: "tolerance hierarchy inverts under inch conversion", "non-decimal scale flips uncertainty ordering", "inch unit breaks vertex/edge tolerance ratio", "tolerance hierarchy fails after mm-to-inch conversion".
reproducer: Three uncertainties at 1.000e-6, 1.001e-6, 1.002e-6 in mm-declared file with hierarchy invariant just barely holding; wrap in PRODUCT chain.
title: Vertex-edge-face hierarchy holds in mm but inverts when scaled to inches

description: Many kernel algorithms compare *areas* to `tol*tol` rather than `tol`. A planar face with side length 3e-4 mm has area 9e-8 mm². The file declares `tol = 1e-4`; a kernel that filters degenerate faces with `area < tol*tol = 1e-8` keeps it. If the kernel later uses `tol = 1e-3` (for example, after a heal that bumped tolerance), the threshold becomes `tol*tol = 1e-6`, and the face is now sub-threshold and silently dropped. A face that survives one Boolean pass disappears in the next.
expected_kernel_behavior: face-area thresholds should be derived from a documented invariant (e.g. minimum-feature-size) rather than `tol*tol`; a face that is non-degenerate at one tolerance must remain non-degenerate at any other tolerance within the operating range. Silent drop of an "infinitesimal" face is unacceptable; reject loudly or preserve the face.
notes: Searchable as "face disappeared after Boolean", "small feature. Synonyms: "small-face check uses tol*tol instead of tol", "kernel compares area to squared tolerance", "linear feature dropped under squared comparison", "face area threshold inconsistent with linear tolerance". silently removed", "ShapeFix dropped my face".
reproducer: A small planar `ADVANCED_FACE` (3e-4 × 3e-4 mm) on a `PLANE`, wrapped in a closed shell so OCCT can transfer; declared uncertainty 1e-4. Wrap in PRODUCT chain so tier-3 can compute area.
title: Face area sub-tolerance squared (`tol*tol` threshold defect)

description: Sister to Tb005 but in pcurve space. Pcurve domain length is the parameter range; some kernels test pcurve degeneracy by comparing parameter range to `tol*tol_param`. A pcurve with parameter range 1e-4 on a face with declared `tol = 1e-3` is alive at `tol_param = sqrt(tol) ≈ 3.16e-2` but degenerate at `tol_param = tol*tol = 1e-6` (different sign/squareroot policies). Receiver A keeps the edge; receiver B drops it.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize the pcurve degeneracy criterion to a single documented invariant; preserve consistency across re-imports.
notes: Synonyms: "pcurve length below tol*tol", "edge length squared comparison in 2D", "pcurve domain length squared vs linear tolerance", "small edge dropped under squared 2D check".
reproducer: An `EDGE_CURVE` on an `ADVANCED_FACE` with a `SURFACE_CURVE.associated_geometry` `PCURVE` whose parameter range is exactly 1e-4 in the U direction; declared uncertainty 1e-3.
title: Edge length sub-tolerance squared in 2D pcurve length

category: §12.2b (sub-class: knot-multiplicity × tolerance) — placed in §12.4 via `Tb` prefix because the *trigger* is tolerance interpretation, not NURBS topology.
description: A `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` has knot vector `(0.0, 1e-8, 1.0)` with multiplicities `(degree+1, 1, degree+1)`. A receiver that collapses near-equal knots within `Precision::PConfusion()` (~1e-9) preserves the inner knot. A receiver collapsing within `Precision::Confusion()` (~1e-7) merges it into the leading knot, effectively raising leading multiplicity by 1 and degenerating the curve start. The B-spline curve has different topology (knot count, control point relevance) under the two regimes.
expected_kernel_behavior: knot-equivalence threshold must be derived from a documented invariant; the curve evaluator must produce identical geometry under both interpretations or reject the input as ambiguous.
notes: **See also**: Gn001, Gn003. Searchable as "B-spline knot. Synonyms: "B-spline knots differ below tolerance", "knot collapses under fuzzy compare", "NURBS knot quantum below working precision", "indistinguishable knots in B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS". collapsed unexpectedly", "different curve in different viewers".
reproducer: Cubic `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` with knots `(0.0, 1e-8, 1.0)`, multiplicities `(4, 1, 4)`, five control points; wrap in a `TRIMMED_CURVE` and a minimal PRODUCT-bound shape representation.
title: NURBS knot-difference quantum below tolerance: knot collapses or doesn't

description: Like Tb007 but the knot vector is scaled; knots `(0.0, 1e-2, 1.0e6)`. The inner knot is "tiny" against the full range (relative spacing ~1e-8) but "large" in absolute terms (1e-2). A receiver using *absolute* parametric tolerance keeps the knot; a receiver using *relative* parametric tolerance (knot-spacing / range) drops it. The same curve evaluates differently under the two policies. Producers that emit large parametric domains (often from re-parameterization or splice operations) hit this regularly.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize to a single documented policy (absolute or relative) for knot-equivalence; the policy is transparently emitted in diagnostics.
notes: **See also**: Tb007. Synonyms: "knot tolerance scaled by parametric range", "absolute knot tolerance wrong on stretched parameter", "NURBS knot comparison ignores range scaling", "stretched parameter range hides distinct knots".
reproducer: Cubic `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` with knots `(0.0, 1.0E-2, 1.0E6)` multiplicities `(4, 1, 4)`, five control points spread across the parametric range; wrap in PRODUCT chain.
title: NURBS knot-difference quantum scaled by parametric range

description: A wire's two consecutive edges cross at a separation of 3e-7 mm (well-defined and detectable by an exact-arithmetic kernel). A receiver that rounds coordinates to its working precision (1e-6) before intersection-testing sees the two edges as touching at a single point and reports the wire as simple. An exact kernel, or one with `tol < 3e-7`, reports a self-intersection. Two kernels disagree on whether the input is malformed.
expected_kernel_behavior: Warn and accept: self-intersection detection normalizes to a documented threshold, not the working precision; if the threshold is the working precision, the kernel emits a warning diagnostic that "self-intersection within working precision" is the same input class as "no self-intersection".
notes: **See also**: Twi045. Searchable as "wire ok in one tool,. Synonyms: "self-intersection rounded out at receiver precision", "near-tangent crossing lost in rounding", "wire crosses itself at sub-tolerance distance", "self-intersection visible only at full precision". self-intersecting in another", "rounded coordinates fixed self-intersection".
reproducer: Two short B-spline edges crossing in 3D at separation 3e-7 mm; declared `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` is 1e-6 (looser than the crossing). Wrap in a face with the crossing wire as `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` and a PRODUCT chain.
title: Self-intersection visible at full precision but rounded out at receiver tolerance

description: Variant of Tb009 where the rounding is done by the format-converter step (e.g. STEP → STL → STEP through a tool that uses `float` not `double`). Coordinates `(0, 0, 0)`, `(1.0000003, 0, 0)`, `(2.0000007, 0, 0)`, `(0.9999997, 0.0000003, 0)` form a near-degenerate quad whose diagonals cross. After float32 round-trip the coordinates collapse to `(0, 0, 0)`, `(1, 0, 0)`, `(2, 0, 0)`, `(1, 0, 0)`; the diagonals no longer cross because the duplicate point makes one edge zero-length. The "fix" was unintentional precision loss.
expected_kernel_behavior: Warn and accept: results normalize to be invariant under coordinate precision changes within the operating range; if not invariant, the kernel emits a warning diagnostic flagging the precision sensitivity.
notes: Synonyms: "self-intersection lost when round-tripped through float32", "float32 round-trip removes crossing", "single-precision conversion masks self-intersection", "intersection visible in double precision only".
reproducer: Quad face with above coordinates exactly; wrap in PRODUCT chain. The fixture itself uses double precision so the self-intersection is real; the time bomb is documented in the comment as "input was generated by a float32-precision producer".
title: Self-intersection that vanishes when round-tripped through float32

description: A `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` of radius 1e6 mm has period 2π·R ≈ 6.28e6. A wire's pcurve U-coordinates differ by `2π + 1e-3` between consecutive edges (one period plus a small drift). A kernel using *fixed* parametric tolerance (e.g. 1e-7 rad) rejects the seam as misaligned. A kernel using `fmod(diff, 2π)` semantics absorbs the period and reports alignment within 1e-3. The same wire is closed or not depending on whose arithmetic policy.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: seam-matching policy is documented and consistent; on a periodic surface, normalize "same modulo period" as the canonical equality.
notes: Searchable as "cylinder seam not closed", "huge cylinder broken. Synonyms: "large-radius cylinder seam matching needs scaled tolerance", "absolute tolerance too tight for large period", "seam compare ignores period scaling", "huge cylinder fails seam match under fixed tolerance". pcurve". **See also**: Twi-XX (the "wire closed in 3D, open in UV" entry).
reproducer: `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` with R = 1e6 mm; a `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` whose two consecutive `EDGE_CURVE`s have pcurve endpoints differing by exactly `2π + 1e-3` rad in U. Wrap in PRODUCT chain.
title: Periodic-surface seam matching requires period-relative tolerance

description: A `SPHERICAL_SURFACE` has a parametric singularity at the poles (V = ±π/2). A wire passing 1e-9 below V=π/2 is at the edge of the pole singularity. A kernel that snaps "near-pole" pcurves to the pole using a fixed angular tolerance (1e-7 rad) does not snap; one using a larger working tolerance (1e-3 rad) snaps the wire onto the pole and collapses the upper face. Different kernels produce a hemisphere vs. a spherical zone.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: pole-snapping is a documented invariant; the snap threshold normalizes into diagnostics, not hidden behind working precision.
notes: Synonyms: "sphere pole singularity breaks seam match", "v-parameter singular at pole", "pole singularity fails parametric tolerance", "sphere seam at pole has multi-valued UV".
reproducer: `SPHERICAL_SURFACE` with R=1; face with outer-bound wire at constant V = π/2 - 1e-9 (a near-pole circle).
title: Sphere seam matching across pole singularity

description: A `CARTESIAN_POINT` has coordinate `(1.0E-300, 0, 0)` — a denormalized double. A kernel comparing `|x| < tol` for tol=1e-7 says "yes, near zero". A kernel comparing `x*x < tol*tol = 1e-14` says `1e-600` which underflows to 0, also "yes, near zero". A kernel that flushes-to-zero in its math library may treat `1e-300` as exactly zero before any tolerance compare. A kernel without flush-to-zero may keep the value alive and trip on `1.0/(1e-300)` overflow elsewhere. The same input behaves differently depending on the host's float environment.
expected_kernel_behavior: subnormal/denormal coordinates must be rejected or normalized to a documented sentinel before downstream math; the "near zero" classification must be defined explicitly.
notes: Searchable as "NaN after import", "kernel crash on tiny. Synonyms: "coordinate at 1e-300 fails near-zero test", "denormalized math affects tolerance compare", "subnormal coordinate values affect equality", "extreme small coord triggers denormal handling". coordinate", "underflow during transform".
reproducer: `CARTESIAN_POINT('escape',(1.0E-300,0.0,0.0))` used as one vertex of a degenerate edge in a wrapped face; declared tolerance 1e-7.
title: Coordinate at 1e-300 tests as "near zero" only under denormalized math

description: A planar triangular face has internal angles of 89.9999°, 89.9999°, and 0.0002°. The 0.0002° angle equals 3.49e-6 rad. Many sliver detectors trigger at "internal angle < 1e-5 rad" (Pro/E vintage policy); some at "1e-7 rad" (precise sliver only); some at "1e-3 rad" (aggressive sliver removal). The triangle is alive in one regime and dead in another.

description: An edge has 3D length 1e-3 mm in a file with declared tolerance 1e-6. A kernel comparing `length < tol` says "alive". A kernel comparing `length < sqrt(tol) ≈ 1e-3` says "right at the boundary — ambiguous". A kernel comparing `length*length < tol` (≡ `length < sqrt(tol)`) says the same boundary. The triple ambiguity (linear, squared, square-root) means three reasonable kernels can disagree on whether the edge survives heal.

description: A wire has 1000 consecutive edges; each pair of adjacent vertices is 1e-9 mm apart in 3D against a declared tolerance of 1e-6. Each individual gap is sub-tolerance and absorbed. But the cumulative drift end-to-end is `1000 * 1e-9 = 1e-6`, exactly equal to the declared tolerance. A kernel comparing endpoint-to-endpoint declares the wire closed (or just barely not). Whether the wire is closed depends on whether the kernel sums residuals or compares only adjacent pairs.
expected_kernel_behavior: tolerance budget across N-edge chains must be documented; either reject as un-closeable, or apply a global re-stitch that distributes residual back across the chain.
notes: Searchable as "long polyline not closing", "sweep wire fails. Synonyms: "error accumulates across 1000 edges", "tolerance budget exhausted by long chain", "chained edges drift far beyond per-edge tolerance", "wire endpoints far apart due to accumulated error". to close", "cumulative tolerance error".
reproducer: Long polyline with 1000 short edges of length ~1e-3 mm each; consecutive vertices have a constant 1e-9 mm gap that always points in the same direction; closing edge declared but its 3D endpoints are at the cumulative-drifted positions.
title: Tolerance budget exhausted by accumulation across long edge chain

description: Two `ADVANCED_FACE`s (planar, parallel, same outline) are separated by exactly 1.0e-6 mm; equal to the declared tolerance. A kernel comparing strict `<` keeps them as separate faces (a thin slab). A kernel comparing `<=` merges them and the slab disappears, leaving a single face. Both interpretations are mathematically reasonable but produce different geometry.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize the equality-vs-strict-inequality choice at the tolerance boundary; tie-breaking is documented.

description: `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(LENGTH_MEASURE(0.0), ..)` declares zero tolerance. A receiver that uses the declared value verbatim performs exact-equality comparisons; any sub-bit drift is a "real" defect. A receiver that floors the working tolerance at `Precision::Confusion()` silently substitutes 1e-7 and behaves identically to a normal file. The zero declaration is a producer's request for exact arithmetic that may or may not be honoured.
expected_kernel_behavior: zero uncertainty must be either honoured (exact arithmetic enabled if available) or rejected; silently substituting a non-zero working tolerance must be flagged in diagnostics.
notes: Searchable as "zero tolerance file", "exact arithmetic STEP". Synonyms: "UNCERTAINTY value of zero", "no fuzzy compare allowed", "tolerance literally zero in file", "exact equality required by zero uncertainty".
reproducer: A simple shape (planar quad or single edge) in a PRODUCT-wrapped representation with `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(LENGTH_MEASURE(0.0), ..)`.
title: UNCERTAINTY value of exactly zero — no fuzzy compare

description: `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(LENGTH_MEASURE(1.0E-30), ..)`. The value is below any reasonable kernel's working precision. A kernel that respects the declared value tries to compare features at 1e-30 precision and rejects everything as having gaps. A kernel that floors at `Precision::Confusion()` silently uses 1e-7; the file imports cleanly but its declared expectation has been overridden. Producer and receiver silently disagree about precision.
expected_kernel_behavior: tolerance values outside the kernel's documented operating range must be flagged; either coerce-and-warn or reject-with-diagnostic; never silent substitution.
notes: **See also**: Tb018, Tb020. **OCC behavior**: silently substitutes the floored working-precision value for the absurdly-tight declared uncertainty; kernel mishandling; the catalog above forbids silent substitution. Synonyms: "uncertainty 1e-30 below working precision", "absurdly tight tolerance", "tolerance below kernel resolution", "tolerance value impossibly small".
reproducer: PRODUCT-wrapped simple shape with `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(LENGTH_MEASURE(1.0E-30), ..)`.

A kernel respecting the declaration treats every pair of vertices as coincident, every face as identical, and collapses the model to nothing. A kernel ceiling-clamping to a sane maximum (e.g. min-feature-size / 100) silently behaves normally. Receiver behaviour diverges wildly.

A kernel taking `min` (most strict) uses 1e-9. A kernel taking `max` (most lax) uses 1e-3. A kernel taking the first uses 1e-3. A kernel taking the last uses 1e-9. description: A file's `LENGTH_UNIT` declared in `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT` is `.MILLI.METRE.` (mm). The `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` uses a *different* inline `LENGTH_UNIT` of `.METRE.` (m), with value 1e-6 — that is, 1e-6 m = 1e-3 mm. A kernel that interprets the uncertainty in the context's units (mm) reads "1e-6 mm = 1 nm — hyper-precise". A kernel that follows the uncertainty's own attached unit reads "1e-6 m = 1 µm = 1000× looser". The receiver's policy on which unit binding to follow determines a 1000× difference in working tolerance — every other defect in this section becomes a different defect class.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize the unit-binding policy for tolerance per spec; each `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` carries its own unit, and receivers convert / coerce before comparing to coordinates.
notes: **See also**: U001. Searchable as "tolerance in wrong units",. "STEP file 1000× too tight or too loose".

description: A producer emits coordinates near 1e15 — for example a model whose origin sits at a real-world UTM-style position. At magnitudes near 1e15, the float64 unit-in-the-last-place is ~0.125 (the spacing between adjacent representable doubles is 2^(53-50) ≈ 2^(-2) at exponent 2^50 ≈ 1.1e15). A `LENGTH_UNIT` of `MM` plus a declared `UNCERTAINTY` of `0.001 mm` sets a kernel's working tolerance below float64's representable spacing at the model's coordinates. Vertex equality, edge connectivity, sliver-detection — every tolerance comparison is dominated by floating-point noise rather than geometric meaning. Two vertices that should be coincident at sub-tolerance distance can differ by 0.125 mm because they round to adjacent representable doubles. Bug-reporter language: "STEP coordinates near 1e15", "GIS-style absolute coords", "model far from origin loses precision", "vertices wobble at huge coords".
expected_kernel_behavior: surface the precision gap when the working tolerance is below the local ULP at the model's coordinates; recommend recentering to a local frame near the origin; reject as numerically meaningless if the user requests strict tolerance handling at far-from-origin scale.
notes: Spatial twin of Tb013 (denormalised near-zero). **See also**: Tb013. Searchable as "STEP file far-from-origin", "GIS coordinates lose precision", "absolute UTM in STEP file". Synonyms: "coordinates near 1e15 lose precision", "model placed at GIS-style absolute coordinates", "vertices wobble at huge coords", "float64 ULP exceeds declared tolerance", "model far from origin loses precision".
reproducer: a `CARTESIAN_POINT` with coordinates `(1.234567890123e15, 2.345678901234e15, 3.456789012345e15)` and a sibling point at `(1.234567890124e15, 2.345678901234e15, 3.456789012345e15)` — the two points differ by 1e3 in the original-units description but, after rounding to float64, occupy the same or adjacent representable doubles. Declared `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(LENGTH_MEASURE(0.001), MILLIMETRE)`.

sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP file with huge coordinates loses precision", "GIS-style absolute coordinates", "model far from origin is wobbly"

title: Coordinates near 1e15 where float64 ULP exceeds declared tolerance

The receiver ignores the producer's `LENGTH_UNIT` context (and any auxiliary `DIMENSIONAL_EXPONENTS` instance) and defaults to base SI.

description: A `PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT` context is declared as degrees via a `CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT('DEG',#x)` complex entity. A receiver that takes the unit declaration at face value reads 1.5708° (a tiny rotation, off by a factor of pi/180 ≈ 57.3); a receiver that hard-assumes radians for any PLANE_ANGLE_MEASURE silently produces the right number for the wrong reason. Symmetrical defect: unit declared `RADIAN` but values stored as degrees (90.0 read as 90 radians ≈ 5157°). The angular twin of U001's mm-vs-inch length defect. Bug-reporter language: "STEP rotation off by 57x", "angles too small", "PMI angle reads 1.57° not 90°", "1 radian or 1 degree?".
expected_kernel_behavior: surface the disagreement when the value's magnitude is implausible for the declared unit (e.g. an angle of 90 rad is unphysical); reject as malformed when out-of-range, or warn and convert per the declared unit. The unit declaration is authoritative; receivers that hard-assume one over the other hide the producer-side defect.
notes: Angular twin of U001 (mm vs inches). **See also**: U031, Pmi067. Synonyms: "STEP angle wrong by 57x", "deg/rad confusion", "rotation off by pi/180".
reproducer: a `PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT` context declared as `CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT('DEGREE',#refRadianMeasure)` (factor pi/180); a `MEASURE_REPRESENTATION_ITEM` carrying `PLANE_ANGLE_MEASURE(1.5708)` whose author intended 90° but emitted the radian value. Counter-fixture: `RADIAN` unit declared, value `90.0` stored.
sender: deduced — multi-source writer pipelines where one subsystem stores angle attributes in degrees and another in radians, with a single PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT context binding both

title: Plane-angle unit declared as DEGREE but values stored as radians (or vice-versa)

description: Pascal (Pa) is dimensionally `kg·m^(-1)·s^(-2)`. A producer that emits pressure as a `DERIVED_UNIT` composed of three `DERIVED_UNIT_ELEMENT` entries (mass at exponent +1, length at exponent -1, time at exponent -2) is spec-conforming but stresses receivers that pattern-match on a single named pressure unit. Defects: an element exponent is wrong (mass at exponent +2 instead of +1); the element ordering differs across files (some receivers' lookup is order-sensitive); the underlying base units mix SI prefixes inconsistently (mass in `kg`, length in `mm`; pressure becomes `kg·mm^(-1)·s^(-2)`, off by 1000× from `kg·m^(-1)·s^(-2)`). Bug-reporter language: "STEP pressure unit not recognised", "Pa from derived units", "validation property pressure 1000x wrong".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: detect / normalize the dimensional signature of pressure (mass^1 length^-1 time^-2) and bind to a Pa context regardless of element order; coerce SI prefix mismatches deterministically; warn when the composition does not reduce to a recognised SI unit.
notes: First entry exercising multi-element DERIVED_UNIT composition. **See also**: U021, U026, U041. Synonyms: "STEP pressure Pa garbled", "Pa unit not recognised from derived chain", "DERIVED_UNIT pressure 1000x wrong", "validation pressure derived unit", "Pa from kg.m^-1.s^-2 not bound".- **Byte assertion**: contains(b'DERIVED_UNIT_ELEMENT') and contains(b'DERIVED_UNIT(')
reproducer: `#1=DERIVED_UNIT_ELEMENT(#mass_unit,1.0)`, `#2=DERIVED_UNIT_ELEMENT(#length_unit,-1.0)`, `#3=DERIVED_UNIT_ELEMENT(#time_unit,-2.0)`, `#4=DERIVED_UNIT((#1,#2,#3))`. Variant fixture: length unit is millimetre (`MILLI METRE`), mass unit is kilogram, time unit is second — the composed unit is 1000× off from Pa.
sender: deduced — exporters that emit pressure as a fully-decomposed SI derived unit rather than a CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT('Pa',..) shorthand
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP pressure unit garbled", "Pa unit not recognised"
title: Pressure unit `Pa` built from a derived-unit chain (`kg / (m * s^2)`)

description: Dynamic viscosity Pa·s is `kg·m^(-1)·s^(-1)`. expected_kernel_behavior: detect the dimensional signature of dynamic viscosity (mass^1 length^-1 time^-1) and bind to a Pa·s context; never silently flatten time exponent and produce Pa.
notes: **See also**: U040. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); catalog disallows silent-accept. description: A producer-side STEP correctly declares `INCH` units with inch-scale numerical values. A receiver that hard-codes "STEP files are mm" silently treats the inch values as mm; yielding a 25.4× too-small model. Mirror image of Wr044. The on-disk file is well-formed; the bug is that some slicer lineage assumes mm regardless of the declared unit context.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: receivers MUST honour the declared `LENGTH_UNIT` context, normalize coordinate values into the kernel's canonical unit, and never assume mm without inspecting it. Reject with E_UNIT_CONTEXT_IGNORED if the unit declaration cannot be parsed; treating inch-tagged data as millimetres without diagnostic is a coverage gap.
notes: **See also**: U015, Wr044. Synonyms: "slicer ignores STEP unit declaration", "INCH unit silently treated as mm by receiver", "unit-context inversion on receiver side".
reproducer: STEP file with `LENGTH_UNIT` complex record `(LENGTH_UNIT() NAMED_UNIT(*) CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT('INCH', ..))` and `CARTESIAN_POINT` corner coordinates `(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)` (one inch — should appear as 25.4 mm to a correct receiver).
sender: STEP-receiving slicers that auto-detect unit by comparing `LENGTH_UNIT` declaration against a hard-coded "expected mm" assumption and silently flip when the file has an explicit `INCH` declaration.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP file marked inch but the model scales up in size", "model is 25.4× too big after import", "unit declaration inverted on receiver side".
title: Slicer-side unit-context inversion: STEP says mm, slicer reads as inches

category: §12.5 units & coordinate systems (sub-class: incorrect placement composition)
description: A `MAPPED_ITEM` requires composing `mapping_target / mapping_origin` to produce the placement transform. When one of the placements is left-handed (the cross product `x × y` does not point along `z`), `gp_Trsf::SetDisplacement` produces a transform that flips the orientation but leaves the geometry in the wrong half-space. The imported instance ends up mirrored or rotated 180° relative to the producer's intent.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; verify both axes orthogonality AND right-handedness when constructing transforms; emit `W_LEFT_HANDED_PLACEMENT` and either flip-and-record or reject. Never produce a silently wrong transform.
notes: **See also**: U015, U016. Synonyms: "gp_Trsf incorrect transformation between two Ax3", "left-handed placement gives wrong transform", "STEP MAPPED_ITEM placement composition wrong", "AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D handedness ignored".
reproducer: STEP file with `MAPPED_ITEM` whose `mapping_origin` is `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D(..)` with right-handed axes and `mapping_target` has axes such that `x × y ≠ z`. Imported instance is in the wrong location.
sender: STEP files with `MAPPED_ITEM` placements where the `mapping_origin` and the `mapping_target` differ in handedness (one is right-handed, the other left-handed).
sources: bug-reporter language: "gp_Trsf computes incorrect transformation between two gp_Ax3", "placement-to-placement transform is wrong", "STEP MAPPED_ITEM placement gives wrong location". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: `gp_Trsf::SetDisplacement` between two `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` records produces wrong transform

category: §12.5 units & coordinate systems (sub-class: transformation operator scale ignored)
description: The `Load` pass parses the optional `scale` REAL into a class member, but `LoadONBrep` is an unconditional stub: the scale never reaches the resulting `ON_Xform`/`gp_Trsf`. A producer's intent — "place this prototype at this location and scale it by k" — is silently lost; the located sub-shape arrives at unit scale, so a 1 inch prototype with `scale = 25.4` to make a 25.4 mm part stays 1 unit big. The reverse defect on the producer side is U015 / Wr050 (writer composes scale twice); this is the symmetric reader-side defect: scale dropped on the floor.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; `LoadONBrep` must build a uniform-scale `ON_Xform` from the parsed `scale` value; emit `W_OPERATOR_SCALE_APPLIED` diagnostic recording the factor.
notes: **See also**: U015, Wr050, M061. Synonyms: "CartesianTransformationOperator scale parsed but ignored", "STEP scale operator does nothing on import", "step-g LoadONBrep stub for transformation operator", "uniform scale 25.4 dropped by reader", "BRL-CAD subassembly arrives unit scale despite operator scale".
reproducer: `#100=CARTESIAN_TRANSFORMATION_OPERATOR_3D('inch_to_mm', #11, #12, #10, 25.4, #13);` referenced as a transformation between two `REPRESENTATION_RELATIONSHIP_WITH_TRANSFORMATION` representations. step-g loads but does not apply `scale`.
sender: STEP producers that emit `CARTESIAN_TRANSFORMATION_OPERATOR_3D` with a non-unit `scale` attribute to convert sub-component units (e.g. inch-prototype scaled to mm by `scale = 25.4`), or that scale a per-instance copy of a shared prototype.
sources: BRL-CAD `src/conv/step/step-g/CartesianTransformationOperator.cpp` `Load` reads optional `scale` REAL attribute then `LoadONBrep` is a stub that prints `"::LoadONBrep(..) not implemented for <entity>"`

title: `CARTESIAN_TRANSFORMATION_OPERATOR` `scale` attribute parsed but never applied (BRL-CAD step-g)

description: STEP exports either reuse one sub-model for many capacitors etc. (KiCad), or emit the same physical component as multiple distinct `PRODUCT_DEFINITION`s (one per sub-assembly use site). Receivers keyed on label-as-primary-key (CadQuery) raise ValueError; AutoCAD reports "Duplicate Definition of Block 1 ignored". FreeCAD silently appends an index.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept duplicates by treating entity IDs (`#NNN`) as primary keys; names are descriptive; disambiguate names on import; never fail on duplicates. Detect by-geometry duplicates; offer to deduplicate on import.
notes: **See also**: N044. Synonyms: "two parts with same name confused on import", "PRODUCT name collision between subassemblies", "duplicate component names cause wrong wiring", "import merges differently-located parts that share a name".
reproducer: STEP with N NAUO rows referencing one PRODUCT named "Cap"; load via `cadquery.Assembly.load`. Or 1000 distinct PRODUCTs named "Bolt_001" with bit-identical geometry.
sender: KiCad STEP writer; large-assembly producers that emit one PRODUCT per use site instead of reusing one PRODUCT with N NAUOs.
sources: I021/I077 (CadQuery on KiCad mobo-3D), J018 (SolidWorks/AutoCAD "Duplicate Definition of Block"), V050.
title: Naming collision: same component referenced by colliding `PRODUCT.name` across sub-assemblies

description: External-file-assignment whose target path resolves to the main file under translation; reader loops forever. Or cyclic `#A=(B(..) C(#A))` complex entity referencing itself; semantic resolver follows `#A → #A` ad infinitum.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect identity by canonical path; skip self-reference; Tarjan-style cycle detection during reference resolution; reject with E_REFERENCE_CYCLE.
notes: **See also**: Pf010, Ad052, M060. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant. Synonyms: "external reference points back to itself", "cyclic file dependency in assembly", "STEP file references its own product", "external-anchor loop crashes reader".
reproducer: `APPLIED_EXTERNAL_IDENTIFICATION_ASSIGNMENT` to same `.step` file path; or `#1=(NAMED_UNIT(*) SI_UNIT(..) DERIVED_UNIT_ELEMENT(#1, 1.0))`.
sources: G032 (OCCT 2547d97 / Mantis 0031711), A004 (cyclic complex-entity reference graph).
title: Self-reference / cyclic external file reference

description: `APPLIED_EXTERNAL_IDENTIFICATION_ASSIGNMENT` paths don't exist; OCCT silently fails resolution but Transfer() returns success. AP242 supports referencing geometric elements (face, edge) in a separate Part 21 file via External Element Reference / DDP linking. When the package is repacked or split, the references break.
expected_kernel_behavior: try alternate paths from `DOCUMENT_FILE`; report failure honestly; archive-stable requires DDP integrity check; reject if cross-file refs do not resolve.
notes: **See also**: M008, Pmi065. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant. Synonyms: "STEP reader returns success even when external file missing", "no error when referenced subassembly file is absent", "silent partial-load on missing externals", "reader treats missing referenced file as OK".
reproducer: STEP assembly whose `APPLIED_EXTERNAL_IDENTIFICATION_ASSIGNMENT` paths don't exist on disk; or a DDP archive where `assembly.stp` references face #47 in `part_3.stp`; rename `part_3.stp`.
sources: G082 (OCCT 3b7f55e / Mantis 0029873), W048 (Datakit AP242 federation), M030 (DDP cross-file refs).
title: STEP assembly reader returns success even when external-reference files are missing

description: For each entity instance there must be at most one EXTERNAL_ANCHOR; every EXTERNAL_ANCHOR must reference exactly one data-section entity. Writers that copy anchors duplicate them. Source files containing `externally_defined_representation_item` must wrap them in a placeholder `externally_defined_representation`. When the assembly tree is split per-level, the same leaf part may be referenced from multiple sub-assembly files with divergent `product.id`.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject duplicate anchors; reject orphan externally-defined items; surface PDM mismatch when same product diverges across files.
notes: **OCC behavior**: emits a diagnostic but produces no shape (warn-and-proceed by oracle, but result is empty); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant. Synonyms: "external anchor points to multiple entities", "EXTERNAL_ANCHOR uniqueness violated", "orphan EER source references", "non-1:1 anchor mapping breaks resolution".
reproducer: `!EXTERNAL_ANCHOR('AAA', #100); !EXTERNAL_ANCHOR('BBB', #100);`. Or `externally_defined_representation_item` whose `source` is set but is not contained inside any `externally_defined_representation`.
sender: per-level split assembly writers; tools that copy anchors when re-exporting.
sources: CAx-IF EER §7.3.1 (entry from 02-caxif: "EXTERNAL_ANCHOR uniqueness rule"), CAx-IF EER §7.3.2 (entry from 02-caxif: "EER source file must include placeholder representation"), CAx-IF EER §6.4 ("Nested external references").
title: EXTERNAL_ANCHOR uniqueness (1:1 anchor↔entity) violated; orphan EER source

description: UDAs at the assembly-instance level can be attached to NAUOs or to MLRDs (multi-level paths). They must be counted at the product representing their context node. Some receivers ignore MLRD-attached UDAs entirely.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept by walking both NAUO and MLRD attachments when counting per-context UDAs; must not silently ignore MLRD-attached UDAs.
notes: **See also**: A029. Synonyms: "user-defined attribute on multi-level path ignored", "MLRD attribute dropped on import", "UDA on nested-instance reference designator lost", "deep-path attribute not preserved".
reproducer: AS1 with one UDA on the NAUO from AS1 to L-Bracket-Assembly, and one UDA on the MLRD from AS1 to a specific Nut instance.
title: UDA on multi-level reference designator (MLRD) ignored

description: A component carries a placement transform attached at the face / edge / vertex level rather than at the assembly node, and the writer's component-attribution path expects identity transforms on leaf subshapes. Names, colors, and other attached metadata bound to the inner subshape are lost in the STEP round-trip, or end up bound to the wrong product instance. Symptom: a translated/rotated component reimports as untitled, uncoloured geometry; or nested compounds (Root → Arm → Cube) drop their inner-level labels.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: preserve component metadata across round-trip regardless of where the transform is attached. Either coerce the subshape transform into the underlying surface/curve before write, or fold the metadata down to the level where the writer can attach it. Identity-collapsing on read keeps round-trips stable. Must not silently lose metadata.
notes: **See also**: A024. Synonyms: "subshape colors disappear when component has location", "labels lost on transformed sub-shape", "XCAF attributes stripped when location is non-identity", "color on subshape lost after round-trip with placement".
reproducer: face with a non-identity transform reinserted into a shell; export to STEP; reimport and observe a near-identity transform on the leaf face plus missing color/name attributes. Or build a two-level Compound (Root → Arm → Cube) and observe inner-level labels missing from the resulting STEP file.
sources: I033 (build123d #1014: Pos*Rot drops labels), I036 (build123d #954: nested compound labels via STEPControl_Writer), I006 (OCCT #541: STEP re-export loses XCAF colors), F056/F084/B028 (orphan TopLoc_Location on subshapes), B001 (spurious face-level locations from STEP round-trip).
title: Component labels/colors/names lost when subshape carries a transform on round-trip

description: When color is overridden at assembly node level (not part level), STEP writers emit per-part STYLED_ITEM rather than per-instance, so receivers see all instances colored alike. Or per-face STYLED_ITEM chains land at the wrong scope (top-level shape-rep instead of per-`SOLID_MODEL`). Multiple `MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION` chains may contradict on the same STYLED_ITEM. When nested compound is flattened/copied, inner STYLED_ITEM is dropped entirely.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: STYLED_ITEM must attach to MAPPED_ITEM-level instances; prefer most-specific styled-item; fall back to next ancestor; never inherit from sibling sub-assembly; propagate STYLED_ITEM through every level of NAUO during flatten.
notes: **See also**: A019, A020, M039, M040, M042. Synonyms: "assembly-level color override lost on import", "STYLED_ITEM at wrong scope ignored", "component color binding misplaced", "color override applied at wrong assembly level".
reproducer: assembly with a top-level color override; export. Verify whether STYLED_ITEM attaches to MAPPED_ITEM-level instances or only to SHAPE_REPRESENTATION. Or build a one-level vs two-level wrapped product and flatten via `XCAFDoc_ShapeTool::CopyShape`.
sources: V046 (SolidWorks assembly-level color), V047 (per-face color → white), V048 (Inventor strips appearances), G097 (OCCT root-label color), J008 (Onshape Apr-2024 pipeline), Y004 (KiCad nested STYLED_ITEM lost on flatten), W024 (HOOPS material merging).
title: STYLED_ITEM at wrong scope: assembly-level color override lost or misbound

description: Multiple distinct face colours in the producer become identical white in the consumer. Per-face colours are bound via `STYLED_ITEM` / `PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT` / `SURFACE_STYLE_FILL_AREA` / `FILL_AREA_STYLE_COLOUR` chains. Common signature: three `ADVANCED_FACE` instances all share the same supporting `PLANE` (e.g. `#64`) but each has its own distinct `STYLED_ITEM` / `COLOUR_RGB`; XCAF risks merging the faces (since they overlap geometrically) and collapsing the per-face colour binding. After re-tessellation or face-merge healing the binding is lost. Non-manifold STEP reader path skips XCAF attribute application.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: honor face-bound colour_assignment without normalizing; re-bind to surviving merged face when possible; bind style to tessellated shape; apply colors/styles on non-manifold path. Must not silently collapse colours.
notes: **See also**: A018, M020, M042, M045, N003. Synonyms: "all faces become one color after import", "face colors lost on round-trip", "uniform white instead of per-face hues", "per-face STYLED_ITEM collapsed to single color", "shared plane causes color merge across faces".
reproducer: Face with full styled_item chain on COLOUR_RGB(0.8,0.1,0.1); subject to sliver-face removal and re-export.
sources: V047 (CATIA → SolidWorks all white), W024 (HOOPS face-level styling), M032 (CAx-IF styling RP), R063 (OCCT bug33317 reference shape color), G036 (tessellated face style binding), G098 (OCCT non-manifold loses attributes).
title: Per-face `STYLED_ITEM` colours collapse to a single hue when multiple `ADVANCED_FACE`s share one supporting `PLANE`

description: Inventor emits `STYLED_ITEM` entities not parented under `MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION` or `DRAUGHTING_MODEL`; older readers skipped them, dropping all colors. Variant: `STYLED_ITEM.item` is NULL or its `PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT.styles` set has NULL elements.
expected_kernel_behavior: Accept bare styled items with a warning; null-check PSA styles; skip NULL silently. Do not reject this pattern.
notes: **See also**: A018, M039, M040. Synonyms: "STYLED_ITEM at top level has no parent draughting model", "bare style entity orphaned in file", "MDGPR / DRAUGHTING_MODEL parent missing for style", "color entity unbound from any view or model".
reproducer: STEP file with bare STYLED_ITEM at top level; or `STYLED_ITEM(name,(..),#null)`.
sender: Autodesk Inventor 2014.
sources: G003 (OCCT ec661e4 / Mantis 0024159), G027 (NULL STYLED_ITEM.item), G063 (PSA NULL handle).
title: Bare STYLED_ITEM at top level (no MDGPR / DRAUGHTING_MODEL parent)

cross_oracle_note: pure-Python Part-21 validator accepts (`accept`); OCCT crashes (`signal(11)`). The crash is on the kernel side; the file is spec-conformant Part-21.
description: Hiding or restyling a single assembly component within a Saved View uses `context_dependent_over_riding_styled_item` whose `style_context` mixes one `mapped_item` with one or more `representation_relationship`s. This violates CDORSI WR1 ("only one rep_item OR all are mapped_items OR all are representation_relationships"). The recommendation is to do it anyway.
expected_kernel_behavior: Warn and accept this pattern despite the WR1 violation; do not reject.
notes: Cross-oracle: pure-Python Part-21 validator accepts (`accept`); OCCT crashes (`signal(11)`). The crash is on the kernel side; the file is spec-conformant Part-21.
reproducer: Two-level assembly; Saved View where one leaf component is hidden by a CDORSI whose `style_context` is `(mapped_item, representation_relationship_1, representation_relationship_2)`.
title: CDORSI WR1 violated by per-component styling in Saved View

description: Multiple `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT` instances with identical names but different visibility flags collide; OCCT did not differentiate them. Empty PLA caused exception. Some producers (CST) use PLA to encode physical-group / material semantics rather than visibility, which OCCT XCAF only honors for visibility, silently dropping material data.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: group layers by (name, visibility) tuple; surface PLA names as queryable group attributes; accept empty PLA.
notes: **See also**: M043, M044, M046. Synonyms: "two layers with the same name collide", "PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT name conflicts", "layer namespace clashes between subassemblies", "duplicate layer names confuse reader".
reproducer: STEP with two `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT` of identical name but different visibility flags. Or `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT('Copper', 'meshable', (#42, #43))` referencing shells.
sources: G110 (OCCT 96049f2 / Mantis 0032049: layers with empty/identical names), G049 (empty PLA), Y014 (CST Microwave Studio uses PLA for materials), R060 (layers count mis-read).
title: PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT collisions / namespace abuse

description: To include part geometry in a Saved View's `draughting_model`, a `mapped_item` plus a `representation_map` must be used. The `axis2_placement_3d` referenced as `mapping_source`/`mapping_origin` MUST be a unit identity transform. Files that put a non-identity transform inadvertently move the geometry only in that view. Variants: MAPPED_ITEM with unrecognized location (location dropped); writer skips MAPPED_ITEM with non-rigid (scaling) transform.
expected_kernel_behavior: validate identity transforms on saved-view mapped items; reject scaling on assembly mapped items, or heal by collapsing the non-identity transform on saved-view mapped items.
notes: Synonyms: "Saved View mapped_item must be identity but isn't", "non-identity transform on representation_map for Saved View", "Saved View mapping_origin not unit transformation".
reproducer: Saved view's mapped_item has `mapping_source = AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D(P0=(10,0,0), Z=(0,0,1), X=(1,0,0))` instead of unit identity.
sources: CAx-IF PMI v4.1 §9.4.2.1 (entry from 02-caxif), Q031 (MAPPED_ITEM unrecognized location), Q084 (mapped_item with scaling).
title: Mapped_item / representation_map identity transform requirement (Saved Views)

description: A `MAPPED_ITEM`'s target `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` uses `DIRECTION` axes that form a left-handed (mirrored) frame; for example Z=(0,0,1) and X=(-1,0,0), so the implicit Y=Z×X=(0,-1,0) gives a negative-determinant placement. Shape locations containing scale or mirror are sources of invalid STEP/IGES output: the mirrored instance is exported with a copy whose orientation is silently corrected, flipping handedness. When "Export parameter space curves" is enabled and the block instance has negative-determinant transform, surfaces import with reversed normals.
expected_kernel_behavior: bake the scale/mirror into geometry changes before STEP write (purging the negative-determinant placement) rather than emitting it as a transform STEP cannot losslessly carry; preserve handedness by flipping face normals coherently; flip pcurve orientation when emitting from a mirrored instance. Or reject the input as un-exportable.
notes: **See also**: A017, Pmi068, Tsh033. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant. Synonyms: "MAPPED_ITEM transform has negative determinant", "left-handed frame in component placement", "mirrored axis placement in MAPPED_ITEM", "improper rotation on assembly transform".
reproducer: Shape with `gp_Trsf` containing scale or mirror; export. Or Rhino model with block instance scaled `(-1,1,1)` exported with pcurves on.
sources: G061 (OCCT 9592ae2 / Mantis 0027457 — BRepTools_PurgeLocations), W039 (HOOPS Exchange Parasolid mirrored MAPPED_ITEM), K017 (Rhino mirrored block + pcurve flip), J006 (Onshape post-rotation disintegration).
title: `MAPPED_ITEM` `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` with left-handed (mirrored, negative-determinant) frame

description: STEP `name` fields contain ISO 10303-21 control directives, raw 8-bit Cyrillic/CJK/CP850 bytes, doubled apostrophes (`''` for "O'Brien"), backslashes (Windows paths), or single-space placeholders; receivers either fail to decode, replace with `?`, drop the name, or trim whitespace too aggressively.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: decode all 10303-21 directives; provide `read.step.codepage` parameter; preserve literal backslashes through encode/decode; standard doubled-quote escape parsing; trim whitespace before assigning names but preserve the original. Must not silently corrupt names.
notes: **See also**: A010, U016. Synonyms: "non-ASCII component name garbled on import", "Unicode characters in part name corrupted", "Part 21 backslash-X encoding not decoded", "special characters in NAUO instance name lost", "Chinese / Japanese / German labels broken on round-trip".
reproducer: PRODUCT name `'\X2\03B1\X0\'` (Greek alpha); or `PRODUCT('O''Brien',..)`; or `PRODUCT(' ',..)`; or `PRODUCT('C:\path\file',..)`.
sender: SolidWorks (Chinese/Japanese locales); Inventor (locale-dependent codepages); Pro/E and Inventor with control-directive names.
sources: G040 (control directives in names), G041 (cp1251/GB2312/DOS850), G042 (Japanese), G043 (embedded apostrophes), G044 (single space), G045 (backslashes), R052/R053 (OCCT bug25440/bug33815), J004 (FreeCAD GH#7987), W031 (CAD Exchanger).
title: Names with special / non-ASCII / encoded characters lost or corrupted

description: STEP-assembly reader performance degrades quadratically with assembly size — entity-name lookup runs as a nested scan. Common stress shape: a wide assembly with many sibling `NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE` instances (e.g. 24 NAUOs) all referencing the same single leaf `PRODUCT_DEFINITION` (e.g. `#32`) — building the name-to-shape map for 10k faces takes ~45 minutes versus ~2 min for the read itself. Importer hangs at "X%" for many minutes and may appear stalled. The shell-orientation healing pass during read is also a known multiplier on top.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept by indexing entity IDs once at parse and using indexed lookup, not nested scan; bound healing loops by entity count; expose costly orientation-healing work as opt-in / progress-reportable. Must not hang on quadratic input.
notes: **See also**: Pf016, Pf017. Synonyms: "huge assembly takes forever to load", "O(n^2) graph traversal during STEP read", "many siblings sharing one product slow loader to crawl", "assembly reader scales quadratically with NAUO count".
reproducer: large nested assembly with thousands of next-assembly-usage occurrences; profile the assembly reader's transfer pass.
sources: G046 (OCCT 63cdf48 / Mantis 0029830), V017 (Creo → Inventor OOM), V051 (Revit-derived data), J019 (440MB STEP entity-name map O(n²)), I047 (20MB STEP 50s).
title: Quadratic-time assembly graph traversal: many `NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE` siblings share a single leaf `PRODUCT_DEFINITION`

description: Roundtripping through neutral formats or running defeaturing blows away face/edge/vertex identifiers. Drawings, mates, in-context assembly references, and dimensioning all break. Read-only parent files cannot be edited to repair the references. Going CAD→CAE is opaque: any upstream CAD edit invalidates downstream boundary conditions silently.
expected_kernel_behavior: maintain stable identifiers across simplification; merge multiple features into one but preserve the union of their face/edge/vertex IDs as aliases; explicit traceable mapping data structure between CAD and engineering-model entities.
notes: **See also**: N044. **OCC behavior**: emits a diagnostic but produces no shape (warn-and-proceed by oracle, but result is empty); outside catalog's allowed set ({heal}). Kernel-bug witnessed: catalog asks for healing; OCC neither heals nor rejects; the input is dropped on the floor without diagnostic. Synonyms: "defeaturing for CAE drops references to original geometry", "simplified mesh loses link to source PMI", "downstream tool can't trace back to original part", "reference loss when feature suppressed for analysis".
reproducer: Suppress a fillet via direct-edit, re-export; downstream drawing's centerline reference (originally to fillet edge) becomes orphaned. Or apply a face-pressure load in Ansys; defeature the face.
sources: X011 (Dassault EP 3472735 A1), X023 (Ansys CAD-to-CAE topology mapping).
title: Reference loss when defeaturing / simplifying for CAE

description: Same UDA template implemented differently across CAD systems; bound to `product`, to `product_definition`, to `next_assembly_usage_occurrence`, or to a shape aspect. Round-trip loses the binding because the receiver expects a different target.
expected_kernel_behavior: preserve UDA verbatim using the rec-practice template; do not silently re-bind.
notes: **See also**: A016. **OCC behavior**: silently drops UDAs whose target binding does not match its expectations rather than preserving them verbatim; kernel mishandling; the catalog above forbids silent re-binding (or silent loss). Synonyms: "UDA bound to wrong target after import", "user-defined attribute target inconsistent", "attribute assigned to part but appears on instance", "UDA target-binding mismatch".
reproducer: NX writes UDA on `product_definition`; CATIA reader expects it on `next_assembly_usage_occurrence`; data is ignored on reimport.
title: User-Defined Attribute (UDA) target-binding inconsistency

description: `FILE_SCHEMA` declares one edition (e.g. AP242 Ed.2) but payload contains entities valid only under another edition (e.g. AP242e3 hole-feature entities, or AP242-only entities like `ROUND_HOLE` in a file declaring `AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN`). Older readers parse newer entity flavors as fatal errors and crash.
expected_kernel_behavior: Warn and accept: parse based on entity availability, not header schema name; warn on mismatch; forward-compatible reader; unknown entities should be ignored, not fatal. Do not reject on edition mismatch.
notes: **See also**: A031, A032, Pmi010. Synonyms: "header schema differs from instance schema in Part 21", "AP203 header but AP242 entities inside", "edition-mixed STEP file confuses reader", "schema declared in HEADER doesn't match body".
reproducer: Hand-edit `FILE_SCHEMA` line to claim Ed.2 in an Ed.3 file; or declare AP214 with AP242-only entities.
sources: M029 (STEP Tools edition notes), W046 (Datakit), V043 (Creo 4 cannot import Creo 7+ STEP).
title: Edition-mixed Part 21 file (header schema vs instance schema)

description: AP242 Ed.1 retired ~53 AP214/AP203 entities (`kinematic_structure`, `mechanism`, `kinematic_property_definition`, etc.). Ed.3 retired three never-implemented Ed.2 entities (`connected_edge_with_length_set_representation`, `edge_with_length`, `vertex_on_edge`). Archived files using them cannot be re-validated against the newer schema.
expected_kernel_behavior: archive-stable in original schema form; on migration drop entities (with recorded loss-of-fidelity) or refuse migration.
notes: **See also**: A030, M049. **OCC behavior**: emits a diagnostic but produces no shape (warn-and-proceed by oracle, but result is empty); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant. Synonyms: "retired AP214 kinematics entity in current file", "obsolete kinematics entity rejected", "schema migration drops legacy kinematics".
reproducer: AP214 file using `kinematic_link_representation_relation` re-headered as AP242; or Ed.2 file with `vertex_on_edge` re-validated against Ed.3.
sources: M016 (STEP Tools AP242 Ed.1 notes — 53 retired entities), M019 (Ed.2 entities deleted in Ed.3).
title: Schema migration: retired AP214/AP203 kinematics entities

description: Four enums reordered between Ed.2 and Ed.3: `area_unit_type`, `datum_reference_modifier_type`, `geometric_tolerance_modifier`, `simple_datum_reference_modifier`. Any code that compares by ordinal index (rather than by name) silently misinterprets values across the boundary.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; compare by string name, not ordinal; detect schema version from `FILE_SCHEMA` and choose mapping accordingly.
notes: **See also**: A030. **OCC behavior**: emits a diagnostic but produces no shape (warn-and-proceed by oracle, but result is empty); outside catalog's allowed set ({heal}). Kernel-bug witnessed: catalog asks for healing; OCC neither heals nor rejects; the input is dropped on the floor without diagnostic. Synonyms: "enum order changed between AP242 Ed.2 and Ed.3", "wrong enum value on schema migration", "enum reordering between editions breaks file".
reproducer: AP242 Ed.2 reader with internal int mapping for `geometric_tolerance_modifier` reads an Ed.3 file.
title: Schema migration: enum-value reordering between AP242 Ed.2 and Ed.3

description: `PRODUCT_DEFINITION_WITH_ASSOCIATED_DOCUMENTS` carries its own `name` attribute that OCCT did not pick up; specific entity-name patterns silently dropped on import.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: honor name from this entity in all readers; must not silently drop the name.
notes: **See also**: A010. Synonyms: "applied_external_identification_assignment name lost", "product_definition_with_associated_documents name dropped", "external doc-id stripped on round-trip", "PLM document reference name disappears".
reproducer: STEP file using PRODUCT_DEFINITION_WITH_ASSOCIATED_DOCUMENTS instead of plain PRODUCT_DEFINITION.
title: `applied_external_identification_assignment` /`product_definition_with_associated_documents` name dropped

description: `SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION` whose `Definition` member of the `RepresentedDefinition` SELECT is a `SHAPE_ASPECT` rather than `PROPERTY_DEFINITION`. OCCT's unguarded chain `SDR->Definition().PropertyDefinition()->Definition().ProductDefinition()` returns null on the SHAPE_ASPECT branch and crashes.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; skip SDRs whose Definition is not PropertyDefinition; emit warning; never deref blindly.
notes: **See also**: A009. Validation observed: silent-empty rather than crash. Kernel-mishandling-by-silent-acceptance still demonstrates the defect class. Synonyms: "CheckSRRReversesNAUO crashes with SHAPE_ASPECT instead of PROPERTY_DEFINITION", "segfault during assembly check", "SDR with shape_aspect breaks reader", "STEP reader null-deref on assembly traversal".
occ_behavior_note: silent-empty rather than crash. Kernel-mishandling-by-silent-acceptance still demonstrates the defect class. Synonyms: "CheckSRRReversesNAUO crashes with SHAPE_ASPECT instead of PROPERTY_DEFINITION", "segfault during assembly check", "SDR with shape_aspect breaks reader", "STEP reader null-deref on assembly traversal".
reproducer: AP214 file with `#27=SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION(#23,#26)` where `#23` is a `SHAPE_ASPECT` instead of `PROPERTY_DEFINITION_SHAPE`.
sender: CATIA V6 "Fast Export STEP AP214 Mapper" (1088/1267 SDRs in a real 430MB file used the SHAPE_ASPECT variant).
title: CheckSRRReversesNAUO segfault on SDR with SHAPE_ASPECT instead of PROPERTY_DEFINITION

description: A `PRODUCT` simultaneously has both sub-assemblies (NAUO children) and a direct geometric `SHAPE_REPRESENTATION` of its own. Strict assembly-vs-leaf classifiers misroute one or the other.
expected_kernel_behavior: Accept hybrid; treat as both parent and leaf; emit both sub-assembly tree and direct geometry. Do not reject hybrid pattern.
notes: **See also**: A036. Synonyms: "product node has both subassemblies and direct geometry", "mixed product structure confuses reader", "leaf shape attached to non-leaf product", "PRODUCT_DEFINITION carries shape AND children".
reproducer: PRODUCT_DEFINITION referenced by both `NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE` (as parent) and a `SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION` carrying its own faces/solids.
title: Product with both sub-assemblies and direct shape

description: Older AP203 (≤1998) hybrid models linked SDRs to the main model via shape_aspect rather than directly via product_definition_shape. Modern readers expect direct linkage.

description: STEP file with `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` data but no `PRODUCT`, `PRODUCT_DEFINITION`, or `SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION`; common in minimalist exporters and many open-source / hobbyist tools.
expected_kernel_behavior: synthesize default product wrapper; warn.
notes: **See also**: A003. **OCC behavior**: emits a diagnostic but produces no shape (warn-and-proceed by oracle, but result is empty); outside catalog's allowed set ({heal}). Kernel-bug witnessed: catalog asks for healing; OCC neither heals nor rejects; the input is dropped on the floor without diagnostic. Synonyms: "minimal STEP has no PRODUCT entity", "implicit product structure missing", "file lacks any product definition", "geometry-only STEP without metadata".

description: AP242 files use inch units inside `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT` for axis placements in `CONSTRUCTIVE_GEOMETRY_REPRESENTATION_RELATIONSHIP`, but unit was not applied; axes land at wrong scale, mis-positioning every component that uses them.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: apply unit scaling to construction-geometry placements; expose `read.step.constructivegeom.relationship` opt-in flag.
notes: **See also**: M011. Synonyms: "constructive geometry representation relationship axis placements", "CGR carries assembly-level placements", "constructive geometry connects subassembly axis frames".

description: `STYLED_ITEM` and `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT` carry human-readable names attached to specific edges, faces, or sub-solids inside an assembly. STEP reader records names only at the top `PRODUCT_DEFINITION` level, dropping per-subshape names.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: every named entity (face, edge, vertex, shell, solid) must propagate its name into the receiving model's attribute store keyed by the corresponding sub-shape. Must not silently drop names.
notes: **See also**: A030. Synonyms: "subshape names not transferred from STEP", "face/edge labels missing after import", "STEPCAFControl_Reader doesn't transfer named subshapes".

sources: OCCT MANTIS#0023895 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Subshape names not transferred on STEP import

description: A document containing an empty group (no sub-shapes assigned) round-trips through the STEP writer and fails because the writer's `AppliedGroupAssignment` emitter requires at least one member. description: An assembly's `UpdateAssemblies` pass rebuilds top-level compounds from current sub-assembly state. When the root assembly itself carries a non-identity location, the rebuild applies the location once at the leaf level and again at the root, producing parts displaced twice from origin.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: location-chain composition follows the hierarchy strictly once; UpdateAssemblies recomputes from leaves up, honouring identity at each level it climbs.
notes: Synonyms: "UpdateAssemblies makes wrong compounds for located roots", "located root produces incorrect compound after UpdateAssemblies", "compound wrong after UpdateAssemblies on positioned part".
reproducer: Assembly tree where root has a translation `(100,0,0)` and one child has a translation `(50,0,0)`. After `UpdateAssemblies`, the leaf appears at `(200,0,0)` (sum applied at both levels) instead of `(150,0,0)`.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0031517 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: `UpdateAssemblies` produces wrong compounds for located roots

description: A compound containing several instances of the same shape via different `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D`s is processed by a pass that bakes locations into geometry. sources: OCCT MANTIS#0028471 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Baking placements into geometry breaks shared-subshape sharing
