category: §12.6 assembly hierarchy (sub-class: writer-side fillet round-trip break)
description: A part with a fillet of radius `r << boundingBox/1000` is exported. The writer emits the fillet as a small `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` plus tiny `EDGE_CURVE`s, but the edge-vertex coordinates round to the same `CARTESIAN_POINT` at the writer's emission precision. On re-import the small fillet collapses to a self-loop edge, the face becomes degenerate, and the round part imports as a sharp-edged version. Visible especially on small mechanical parts (~10mm) with sub-mm fillets.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; writer chooses precision based on minimum-feature-size, not just bounding box; emit `W_PRECISION_LIMITED` if any pair of distinct vertices would round to the same coordinate at the chosen precision and bump precision automatically.
notes: **See also**: N028, Twi099. Synonyms: "STEP export fail for round part in FreeCAD", "fillet edges go missing on round-trip", "writer precision drops sub-mm fillet", "round part exported as sharp edges".
reproducer: `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` of a 10mm cube with a 0.05mm fillet on one edge. Writer emits coordinates rounded to 1e-6; the fillet's distinct vertices collapse to one. Receiver sees a degenerate face.
sender: FreeCAD / OCCT writer when exporting a part whose fillet edges have very small radii (sub-millimetre) compared to the part bounding box.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP export fail for a round part in FreeCAD", "fillet edges go missing on round-trip", "round part exports as broken shape". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: STEP export of a part with a fillet/round generates malformed shape on receiver

category: §12.6 assembly hierarchy (sub-class: writer drops identity-located instance)
description: An assembly contains three instances of the same part: one at the world origin (identity location) and two placed by transforms. The writer's de-duplication pass mistakes "identity location" for "no instance" and skips the world-origin instance entirely. Output file has the part placed twice instead of three times. Asymmetric; the bug only manifests when at least one instance is at identity AND at least one instance has a non-identity transform.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; every distinct `NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE` corresponds to one emitted instance regardless of its location's identity; never use "is identity transform" as a skip predicate.
notes: **See also**: A082, A104. Synonyms: "STEPCAFControl_Writer drops identity-placed instance", "writer skips identity-location instance with partners", "STEP export missing assembly instance", "identity-transform instance not exported".
reproducer: Assembly with one `NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE` whose location is identity, plus two more whose locations are non-identity. Output drops the identity-placed instance.
sender: OCCT's `STEPCAFControl_Writer` when exporting an assembly with multiple instances of the same part, where one instance is at the identity transform and others are placed.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEPCAFControl_Writer will not export shape with Identity Location if there are other partner shapes with diff Location", "writer drops identity-placed instance from assembly", "STEP export skips master shape". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: `STEPCAFControl_Writer` skips a shape when it has identity location and partner shapes have non-identity locations

category: §12.6 assembly hierarchy (sub-class: transfer-pipeline error after successful parse)
description: `STEPControl_Reader::ReadFile` returns OK and `NbRoots() > 0`; `STEPCAFControl_Reader::Transfer(doc)` returns `Standard_False` and the OCAF document is empty. The transfer pass walks `PRODUCT_DEFINITION → PRODUCT_DEFINITION_CONTEXT → APPLICATION_CONTEXT` and the chain has a mismatch (two distinct `APPLICATION_CONTEXT` instances with the same string content). The user's reasonable interpretation — "the parser said it worked" — is contradicted by the empty document.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; transfer pass tolerates multiple `APPLICATION_CONTEXT` records by matching on string content; emit `W_DUPLICATE_APPLICATION_CONTEXT` and proceed. Parser-OK + empty-document is a contract violation.
notes: **See also**: M165, A067. Synonyms: "error transferring STEP model to OCAF document", "STEPCAFControl_Reader Transfer returns false", "parser succeeds but transfer fails", "duplicate APPLICATION_CONTEXT breaks transfer".
reproducer: STEP file with two distinct `APPLICATION_CONTEXT` records. Parser accepts; `STEPCAFControl_Reader::Transfer` returns false. Document is empty.
sender: Producers that emit `PRODUCT_DEFINITION` records whose context (`PRODUCT_DEFINITION_CONTEXT`) is not the same instance referenced from the document's `APPLICATION_CONTEXT` — the reader's two-pass design rejects the link.
sources: bug-reporter language: "error with a .stp model during transfer from STEPCAFControl_Reader to document", "parser succeeds but transfer fails", "STEP file parses OK but does not become an OCAF document". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Error transferring `.stp` model from `STEPCAFControl_Reader` to OCAF document

description: A file authored in build N, exported as STEP from build N, and re-imported into build N produces zero geometry; yet the same file imports cleanly into build N-1. The signature is a `SHAPE_REPRESENTATION` whose `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` first attribute (`location`) refers to a `CARTESIAN_POINT` that was emitted *after* the `SHAPE_REPRESENTATION` in the file but referenced from within (forward reference is legal per ISO 10303-21 §11 but the build-N reader has a regression in its forward-reference resolver).
expected_kernel_behavior: forward references are spec-legal; the importer must do a two-pass parse. Reject with a clear diagnostic rather than silent-empty if forward resolution fails.
notes: Synonyms: "self-import refused", "round-trip with same version broken", "freecad cannot read its own export", "RC2-exported STEP fails RC2 import".
reproducer: STEP file where `#10=SHAPE_REPRESENTATION('part',(#100),#101);` appears before `#100=AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D('',#150,#151,#152);` and `#150=CARTESIAN_POINT('',(0.0,0.0,0.0));` — every reference is forward-only.
sender: FreeCAD 1.0RC2 (and earlier stretches): export pipeline emits a file that the import pipeline of the same build silently rejects.
sources: bug-reporter language: "Once a FreeCad file is exported to step, the same step file cannot be opened in FreeCad", "Importing the step file in same RC2 only gives a single error and no imported geometry", "round-trip into the same version is broken".
title: Writer-emitted STEP cannot be re-imported by the same writing process (round-trip refused)

description: A Body whose linear feature stack is `Pad → Fillet → Pocket` with the Tip set to `Pocket` exports as `Pad → Fillet` only. The visible result in the 3D view shows the Pocket; the STEP file has it stripped. The on-disk symptom is a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` that lacks the inner `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` corresponding to the pocket walls; every face of the pre-pocket Pad+Fillet shape is present, but no pocket-bottom face nor pocket-wall faces.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: writer emits the visible Tip; or warn and accept with a diagnostic when the in-memory model and the exported feature pointer disagree. Loading stale geometry without diagnostic is a coverage gap.
notes: Synonyms: "PartDesign Tip not exported", "last feature missing from STEP", "pocket dropped on STEP export", "exported body is one feature behind the Tip".
reproducer: STEP solid representing a 20 mm cube with a fillet on one edge but no pocket — even though the catalog entry claims the body is "cube, filleted, pocketed".
sender: FreeCAD PartDesign Body whose visible Tip is the last operation (e.g., a Pocket) but where the document's "exported feature" pointer is one revision behind.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP Export of Body leaves out last operation", "the pocket is not included even though it is visible and set as the tip", "exported file looks like the body before the last feature".
title: PartDesign Body export omits last-feature operation when feature is the visible Tip

description: A STEP assembly that carries `MECHANISM` / `KINEMATIC_JOINT` annotations alongside the geometry is imported as a flat tree of Part containers; the joint-and-kinematic graph is silently dropped. The on-disk file has a `KINEMATIC_TOPOLOGY_STRUCTURE` referencing geometry sub-shapes; the importer reads only the geometric faces and discards the kinematic graph.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: importer routes assemblies with kinematic data into the Assembly container; or warn and accept by routing into Part with a diagnostic listing dropped kinematic entities. Dropping the kinematic graph without diagnostic is a coverage gap.
notes: **See also**: P011 (PMI silently discarded). Synonyms: "Assembly module not supported by STEP importer", "joints lost on STEP import", "kinematic data discarded", "imported into Part not Assembly".
reproducer: STEP file with two `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`s plus a `MECHANISM('joint1', ..)` referencing them.
sender: FreeCAD STEP importer prior to Assembly-module integration; STEP file authored by a tool that emitted joint/kinematic data alongside the geometry.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP file importer doesn't support new assembly module", "whole assembly is imported into Part containers, not into Assembly container", "joints and constraints are dropped".
title: Importer routes Assembly-module assemblies into Part containers (Assembly graph lost)

description: A body authored as `BasePad → BooleanCut(tool=SubShapeBinder('Other_Body.Face'))` exports a STEP whose `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` contains `ADVANCED_FACE`s with `EDGE_CURVE` references that point to entity numbers existing in the file but whose `EDGE_LOOP` contains an `ORIENTED_EDGE` whose `edge_element` is `*` (asterisk-implicit) without the matching parent definition; in other words, `*`-oriented edges escape into the file body. The receiver attempts to dereference and crashes (PrusaSlicer) or yields empty (FreeCAD self-import).
expected_kernel_behavior: writer materialises every `*`-implicit reference before emission; receivers reject `*` `edge_element` with a precise diagnostic.
notes: **See also**: A018. Synonyms: "SubShapeBinder Boolean Cut crashes slicer", "asterisk edge element escapes file body", "STEP makes PrusaSlicer crash on import", "boolean from SubShapeBinder broken on export".
reproducer: STEP body where one `EDGE_LOOP` contains an `ORIENTED_EDGE('',*,*,#99,.T.)` referencing `#99` whose `edge_element` is itself `*`.
sender: FreeCAD PartDesign body whose history includes a Boolean Cut whose tool comes from a SubShapeBinder cross-document reference.
sources: bug-reporter language: "Export of PartDesign body containing Boolean Cut with SubShapeBinder is broken", "PrusaSlicer just crashes for STEP", "the very STEP exported by FreeCAD makes it crash on re-import".
title: SubShapeBinder-derived Boolean Cut crashes downstream slicers and re-import

description: A Cap part — a thin-walled cup/cap shape — exports a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` whose outer shell is missing one face (the cap-bottom interior). Downstream slicers (Orca, Bambu Studio) detect non-manifold geometry and refuse the print job. The companion STL export tessellates fine because the StL writer ignores topology. Distinct from P015 because the missing-face symptom is reproducibly tied to the Cap-feature pipeline (not a SubShapeBinder offset).
expected_kernel_behavior: writer validates closure before wrapping in `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`; or downgrades to `SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL` with a warning.
notes: **See also**: P015. Synonyms: "cap export marked damaged by slicer", "thin-walled body has open shell", "PartDesign cap STEP fails slicer ingest", "step broken but stl fine".
reproducer: thin-walled cup `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` (8 faces expected: 4 outer-side, 4 inner-side, 1 outer-bottom, 1 inner-bottom, 1 top-rim) with one face omitted, leaving a 7-face shell wrapped as a solid.
sender: FreeCAD PartDesign Cap-feature export in 1.2.0dev.
sources: bug-reporter language: "Sometimes exported STEP/STL damaged or contains errors", "Cap object marked as damaged in slicers like Orca or Bambu Studio", "step is broken but stl is fine".
title: Cap part exports as STEP that downstream slicers flag as damaged (open shell wrapped as solid)

category: §12.6 assembly hierarchy (sub-class: appearance dropped on import)
description: A STEP file has well-formed `COLOUR_RGB` records and `PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT`s wired to faces, but the reader's `XCAFDoc_ColorTool::SetColor` does not pick them up. The geometry imports cleanly, but the resulting `XCAFDoc_DocumentTool` has no colour assignments at all; every face is the default grey. The producer's intent (red shaft, blue housing) is silently lost.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; every `STYLED_ITEM` whose target resolves to a known shape contributes a colour assignment to XCAF; unresolved styles emit `W_UNREACHED_STYLE` but never silently disappear.
notes: **See also**: A105, A081. Synonyms: "STEP model imported with no colours", "colours present in file lost on import", "STYLED_ITEM not reaching XCAFDoc_ColorTool", "appearance dropped during STEP read".
reproducer: STEP solid with `STYLED_ITEM` referring to `PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT` containing `SURFACE_STYLE_USAGE` with `SURFACE_SIDE_STYLE` and `SURFACE_STYLE_FILL_AREA` plus `FILL_AREA_STYLE_COLOUR` pointing at `COLOUR_RGB`. Reader imports geometry but no colour reaches XCAF.
sender: Authoring tools that emit `STYLED_ITEM` colour assignments at the assembly-occurrence level rather than per-face, or that route colour through `MECHANICAL_DESIGN_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION_WITH_DRAUGHTING` which the reader's first pass may skip.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP model is imported with no colours", "all faces appear default grey", "colours present in file are not picked up by reader". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Geometry imports correctly but every face arrives with no colour assigned

category: §12.6 assembly hierarchy (sub-class: writer crash on external-ref mode)
description: When the writer is asked to emit a multi-file assembly (one file per part, plus a top-level file with `EXTERNAL_REFERENCED_DOCUMENT` pointing to peers), an unhandled `Standard_DomainError` propagates out of the call when one of the peer documents has not been previously saved or when a label has no associated `TopoDS_Shape`. The writer aborts mid-stream, leaving partial output files on disk.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; every writer entry point validates the document graph before opening output files; emit `W_EMPTY_BRANCH` and skip empty branches; never throw across the writer's public API.
notes: **See also**: A082, A096. Synonyms: "STEP writer exception in ExternalReferences mode", "multi-file STEP export throws on empty branch", "writer crashes when peer document missing", "Standard_DomainError during STEP write".
reproducer: XDE document with two assembly branches; branch A has shape, branch B is empty. Call `STEPCAFControl_Writer::Perform` with external-reference mode. Writer throws.
sender: OCCT's STEP writer when the document uses `STEPControl_Writer::Transfer` with `mode = STEPCAFControl_ExternalFileReferences` and the document references unsaved external `.stp` peers.
sources: bug-reporter language: "exception is raised during writing with ExternalReferences mode in STEP XDE document", "writer throws on multi-file export", "STEP write mode crashes on assembly with external part files". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Exception raised during STEP write with `ExternalReferences` mode in XDE document

category: §12.6 assembly hierarchy (sub-class: appearance regression across kernel versions)
description: A STEP file declares colours through `MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION` containing `STYLED_ITEM`s that point at the assembly-occurrence level rather than per-face. The 6.9.x reader resolved these and assigned colours; the 7.4.0 reader's refactored colour pipeline only consults the per-face route, so the file's colours are silently dropped. A regression; the producer is unchanged; the receiver lost coverage.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; every recognised colour-assignment path (per-face, per-occurrence, per-representation, draughting-presentation) must contribute to XCAF; emit `W_LEGACY_COLOUR_ROUTE` rather than dropping the assignment.
notes: **See also**: A103, A081. Synonyms: "regression colours no longer showing on STEP files", "OCC 7.4 colour pipeline regression", "MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION colour dropped", "appearance lost across kernel versions".
reproducer: STEP file with `MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION` containing one `STYLED_ITEM` pointing at a `SHAPE_REPRESENTATION`. 6.9.x renders red; 7.4.0+ renders grey.
sender: STEP files emitted by older toolchains that use the `MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION` route for colours rather than the per-face `STYLED_ITEM` route.
sources: bug-reporter language: "regression v.6.9.1-7.4.0 colors no longer showing on certain STEP files", "files that displayed colour in 6.9.1 are grey in 7.4.0", "appearance regression". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Regression OCC 6.9.1 → 7.4.0: colours stop appearing on certain STEP files

category: §12.6 assembly hierarchy (sub-class: SEGV in style translation)
description: A `PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT` arrives with an empty `styles` list. The translation pass dereferences `styles[0]` without a bounds check and crashes with `SIGSEGV` / Windows access violation. Distinct from Ad117 (dangling reference); here the list is well-formed but empty.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject — emit `E_EMPTY_STYLE_LIST` and skip the assignment; never index into a list without checking its length. A crash on schema-illegal input is a reliability defect.
notes: **See also**: Ad117, A104. Synonyms: "access violation in StepVisual_PresentationStyleAssignment", "crash on empty style list", "STEP translator segfault on style", "presentation style assignment indexing past end".
reproducer: `#100=PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT(());` referenced from a `STYLED_ITEM`. Reader crashes when translating the styled item.
sender: Producers that emit a `PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT` whose `styles` list is empty (`( )`) — schema-illegal but emitted by some hand-edited fixtures and a handful of legacy translators.
sources: bug-reporter language: "access violation in StepVisual_PresentationStyleAssignment while translating STEP file", "crash in style assignment", "segfault during STEP visual translation". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Access violation in `StepVisual_PresentationStyleAssignment` while translating STEP file

description: A document with `XCAFDoc_ColorTool` assignments is saved to `BinXCAF` (binary `.xbf`). When reloaded by 7.4.0+, the colour-driver registration order changed: the binary stream is parsed but the colour records hit an unknown driver tag and are silently discarded. The geometry reloads, the colours do not. This is a forward-compat regression in the persistence format; round-tripping through STEP exposes the same colour-loss path.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; the persistence layer registers all historical driver tags; emit `W_UNKNOWN_DRIVER_TAG` and skip rather than corrupting the file. Round-trip through STEP must preserve colour.
notes: **See also**: A105, A081, U036. Synonyms: "regression cannot read BinOcaf document with colour", "BinXCAF colour driver tag unknown", "persistence format regression after 7.4", "OCAF colour lost on reload".
reproducer: Document with one box, one colour assignment. Save BinXCAF in 6.9.x. Reload in 7.4.0+. Colours absent.
sender: OCCT's own `BinXCAFDrivers` persistence layer when saving a document that has colour assignments and reading it back with a different (newer) kernel build.
sources: bug-reporter language: "regression to OCCT 7.4.0 cannot read BinOcaf document with colour", "BinXCAF colour read fails after 7.4 upgrade", "binary OCAF format colour regression". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: `BinXCAF` regression: documents with colour cannot be re-loaded after save

description: An assembly compound containing a PRODUCT subassembly with one body and a mirrored copy of that body has the mirror dropped during STEP export. The mirrored body is structurally a NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE that references the source PRODUCT via a MAPPED_ITEM under an AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D whose ref_direction is negated (mirror reflection, negative determinant). Some writers' NAUO emit-path silently skips placements with a negative-determinant transformation, dropping the mirrored sub-assembly from the output.
expected_kernel_behavior: preserve all NAUO entries through export regardless of placement determinant; emit MAPPED_ITEM with the mirror placement; flag negative-determinant placements as mirror transforms in the consuming reader rather than dropping.
notes: Synonyms: "Draft Mirror lost on STEP export", "mirrored body not in STEP", "negative-determinant NAUO dropped", "STEP writer skips mirror placement", "Part Design mirror body missing after export". See also A104 (mirror-related Mantis ticket).
reproducer: parent PRODUCT 'Body' + child PRODUCT 'Body_Mirrored'; child reached via NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE → MAPPED_ITEM → REPRESENTATION_MAP whose location is an AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D with ref_direction `(-1, 0, 0)` (mirror across YZ plane).
sources: Pattern-mined from FreeCAD/FreeCAD#13581 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: Part Design body + Draft 'Mirror' tool → STEP export drops the mirrored body. "Only one of the bodies will be in the step file."
title: Draft-mirrored body silently dropped on STEP export (mirror NAUO)

description: After merging two STEP files, a `NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE` points to the *wrong* parent PRODUCT — typically because the merge tool didn't re-key the assembly graph. Receivers see a sub-assembly under the wrong parent or as an orphan node.
expected_kernel_behavior: merge tools must re-key all NAUO references; readers should validate NAUO endpoints are PRODUCT entities.
notes: Synonyms: "STEP merge tree corruption", "NAUO wrong parent after combine", "combining STEP files tree messed up", "STEP assembly graph re-keyed wrong", "FreeCAD combine STEP tree broken".
reproducer: `NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE('wrong_parent','...','',#9001,#9999,$)` where `#9999` is not a PRODUCT.
sources: Pattern-mined from FreeCAD/FreeCAD#11441 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: "Combining STEP files messes tree structure in resulting file".
title: Combining STEP files corrupts assembly tree (NAUO wrong parent)

description: The writer emits `PRODUCT('#9001','step-id-as-name','',(#9001))` — the human-readable name slot is populated with the STEP entity ID rather than a real label. Downstream BoM tools display "Part #9001" instead of "Door Handle".
expected_kernel_behavior: preserve source-side labels; only fall back to entity IDs when no label is available, with a diagnostic.
notes: Synonyms: "STEP id used as element name", "PRODUCT name is STEP id", "IfcConverter step-id naming", "writer used entity id for product name", "STEP serialization names from id".
sources: Pattern-mined from IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell#923 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: "use entity STEP id for naming elements upon serialization in IfcConverter".
title: Entity STEP id used as element name on serialization

description: A MAPPED_ITEM emits a REPRESENTATION_MAP whose target (`#9999` here) is a dangling forward reference. The producer logs "Cannot add a VRML model to a STEP file" but emits the PCB with placeholders anyway. STEP-level diagnostic is absent.
expected_kernel_behavior: emit a STEP-level diagnostic (PROPERTY_DEFINITION or comment) for each silently-dropped component; track in PRODUCT_DEFINITION chain.
notes: Synonyms: "KiCad VRML STEP placeholders dropped", "PCB STEP bare board no components", "MAPPED_ITEM dangling target on PCB", "VRML→STEP gateway silent", "KiCad cannot add VRML to STEP".
reproducer: `REPRESENTATION_MAP(#plc, #9999)` + `MAPPED_ITEM('vrml_placeholder',...,#9999)`.
sources: Pattern-mined from KiCad gitlab#11482 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: VRML 3D-model components in a KiCad PCB project survive into the STEP file as placeholder MAPPED_ITEMs whose REPRESENTATION_MAP target was never resolved
receivers see a bare PCB with no components and no diagnostic.
title: VRML→STEP gateway silently drops non-STEP component placeholders

description: Three `NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE` entries share the same `id` slot (`C1`). Receivers that key on NAUO.id (rather than entity #N) deduplicate and lose two of the three instances.
expected_kernel_behavior: NAUO ids should not be assumed unique within a file; key dedup on entity reference, not the label string.
notes: Synonyms: "KiCad STEP NAUO duplicate names", "CadQuery STEP assembly dedup collapse", "STEP NAUO name reuse loses instances", "C1 C1 C1 in STEP collapses", "PCB assembly STEP same-name NAUOs".
reproducer: three NAUOs with identical first-arg label.
sources: Pattern-mined from KiCad gitlab#14125 + CadQuery/cadquery#1962 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: KiCad emits N capacitor instances all labelled `C1`
downstream kernels (and some converters) deduplicate by NAUO.id and collapse all instances into one placement.
title: NAUO name reuse: dedup-by-name collapses distinct instances

description: A re-exported file using the older `CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN` schema (rather than `AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN`) and lacking a `PRODUCT` entity at the protocol layer is silently dropped by OCCT's reader: import returns success with zero objects, no message in console or report panel. Other readers (e.g., Rhino) accept it.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject with explicit diagnostic identifying the missing `PRODUCT` parent, or accept successfully. Silent empty result (silent-accept) is the bug; must not silently accept.
notes: Synonyms: "CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN file with no PRODUCT entity", "schema variant missing required PRODUCT", "CCD-only STEP file rejected by readers".
reproducer: Author a STEP-AP203 file whose HEADER declares `CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN`, omit the `PRODUCT`/`PRODUCT_DEFINITION` chain that AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN tooling expects, but keep a normal `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` payload.
sender: re-export from unspecified application (original was AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN)
title: Schema variant: CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN with no PRODUCT entity

description: STEP-21 lines like `SHAPE_REPRESENTATION ('海绵2', ..)` appear in files encoded as GB18030 / Shift-JIS / CP1252 because exporters write the OS code page directly. Readers that assume UTF-8 produce mojibake in object labels and attributes; round-tripping then corrupts the saved project document.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: auto-detect or honor STEP-21 `\X2\` / `\X4\` escape sequences; expose a per-file encoding override; warn if bytes don't decode as declared encoding.
notes: Synonyms: "GB18030 encoded part names corrupt after read", "non-UTF-8 string literals in STEP", "Chinese locale code page in name strings", "encoding mismatch garbles labels".
reproducer: Generate a STEP file containing `PRODUCT`/`SHAPE_REPRESENTATION` name strings with high-bit bytes interpretable in GB18030 but not UTF-8 (or with the standard `\X2\…\X0\` Unicode escape sequences that exporters rarely emit).
sender: SolidWorks (Chinese-locale install) and any non-Western Windows export
title: Non-UTF-8 (GB18030 / locale code page) in string literals

description: A STEP file whose `PRODUCT` / `NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE` name fields contain bytes that are illegal in downstream serialization (control chars `\x00`–`\x1F`, lone surrogates, unescaped `<`/`&`/`>`, invalid UTF-8 continuation bytes) imports without complaint, but a save-and-reopen of the receiving document fails to parse.
expected_kernel_behavior: Sanitize/escape names at parse time; reject obviously invalid bytes with a warning.
notes: Synonyms: "control characters in STEP name strings", "illegal-XML bytes break downstream tools", "raw 0x00-0x1F in PRODUCT.name", "XML serializer chokes on bytes from STEP".
reproducer: Produce a STEP file with names containing raw control bytes, lone surrogates, or characters that become illegal XML when serialized.
sender: KiCad or its STEP add-on (TO-92 footprint package names)
title: Control characters / illegal-XML bytes in name strings corrupt downstream documents

description: A face on a sphere produced by sweeping with a particular profile orientation has its `FACE_OUTER_BOUND.orientation` reversed in the output STEP; visually inside-out. Mirror-sweep variant is correct.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: face orientation preserved; both sweep variants yield the same closed solid.
notes: Synonyms: "spherical face inverted on certain sweep orientations", "sphere normal pointing inward", "revolved sphere face flipped", "inside-out spherical surface".
reproducer: Author a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` containing an `ADVANCED_FACE` with `SPHERICAL_SURFACE` underlying, whose `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` includes seam edges with explicit `.F.` orientation flags on a `surface_curve`.
sender: FreeCAD itself (Part workbench Sweep)
title: Inverted spherical face on certain sweep orientations

description: A solid produced by 360° revolution of a half-ellipse profile (major axis on X) emits self-intersecting / mirrored surface; with major axis on Y, or generatrix converted to B-spline, round-trips correctly. Suggests bug in OCCT's `CONIC` / `ELLIPSE` parametric-domain handling near the seam u=0/2π.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: closed valid solid (no self-intersection or mirroring near seam).
notes: Synonyms: "360 degree revolved ellipse self-intersects", "full revolution of arc-of-ellipse produces invalid solid", "self-intersecting solid from elliptical revolve", "degenerate solid from full ellipse revolve".
reproducer: STEP file with `SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION` whose generatrix is a `TRIMMED_CURVE(ELLIPSE(..))` spanning 0.π/2 of an ellipse with `semi_axis_1 > semi_axis_2`, revolved 2π.
sender: FreeCAD (Part Revolve)
title: 360° revolution of arc-of-ellipse produces self-intersecting solid

description: Files with `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS` of degree (3,3) representing strongly curved involute / hypoid surfaces with closely spaced knots load fine in OCCT 7.5 but display as flat planes in 7.6.x. The geometry is parsed but tessellation degenerates.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: surface honored as curved on display tessellation across versions. Must not silently flatten.
notes: Synonyms: "sharp B-spline surface flattens between OCCT versions", "high-curvature NURBS surface loses detail", "B-spline curvature flattened on import", "surface detail lost across version upgrade".
reproducer: Generate `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS` with bicubic degree, strongly curved, knot vector with closely-spaced knots representing gear flank.
sender: HyGEARS / Involute Simulation Softwares (gear-design tool)
title: High-curvature B-spline surface flattens between OCCT versions

description: A single long thread/helix represented as a `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` with thousands of control points (e.g. M10×300 thread) takes >1 hour in FreeCAD vs. <1 minute in SolidWorks/VariCAD. The helix dominates cost; rest of model is fast.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: linear scaling with face count, not catastrophic. Must not hang on long helix.
notes: **See also**: Pf014. Synonyms: "long helix becomes huge B-spline that takes forever to import", "spring/screw thread import hangs", "helical curve approximation explodes file size", "catastrophic import time on long helix".
reproducer: STEP file with one helical sweep represented as a NURBS curve with 5000+ control points spanning many turns, plus minimal capping faces.
sender: SolidWorks (`EixoY.STEP`); thread-profile tools
title: Long helix represented as huge B-spline causes catastrophic import time

description: A spring (helical sweep solid) renders as garbled facets in OCCT due to pathological chord-deviation tessellation at the helix seam, but renders correctly in Inventor.
expected_kernel_behavior: Smooth tessellation matching producer.
notes: **See also**: Pf014. Synonyms: "helical sweep tessellation garbled at seam", "thread mesh broken at start/end", "helix tessellator produces bad facets at seam", "screw thread visualizer artifacts at seam".
reproducer: STEP `SWEPT_SURFACE` whose directrix is a parametric helix with constant pitch and several turns.
sender: Autodesk Inventor
title: Helical sweep tessellates with garbled facets at seam

description: Standalone `AXIS_PLACEMENT` / `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` entities used as datum/feature axes (often referenced from `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT`) are silently dropped on import; no warning. Useful design-intent information is lost.
expected_kernel_behavior: Either ignore-with-warning, or surface as construction objects.
notes: Synonyms: "standalone AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D entities silently dropped", "datum frame lost on import", "orphan axis placement disappears", "construction frames stripped by reader".
reproducer: STEP file with `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D('Axis_A', ..)` referenced from `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT`.
sender: unspecified (multiple)
title: Standalone AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D entities silently dropped

description: AP242 files carry semantic PMI (dimensional / geometric tolerances, datum features), graphic PMI, saved views, clipping planes, materials, kinematic joints, design-history attributes. OCCT silently discards these; the geometric BREP imports but assembly is dimensionally context-less.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept (preservation), or at minimum warn-and-accept with diagnostics listing dropped entity types. Must not silently discard PMI.
notes: Synonyms: "PMI annotations silently discarded on import", "GD&T tolerances dropped", "AP242 kinematics annotations lost", "tolerances and notes vanish from STEP".
reproducer: AP242-ed2 file emitting GD&T tolerances on faces, plus kinematic joints, plus saved camera views.
sender: any AP242-capable CAD (Siemens NX, CATIA, Creo)
title: AP242 PMI / GD&T / kinematics annotations silently discarded

description: STEP-XML (`.stpx`, AP242 XML form) and gzip-compressed STEP (`.stpz`) are emitted by some commercial tools but only plain ISO-10303-21 is parsed.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: recognize and decompress / parse the XML form (`.stpx` / `.stpz`); or reject with E_UNSUPPORTED_VARIANT diagnostic.
notes: Synonyms: "STEP-XML stpx file unsupported", "compressed stpz STEP file can't open", ".stpx and .stpz formats not handled", "XML-encoded STEP rejected".

The spec does not forbid mismatched units between the two halves; a producer that sources one half from an inch-based legacy CAD library and the other from a millimetre-based current export emits the pair with mixed units. The pair is mathematically inconsistent unless the receiver normalises units before comparing.

description: AP242 Edition 4 introduces COMPOUND_FEATURE as a grouping of feature definitions (e.g. a "hole pattern" of N counterbore holes treated as one PMI target). The spec does not explicitly forbid a compound feature including itself as one of its components; a programmatic exporter that builds compound features by recursive descent and forgets the recursion guard emits a cycle.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect cycles in the part-of graph and reject; or treat the self-loop as a no-op (the pattern is "part of" itself trivially) with a warning.
notes: **See also**: Pmi070. Synonyms: "compound feature with self-referential pattern membership", "hole pattern includes itself", "self-loop in pattern membership".
reproducer: SHAPE_ASPECT `'compound_pattern'` linked via SHAPE_ASPECT_RELATIONSHIP `'part_of'` to itself, alongside SHAPE_ASPECT_RELATIONSHIP linking two member features `'hole1'` and `'hole2'` to the same pattern.
title: Compound feature with self-referential pattern membership

description: AP242 ROUND_HOLE carries a `depth` or `through_depth` attribute. A producer that copies a hole feature from a thicker design without updating the depth emits a hole deeper than the material thickness; geometrically the hole exits the back face but is encoded as a blind hole. Receivers that simulate hole removal compute either a non-watertight result or an error.
expected_kernel_behavior: Warn and accept: validate hole depth against host-part topology when the host is loaded; warn if the depth exceeds the local thickness; in tolerant mode, heal and accept by coercing the feature to a through-hole.
notes: **See also**: Pmi055. Synonyms: "hole depth exceeds part thickness", "blind hole drilled deeper than part", "hole feature depth bigger than bounding box".
reproducer: SHAPE_ASPECT `'round_hole'` with DIMENSIONAL_SIZE(`'distance'`) of 50.0mm in a host part 5mm thick.
title: Hole feature whose `depth` exceeds host-part bounding-box thickness

description: AP242 kinematic representation models a mechanism as a graph: KINEMATIC_LINK nodes joined by KINEMATIC_JOINT edges. A joint should reference exactly two distinct links (one per end). A producer that omits one end (referencing the same link twice, or pointing the second end to a deleted link) yields an inconsistent kinematic graph that cannot be simulated.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject self-loops and joints with missing endpoints with a precise diagnostic; do not allow a kinematic graph with self-loops to enter simulation pipelines.
notes: First entry exercising kinematic joint topology consistency. Synonyms: "kinematic joint references same link twice", "self-loop kinematic joint", "joint with both ends on same link".
reproducer: NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE whose relating and related PRODUCT_DEFINITIONs are the same instance — modelling a self-loop joint.
title: `KINEMATIC_JOINT` referencing the same link as both ends (self-loop)

description: AP242 ED4 introduces composite-property entities to describe layered or fibre-reinforced materials, with one property record per layer. A producer that re-uses a layer-stack template across products without updating layer-specific material references emits a stack where two adjacent layers claim the same fibre angle but reference different material grades; downstream FEA pre-processors silently take the first match.
expected_kernel_behavior: surface contradictory layer-property combinations; do not silently accept the first material as authoritative.
notes: First entry exercising AP242 ED4 composite-property semantics. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts the contradictory composite layer stack with no diagnostic; kernel mishandling; the catalog above forbids silent first-wins acceptance. Synonyms: "composite-property layer stack with contradictory materials", "layered material attributes conflict", "composite layer materials inconsistent".
reproducer: two PROPERTY_DEFINITIONs `'layer1','0deg orientation, T300'` and `'layer2','0deg orientation, M55J'` linked by PROPERTY_DEFINITION_RELATIONSHIP claiming a single stack.
title: Composite-property layer stack with contradictory material attributes

description: A document declares its length unit as metres; PMI dimension records are emitted as inches because the GD&T module assumed millimetres. Visible as dimension labels reading "0.0394" where the user expects "1.0" (a 1-inch dimension on a 1-inch hole displayed in metres). Round-trip both ways.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: PMI emitter normalizes via the document's length unit and converts dimension values consistently; record unit on the dimension entity to allow round-trip without re-conversion ambiguity.
notes: **See also**: U023, U028. Synonyms: "PMI text values wrong when LENGTH_UNIT is METRE but values in inches", "dimension unit conversion missing", "DIMENSIONAL_VALUE without unit conversion shows wrong number".
reproducer: Document with `LENGTH_UNIT = METRE`; one PMI dimension entity emitting value `1.0` with no unit conversion to metres.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0033095 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: PMI text values wrong when document LENGTH_UNIT is METRE but DIMENSIONAL_VALUE is in inches/mm without unit conversion

description: A `DIMENSION` PMI entity carries an annotation text position. STEP reader treats the position relative to the part origin, but the producer emitted it relative to the part's `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` (the local frame). Result: PMI text appears displaced from the feature it labels by the axis-placement offset.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: PMI text positions normalized to the same coordinate frame as the geometry they annotate; respect the part's local axis placement.
notes: Synonyms: "PMI text location wrong after import", "annotation moved to wrong place on import", "PMI text appears displaced".
reproducer: Part with `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` origin at `(100,0,0)`; PMI text position `(5,0,0)` (relative to part frame). Reader places text at `(5,0,0)` instead of `(105,0,0)`.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0032731 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: PMI text location wrong after import

description: A dimension PMI is created in the source CAD tool, imported correctly, but lost on a subsequent export; the writer's GD&T emitter does not iterate the document's full attribute tree.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: writer emits every PMI attached anywhere in the assembly tree, regardless of attachment style.
notes: **See also**: A077, Pmi076. Synonyms: "dimension lost after STEP export round-trip", "tolerance gone after round-trip", "dimension entity dropped on re-export".
reproducer: Document with two PMI dimensions; only one attached to a face directly, the other attached via `SHAPE_ASPECT`. Write STEP. Output has only the face-attached dimension.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0027313 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Dimension lost after STEP export round-trip

description: A geometric tolerance specifies a tolerance zone (e.g., perpendicularity within 0.1 mm). AP242 requires the zone be expressed with a plane reference; older AP203 emissions drop the plane reference, leaving the zone direction ambiguous. Reader silently picks an arbitrary plane.
expected_kernel_behavior: missing tolerance-zone plane is a hard error; readers reject or emit an explicit "ambiguous zone" diagnostic.
notes: **See also**: Pmi077. Synonyms: "GD&T tolerance frame missing tolerance-zone plane reference", "tolerance zone plane reference absent", "FCF lacks zone plane".
reproducer: Geometric tolerance with `tolerance_zone_form = unbounded` and no `tolerance_zone_plane` reference. Reader assigns `+Z` plane silently.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0029338 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: GD&T tolerance frame missing tolerance-zone plane reference

description: A document has reserved labels (saved-view labels) that must be cleared but not deleted. A "clear contents" pass empties their *children* but also empties the label name itself, producing nameless reserved labels that downstream PMI tools cannot find.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: clear-contents preserves the label name attribute and only normalizes (zaps) non-name child attributes.
notes: **See also**: Pmi078. Synonyms: "GD&T saved-views label name silently emptied", "saved view label blank after export", "GD&T view name dropped silently".
reproducer: Document with two saved-view labels named "front" and "iso". Run "clear contents". Names become empty.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0029854 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: GD&T saved-views label name silently emptied

description: A STEP file containing AP242 saved-view entities (`PRESENTATION_VIEW`) and clipping-plane references is imported; saved views are silently discarded by readers unaware of these AP242 subtypes.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: AP242 saved views populate the XCAF document view list; clipping-plane references are retained across round-trip.
notes: **See also**: A076. Synonyms: "saved-views and clipping planes lost on STEP read", "section-plane data dropped on import", "saved-view clipping planes vanish".
reproducer: STEP file with one `PRESENTATION_VIEW` linking three PMI annotations to a "side view" and one clipping plane.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0028044 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Saved-views and clipping planes lost on STEP read

description: A GD&T annotation plane on a face has its normal vector pointing into the part rather than out. Reader copies the plane normal from the underlying surface but does not consult the face orientation, so flipped faces produce flipped annotation planes; text appears facing away from viewer.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: coerce the annotation plane normal to follow face orientation, not just the underlying surface; consult `ADVANCED_FACE` same-sense flag.
notes: **See also**: Tsh001. Synonyms: "annotation plane orientation flipped on GD&T import", "GD&T text faces wrong way on read", "annotation reads backward", "PMI plane normal points into part".
reproducer: Face with reversed orientation (`.F.`); GD&T annotation plane sharing the face's surface. Reader produces annotation with normal opposite the face's outward direction.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0028449 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Annotation plane orientation flipped on GD&T import

description: AP242 dimensions reference coordinate-system connection points (`PRESENTED_ITEM` chains pointing to `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` anchors). Older readers ignore the chain; the dimension's anchor falls back to the part origin, which displaces text away from the dimensioned feature.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: walk the entire connection-point chain composing transforms; respect every intermediate placement.
notes: **See also**: A073. Synonyms: "coordinate-system connection points for dimensions missing", "dimension attachment points lost", "PMI connection points absent".
reproducer: PMI dimension with explicit connection-point chain through three intermediate placements. Reader resolves only the leaf and ignores the chain.
title: Coordinate-system connection points for dimensions missing

description: A PMI dimension's `name` attribute (an identifier used by downstream design-of-experiments tools) is read but never written back on export. Round-trip files have anonymous dimensions.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: every named entity round-trips via the schema's name attribute; dimensions are no exception.
notes: **See also**: A076. Synonyms: "dimension names dropped on round-trip", "tolerance label disappears", "dimension name not preserved".
reproducer: PMI dimension with `name = "OD_critical"`. Read, export. Output dimension has empty name.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0029525 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Dimension names dropped on round-trip

description: A document with `GENERAL_PROPERTY` entries (AP242 free-form attributes) writes to STEP successfully. But the writer routes attributes through the styled-item pipeline only for shapes with non-trivial geometry; empty shape representations lose their general attributes even when they have valuable metadata.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: attribute emission iterates every label in the XCAF document, regardless of whether the label has geometry attached.
notes: **See also**: A076. Synonyms: "empty IGES/STEP write loses general attributes", "writing empty doc strips general attributes", "general attributes dropped on empty write".
reproducer: Document with one part marked as a "configuration placeholder" (no geometry, only metadata: revision, status, owner). Writer drops the metadata.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0033165 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Empty IGES/STEP write loses general attributes

description: AP242 supports `GEOMETRIC_VALIDATION_PROPERTY` entries: a producer asserts the volume / surface-area / centroid of a body so a receiver can verify the geometry round-tripped without distortion. A producer that emits the validation property from a stale cache (last computed before a final scaling/translation step) leaves a volume claim that disagrees with the geometry the receiver computes. The disagreement is the diagnostic: receivers must surface it. Silent acceptance hides the round-trip distortion the validation property exists to detect. Bug-reporter language: "STEP validation property volume wrong", "claimed volume different from computed", "validation property fails round-trip".
expected_kernel_behavior: compute the validation property at load time and compare to the claimed value; surface the disagreement with both numbers and the offending body. The validation property's purpose is exactly this discrepancy; silent acceptance defeats it.
notes: First entry exercising GEOMETRIC_VALIDATION_PROPERTY for the volume metric. **See also**: Pmi088, Pmi089, M029. Synonyms: "STEP validation volume mismatch", "round-trip volume drift", "GEOMETRIC_VALIDATION_PROPERTY claimed volume disagrees with geometry", "volume validation property mismatch", "claimed solid volume wrong".
reproducer: a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` representing a 10x10x10 mm cube (volume 1000 mm³); a `GEOMETRIC_VALIDATION_PROPERTY` with `VOLUME_MEASURE(500.0)` claiming half the actual volume.
sender: deduced — exporters that emit validation properties from a stale cache or from a different revision of the geometry than what the file body contains
sources: 02-caxif (Validation Properties Recommended Practice §6.2 — volume / area / centroid for downstream verification)
bug-reporter language: "STEP validation volume wrong", "claimed volume disagrees with computed"
title: `GEOMETRIC_VALIDATION_PROPERTY` claimed volume disagrees with geometry

description: A `GEOMETRIC_VALIDATION_PROPERTY` of type surface-area is claimed for a body; the actually-computed surface area of the body disagrees. Common cause: the producer's exporter computes area before a final face-merge / sliver-removal pass. A receiver that recomputes detects the drift; one that trusts the producer-emitted value carries forward a value the geometry no longer supports. Bug-reporter language: "STEP surface area wrong", "validation area disagrees".
expected_kernel_behavior: Warn and accept: compute the surface area at load time, compare against the validation-property value, and emit a warning diagnostic for the disagreement.
notes: **See also**: Pmi087, Pmi089. Synonyms: "claimed surface area disagrees with geometry", "validation surface area mismatch", "GVP surface area incorrect".
reproducer: a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` representing a 10x10x10 mm cube (surface area 600 mm²); a `GEOMETRIC_VALIDATION_PROPERTY` with `AREA_MEASURE(540.0)` claiming an area lower by 10%.
sender: deduced — exporters where the surface-area cache becomes stale after Boolean trimming or face merging
title: `GEOMETRIC_VALIDATION_PROPERTY` claimed surface area disagrees with geometry

description: A `GEOMETRIC_VALIDATION_PROPERTY` claims a centroid (a `CARTESIAN_POINT`) for a body; the centroid the receiver computes is at a different location. Common cause: the producer's exporter computes the centroid in the body's local frame and the file emits the body in a parent-applied placement, but the validation property is in the local frame too; the receiver compares world-frame computed centroid against local-frame claimed centroid. Bug-reporter language: "STEP centroid wrong", "validation centroid mislocated", "centroid in wrong frame".
expected_kernel_behavior: Warn and accept: compute the centroid in a documented reference frame (local or world) and compare against the validation property; emit the frame in the diagnostic so the producer-receiver disagreement on frame can be diagnosed.
notes: **See also**: Pmi087, Pmi088. Synonyms: "claimed centroid disagrees with geometry", "validation centroid wrong", "GVP centroid coordinate mismatch".
reproducer: a 10x10x10 mm cube whose `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` is placed at world `(100, 0, 0)`. The body's actual centroid is `(105, 5, 5)` in world coordinates. A `GEOMETRIC_VALIDATION_PROPERTY` claims centroid `(5.0, 5.0, 5.0)` (the local-frame value, missing the parent translation).
sender: deduced — exporters where the centroid cache becomes stale after a final translation / placement-flatten step
title: `GEOMETRIC_VALIDATION_PROPERTY` claimed centroid disagrees with geometry

description: AP242 supports persistent UUID-based identification of features via `APPLIED_IDENTIFICATION_ASSIGNMENT` with `IDENTIFICATION_ROLE('uuid','')` and a UUID string item. A receiver that imports the file, manipulates the model, and re-exports must preserve every input UUID on every entity that survives; that is the entire point of the persistent-id mechanism. A receiver that regenerates UUIDs on import / on export silently breaks PMI links from external files (DDP-style cross-file references resolve via UUID). The first round-trip is the discovery moment: a downstream tool that loads the original file plus the re-exported one cannot reconcile their feature lists. Bug-reporter language: "STEP UUID changes on round-trip", "PMI link breaks after re-export", "DDP cross-file ref resolves to wrong feature after round-trip".
expected_kernel_behavior: preserve every persistent UUID on every entity that survives a round-trip; emit a new UUID only for entities that did not exist in input. Reject the import if a UUID format is invalid; never silently overwrite a producer-emitted UUID with a fresh one.
notes: **See also**: Pmi001, Pmi065. Provenance tier: requires-sibling-pair; the defect is the differential between the input UUID and the re-exported UUID; demonstrating it requires both an input fixture and the corrupted output a receiver produces. Synonyms: "persistent UUID lost on round-trip", "PMI association breaks because UUID changed", "UUID regenerated, link broken".
reproducer: an `ADVANCED_FACE` `#35` carries an `APPLIED_IDENTIFICATION_ASSIGNMENT('4ce0acf8-1a2b-4c3d-9e8f-7a6b5c4d3e2f', IDENTIFICATION_ROLE('uuid',''), (#35))`. A receiver-side round-trip that emits a new UUID for the same face is the defect; the input fixture establishes the original UUID. Provenance tier: requires-sibling-pair — bytes alone (the input fixture) cannot demonstrate the round-trip drift; the defect lives in the differential between the input file's UUID assignment and the re-exported file's.
sender: deduced — receivers that regenerate UUIDs on import rather than honouring the producer-emitted `APPLIED_IDENTIFICATION_ASSIGNMENT('uuid',..)`
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP UUID changes on round-trip", "PMI link breaks after re-export"
title: Persistent UUID lost on round-trip (PMI association breaks)

description: AP242 ROUND_HOLE is a feature definition that asserts a circular hole on a host face with a stated diameter and depth. A producer that authors a hole feature with a diameter larger than the host face's local extent (a 50 mm hole on a face whose smallest extent is 30 mm) leaves a feature definition that the host geometry cannot support. Receivers that build downstream representations (PMI dimensioning, manufacturing simulation, hole-pattern detection) either trim the diameter, error, or accept the contradiction silently. Bug-reporter language: "ROUND_HOLE bigger than face", "AP242 hole feature exceeds host", "hole diameter inconsistent with face".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate hole-feature attributes against the host face's measured extent; reject as inconsistent or warn deterministically.
notes: First fully-AP242-feature-definition entry exercising ROUND_HOLE attribute consistency beyond the existing entries Pmi055/Pmi066/Pmi074. **See also**: Pmi055, Pmi074, Pmi092, Pmi093. Synonyms: "ROUND_HOLE internal_diameter exceeds host face extent", "hole bigger than the face it's drilled into", "hole diameter larger than parent face".
reproducer: a 30x30 mm planar `ADVANCED_FACE` host; a `ROUND_HOLE` feature with `internal_diameter` of 50 mm referencing the face.
title: `ROUND_HOLE` feature whose `internal_diameter` exceeds host face's bounded extent

description: AP242 COUNTERBORE_HOLE represents a counterbored hole: a smaller-diameter through-feature plus a larger-diameter shallow recess at one end. The defining geometric invariant: counterbore_diameter must be strictly greater than thru_hole_diameter (otherwise the counterbore is not a counterbore). A producer that emits a counterbore_diameter equal to or smaller than the thru-hole diameter leaves a malformed feature. Receivers diverge: some reject, some swap the two values heuristically, some accept and produce a downstream model that contradicts itself. Bug-reporter language: "counterbore smaller than hole", "AP242 counterbore inverted", "feature attributes contradict each other".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as malformed and name the attribute relationship that is violated; never silently swap values.
notes: Distinct from Pmi055 (missing required attributes); Pmi092 is contradiction within attributes. **See also**: Pmi055, Pmi066, Pmi091, Pmi093. Synonyms: "counterbore diameter smaller than thru-hole diameter", "counterbore smaller than through-hole", "C'BORE diameter less than parent hole".
reproducer: a `COUNTERBORE_HOLE` (or its `SHAPE_ASPECT` equivalent with the dimensional-size pattern) with `internal_diameter` 12 mm (thru-hole) and `counterbore_diameter` 8 mm (smaller — invalid).
title: `COUNTERBORE_HOLE` feature with counterbore diameter smaller than thru-hole diameter

description: AP242 RECTANGULAR_PATTERN replicates a feature on a regular rectangular grid: count along U, count along V, spacing along U, spacing along V. The geometric invariant: spacings must be strictly positive (zero spacing collapses all instances onto each other). A producer that authors a 1-D pattern (a row of holes) and emits it as a 2-D rectangular pattern with `count_v=4, spacing_v=0.0` leaves a contradiction: nominally four rows along V, but every row coincides with row 1. Receivers either collapse to one row (intended), interpret as four phantom-coincident rows (a different defect class), or reject. Bug-reporter language: "AP242 pattern has zero spacing", "pattern count says 4 but spacing 0".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as malformed when a pattern spacing is zero with count > 1; or treat as a 1-D pattern (collapsing V) with a warning that documents the silent re-interpretation.
notes: First entry exercising AP242 pattern feature definitions. **See also**: Pmi091, Pmi092. Synonyms: "rectangular pattern with zero spacing in one direction", "pattern row/column spacing zero", "duplicate pattern members at same location".
reproducer: a `RECTANGULAR_PATTERN` linked feature with `pattern_count_u=3, pattern_count_v=4, pattern_spacing_u=10.0, pattern_spacing_v=0.0` (the V spacing collapses all V copies onto V index 0).
title: `RECTANGULAR_PATTERN` with zero spacing in one direction

category: §12.7 PMI / GD&T (sub-class: GD&T export coverage gap)
description: An XCAF document has a flatness tolerance, a position tolerance, and a datum reference attached to a face. The writer's STEP-AP242 export pass emits the geometry but not the GD&T records; the output file has no `GEOMETRIC_TOLERANCE`, no `DIMENSIONAL_LOCATION`, no `DATUM_REFERENCE`. The producer's intent is lost. Bug class: writer coverage gap on PMI side.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; writer emits every GD&T record present in the XCAF document; missing record types raise `W_GDT_NOT_SUPPORTED` rather than silently dropping. AP242 is the canonical schema for PMI export.
notes: **See also**: Pmi031. Synonyms: "export of GDT from XCAF to STEP", "geometric tolerances not written to STEP AP242", "PMI lost on STEP export", "XCAF GD&T not round-tripping".
reproducer: XCAF document with one face and a flatness tolerance. Run `STEPCAFControl_Writer::Perform`. Output omits GD&T entirely.
sender: OCCT writer when an XCAF document carries `XCAFDoc_GeomToleranceTool` or `XCAFDoc_DimTolTool` records.
sources: bug-reporter language: "export of GDT from XCAF to STEP", "geometric tolerances in XCAF document not written to STEP", "GD&T not preserved on export". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: XCAF GD&T data does not round-trip to STEP AP242 PMI

description: AP242 `slot` is a feature definition for a rectangular linear cut on a host face with `slot_length`, `slot_width`, `slot_depth`, and an end-condition. The defining geometric invariant: `slot_length >= slot_width` (otherwise the feature is a wide rectangular pocket, not a slot, different feature class with different downstream PMI semantics). A producer that emits `slot_length=8 mm` and `slot_width=20 mm` leaves a malformed feature. Receivers diverge: NX-style importers swap the values heuristically, CATIA-style importers reject, Solid Edge accepts and produces a downstream pocket-shaped feature contradicting the SLOT class. Bug-reporter language: "SLOT length less than width", "AP242 slot is degenerate", "slot wider than long".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as malformed and name the attribute relationship that is violated; never silently swap values; alternative: reclassify as a rectangular pocket with a deterministic warning.
notes: First entry exercising AP242 SLOT feature-definition attribute consistency. **See also**: Pmi091, Pmi092, Pmi096, Pmi097. Synonyms: "SLOT length < width", "degenerate slot (length < width)", "slot wider than long", "AP242 slot dimension swap".
reproducer: a 50x50 mm planar `ADVANCED_FACE` host; a `SHAPE_ASPECT('SLOT',..)` linked via `GEOMETRIC_ITEM_SPECIFIC_USAGE` with `DIMENSIONAL_SIZE` of `slot_length=8.0 mm` and `slot_width=20.0 mm` (length < width).
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP242 slot length less than width", "slot is wider than it is long", "SLOT feature attributes contradict slot semantics".
title: `SLOT` feature with length less than width (degenerate slot)

description: AP242 `slot` carries a depth attribute and an end-condition (open/closed/blind/through). The geometric invariant: when `end_condition='blind'`, `slot_depth < host_thickness`; when `slot_depth >= host_thickness`, the feature must declare `end_condition='through'`. A producer that emits `slot_depth=8 mm` on a 5 mm-thick plate while still declaring `end_condition='blind'` leaves a contradiction: the slot would punch through the host but the feature definition denies it. Receivers diverge: some auto-promote to through, some leave the feature misclassified, some reject. Bug-reporter language: "blind slot is deeper than the plate", "slot depth exceeds host thickness", "AP242 slot end condition wrong".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as inconsistent; or auto-promote `end_condition` to `through` and emit a deterministic warning; never accept silently.
notes: **See also**: Pmi091, Pmi095, Pmi097, Pmi100. Synonyms: "SLOT depth >= host thickness", "blind slot deeper than host", "slot end_condition contradicts depth", "through-slot mis-declared as blind".
reproducer: a 60x40 mm planar host face advertised at 5 mm thickness; a `SHAPE_ASPECT('SLOT',..)` with `slot_depth=8.0 mm` and `end_condition='blind'`.
sources: CAx-IF Feature Information Recommended Practice §slot end-condition
bug-reporter language: "AP242 slot deeper than plate", "blind slot goes through", "slot end_condition mismatch with depth".
title: `SLOT` blind depth exceeds host face thickness (through-slot in non-through context)

description: AP242 `slot` carries an end-condition attribute (`open`, `closed`, `round_end`, `flat_end`) that constrains the profile shape. The defining invariant: `end_condition='round_end'` requires the explicit profile (when one is provided) to terminate in semicircular ends. A producer that declares `end_condition='round_end'` while emitting a profile with four sharp corners (rectangular) leaves a contradiction. Receivers diverge: some honour the end-condition string and ignore the profile, some honour the profile and ignore the string, some reject. Bug-reporter language: "round-end slot has rectangular profile", "SLOT end-condition string contradicts profile", "AP242 slot mixed metaphor".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as inconsistent and name the attribute that contradicts the profile; never silently pick one side.
notes: **See also**: Pmi095, Pmi096, Pmi099. Synonyms: "SLOT end_condition mismatch with profile", "round-end declaration but rectangular profile", "SLOT shape contradicts end-condition string".
reproducer: a `SHAPE_ASPECT('SLOT',..)` with `DESCRIPTIVE_REPRESENTATION_ITEM('end_condition','round_end')` and `DESCRIPTIVE_REPRESENTATION_ITEM('profile_shape','rectangular')` on the same feature.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP242 slot end_condition does not match profile", "round-end slot has square corners", "SLOT profile contradicts end-condition".
title: `SLOT` end-condition declared `round_end` but profile is rectangular

description: AP242 `slot` carries an `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` whose Z direction is the slot's cutting axis. For a planar host face, the slot's cutting axis must be parallel to the host face normal (i.e., perpendicular to the face). When the slot's axis is parallel to the host face (Z direction in-plane), the slot would not actually engrave the host. A producer that emits a slot with Z=(1,0,0) on a host face whose normal is (0,0,1) leaves a feature that cannot be physically realised. Receivers diverge: some silently re-orient, some accept and produce a malformed solid, some reject. Bug-reporter language: "SLOT axis parallel to host face", "slot would not cut the part", "AP242 slot orientation defect".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate slot axis vs host face normal; reject as inconsistent or auto-correct with a deterministic warning. Never accept silently.
notes: **See also**: Pmi091, Pmi095, Pmi105. Synonyms: "SLOT axis parallel to host face", "slot placement orientation wrong", "AP242 slot Z direction mis-aligned".
reproducer: a planar host face with normal (0,0,1); a `SHAPE_ASPECT('SLOT',..)` whose linked `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` has Z direction (1,0,0) — parallel to the face.
sources: CAx-IF Feature Information Recommended Practice §slot orientation
bug-reporter language: "SLOT axis parallel to face", "AP242 slot orientation wrong", "slot placement does not engrave host".
title: `SLOT` axis not perpendicular to host face

description: AP242 supports parametric patterns (`rectangular_pattern`, `circular_pattern`) that capture the relationship between a primary feature and its copies. The canonical form for three identical SLOTs sharing a direction with even spacing is one SLOT plus a 3-instance RECTANGULAR_PATTERN. A producer that decomposes the pattern at export and emits three independent SLOT features — same orientation, same dimensions, evenly spaced — loses the parametric relationship. Receivers cannot reconstruct downstream pattern PMI from this form: each SLOT is treated as an independent feature, and modifying the pattern (changing instance count, spacing) becomes impossible. Bug-reporter language: "AP242 pattern lost on export", "three identical slots emitted as instances", "pattern decomposition at export".
expected_kernel_behavior: Warn and accept: writer should detect identical co-axial features and heal by emitting one feature plus a pattern record; reader should emit a warning `W_FEATURE_PATTERN_LOST` when it observes the decomposed form. Accepting the decomposed form without surfacing the lost pattern relationship is a coverage gap.
notes: **See also**: Pmi093, Pmi095. Synonyms: "coaxial SLOTs not patterned", "AP242 pattern decomposed to instances", "three slots no pattern", "feature pattern relationship lost".
reproducer: three `SHAPE_ASPECT('SLOT',..)` records sharing the same dimensions (length=15, width=5, depth=2), evenly spaced 25 mm apart along X, no `RECTANGULAR_PATTERN` linking them.
sources: bug-reporter language: "three identical slots, no pattern emitted", "AP242 lost pattern relationship", "feature pattern decomposed to instances".
title: Three coaxial `SLOT` features instead of a `RECTANGULAR_PATTERN`

description: AP242 `groove` is a recessed feature with `groove_width`, `groove_depth`, and a profile/sweep description. The geometric invariant: `groove_width > 0` (a zero-width groove removes no material, the feature is degenerate). A producer that emits `groove_width=0.0` leaves a feature definition that cannot be physically realised. Receivers diverge: some accept and produce a zero-volume cut, some reject as malformed, some silently substitute a default width. Bug-reporter language: "GROOVE has zero width", "AP242 groove with no opening", "groove width attribute is zero".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as malformed and name `groove_width` as the violated attribute; never substitute a default silently.
notes: First entry exercising AP242 GROOVE feature-definition attribute consistency. **See also**: Pmi101, Pmi102, Pmi104. Synonyms: "GROOVE width <= 0", "zero-width groove", "groove with no opening", "degenerate AP242 groove".
reproducer: a planar host face; a `SHAPE_ASPECT('GROOVE',..)` with `DIMENSIONAL_SIZE` of `groove_width=0.0 mm` and `groove_depth=2.0 mm`.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP242 groove width zero", "groove with no opening", "GROOVE degenerate width".
title: `GROOVE` feature with width = 0 (degenerate)

description: AP242 `groove` carries a sweep description; for a circumferential groove on a cylindrical host, the sweep must close; `sweep_end_angle - sweep_start_angle = 2π`. A producer that emits a circumferential groove with `sweep_start=0` and `sweep_end=4.8869 rad` (≈280°) leaves an open path: the groove cuts roughly three-quarters of the way around the cylinder and stops mid-pass. The feature class is `groove` (closed by definition), but the path is unmistakably open. Receivers diverge: some auto-close the path with a warning, some leave it open and produce a partial cut, some reject. Bug-reporter language: "groove path does not close", "circumferential groove ends mid-pass", "AP242 groove sweep open".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as inconsistent (groove class implies closed sweep); or reclassify the feature as a partial-arc slot with a deterministic warning.
notes: **See also**: Pmi100, Pmi102. Synonyms: "GROOVE profile not closed", "groove sweep stops mid-pass", "AP242 groove open path", "circumferential groove ends short".
reproducer: a `SHAPE_ASPECT('GROOVE',..)` on a planar host with `sweep_start_angle=0.0` and `sweep_end_angle=4.8869` rad (≈280°, not 2π).
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP242 groove sweep does not close", "circumferential groove stops mid-pass", "groove path open".
title: `GROOVE` sweep does not close (open path on cylindrical host)

description: AP242 `groove` on a cylindrical host has a radial depth that must be strictly less than the cylinder radius (otherwise the groove cuts through the cylinder centerline and "wraps" past the axis to reappear on the other side, leaving a self-intersecting feature definition). A producer that emits a groove with `radial_depth=15 mm` on a cylinder of radius 10 mm leaves a feature whose constructive evaluation is non-manifold. Receivers diverge: some clamp the depth to the radius, some accept and produce a self-intersecting solid, some reject. Bug-reporter language: "groove depth exceeds host radius", "GROOVE cuts past cylinder centreline", "AP242 groove wrap-around".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate radial depth < host radius for circumferential grooves; reject as inconsistent or clamp with a deterministic warning. Never accept silently.
notes: **See also**: Pmi091, Pmi100, Pmi101. Synonyms: "GROOVE depth wrap-around", "groove cuts through cylinder centerline", "AP242 circumferential groove too deep", "radial depth exceeds host radius".
reproducer: a cylindrical host face with radius 10; a `SHAPE_ASPECT('GROOVE',..)` with `groove_radial_depth=15.0 mm` and `host_cylinder_radius=10.0 mm`.
sources: CAx-IF Feature Information Recommended Practice §groove on cylindrical host
bug-reporter language: "AP242 groove cuts through cylinder centerline", "groove depth wraps around axis", "circumferential groove depth too deep".
title: `GROOVE` radial depth exceeds cylindrical host radius (depth wraps past axis)

description: AP242 `boss` is a raised cylindrical feature representing a substantial protrusion on a host face. The conventional invariant: `boss_diameter >= host_thickness` (a boss thinner than its substrate is a `stud` or `pin`; a different feature class with different downstream PMI semantics, including thread-bearing assumptions). A producer that emits `boss_diameter=2 mm` on a 10 mm-thick plate leaves the feature mis-classified: downstream tooling that processes BOSSes expects a substantial protrusion and may attempt operations (chamfer-the-base, attach-counterbore) that do not make sense for a thin pin. Bug-reporter language: "BOSS thinner than plate", "AP242 boss is actually a stud", "boss diameter < host thickness".
expected_kernel_behavior: warn `W_BOSS_FEATURE_CLASS_MISMATCH` when boss diameter is below host thickness; suggest reclassification as `stud` or `pin`. Receivers must not silently treat the feature as a heavy boss.
notes: **See also**: Pmi091, Pmi104, Pmi105. Synonyms: "BOSS diameter < host thickness", "boss thinner than plate", "AP242 boss is really a stud", "feature class mis-classified as boss".
reproducer: a 50x50 mm planar host face advertised at 10 mm thickness; a `SHAPE_ASPECT('BOSS',..)` with `boss_diameter=2.0 mm` and `boss_height=4.0 mm`.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP242 boss thinner than plate", "BOSS smaller than host thickness", "boss is really a stud".
title: `BOSS` diameter smaller than host plate thickness (feature-class mismatch)

description: AP242 `boss` height must be strictly positive (the boss is a *raised* feature). A producer that emits `boss_height=0.0` leaves a feature that adds no material; equivalent to drawing a circular outline on the host face with no extrusion. Receivers diverge: some accept and produce a zero-volume feature that confuses downstream BOM and machining tooling, some reject as malformed, some silently substitute a default height. Bug-reporter language: "BOSS has zero height", "AP242 boss with no protrusion", "boss height is zero".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as degenerate and name `boss_height` as the violated attribute; never substitute a default height silently.
notes: **See also**: Pmi100, Pmi103, Pmi105. Synonyms: "BOSS height <= 0", "zero-height boss", "boss with no protrusion", "degenerate AP242 boss".
reproducer: a planar host face; a `SHAPE_ASPECT('BOSS',..)` with `DIMENSIONAL_SIZE` of `boss_diameter=12.0 mm` and `boss_height=0.0 mm`.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP242 boss with no protrusion", "BOSS height zero", "boss is just an outline".
title: `BOSS` height = 0 (zero-protrusion boss)

description: AP242 `boss` carries an `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` for its base; the geometric invariant is that the boss base plane coincides with the host face plane (the boss attaches *to* the substrate). A producer that emits a boss whose base is offset by 5 mm from the host face leaves the feature physically disconnected from the substrate; constructive evaluation produces a floating cylinder. Receivers diverge: some snap the boss to the face, some accept and produce a non-manifold solid, some reject. Bug-reporter language: "BOSS base not coplanar with host", "boss floats above plate", "AP242 boss base offset".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate boss base plane against host face plane; reject as inconsistent or snap-and-warn deterministically. Never accept silently.
notes: **See also**: Pmi098, Pmi103, Pmi104. Synonyms: "BOSS base not coplanar with host face", "boss floating above plate", "AP242 boss base disconnected from host", "boss placement Z offset".
reproducer: a planar host face at z=0; a `SHAPE_ASPECT('BOSS',..)` whose `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` location is `(25.0, 25.0, 5.0)` (5 mm offset above the host face).
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP242 boss base not on face", "boss floating above plate", "BOSS base offset from host".
title: `BOSS` base not coplanar with host face (boss floats above substrate)

description: AP242 feature definitions (SLOT, GROOVE, BOSS, etc.) link to host geometry via `GEOMETRIC_ITEM_SPECIFIC_USAGE` whose `definition` references the host face's `ADVANCED_FACE` entity id. A producer that emits SHAPE_ASPECT/GISU records for SLOT, GROOVE, and BOSS — all pointing at entity id `#9999` which is never declared in the file — leaves three orphaned feature definitions. Strict readers reject the file at the cross-reference pass; lenient readers silently drop the linkage and the features become un-anchored (they appear in the file's PMI section but cannot be tied to any geometry). Bug-reporter language: "AP242 feature references missing entity", "GISU host face does not exist", "SHAPE_ASPECT dangling target".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject the file at the cross-reference pass and name every dangling target; never silently drop feature linkages.
notes: **See also**: Pmi091, M161 (cross-reference validation). Synonyms: "feature definition with dangling host face", "SLOT/GROOVE/BOSS link to nonexistent geometry", "GISU dangling reference", "AP242 feature linkage broken".
reproducer: three `SHAPE_ASPECT` records (SLOT, GROOVE, BOSS) each linked through `GEOMETRIC_ITEM_SPECIFIC_USAGE(..,#9999)` where `#9999` is never declared.
sources: CAx-IF Feature Information Recommended Practice §feature linkage
bug-reporter language: "AP242 feature references missing face", "GISU dangling reference", "SHAPE_ASPECT linked to nonexistent geometry".
title: `SLOT`/`GROOVE`/`BOSS` reference non-existent host face (dangling GISU target)

description: AP242 `composite_feature` aggregates several sub-features (each a `SHAPE_ASPECT`) and presents them to receivers as a single defect-bearing unit (a slot whose floor carries a sub-groove, a counterbore where the recess and through-hole are siblings, etc.). The defining invariant: the wrapped sub-features must share at least one host-shape boundary (a shared edge, vertex, or co-incident face) so that the "composite" label is geometrically meaningful. A producer that emits a composite_feature whose sub-features reference disjoint regions of the host (slot on face A, groove on face B, no shared edge) leaves a feature definition whose grouping is meaningless. Receivers diverge: some treat the composite as two unrelated features (silently dropping the composite grouping), some reject (no shared boundary), some accept the contradictory link. Bug-reporter language: "composite_feature sub-features disjoint", "AP242 composite has no shared boundary", "composite groups unrelated features".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as malformed (composite-feature semantics require shared boundary); or warn and degrade to a flat list of unrelated features with `W_COMPOSITE_BOUNDARY_MISSING`.
